ayat.mukhtasar: Just as We sent down the previous scriptures in the language of their people, We have sent down to you, O Messenger, the Qur’ān as a decisive word indicating the truth in the Arabic language. If you, O Messenger, follow the desires of the People of the Scripture, in their request to you to delete what does not conform to their desires, after you have received the knowledge that Allah has taught you, then you will not have anyone to take charge of your affairs and to assist you against your enemies and you will not have anyone to protect you from Allah’s punishment.

note.title: Arabic, and the warning to the Messenger
note.text: The Qur'ān is given as a decisive Arabic judgement. Then the āyah addresses the Prophet ﷺ himself: do not follow their inclinations after knowledge has come. A warning in the second person to the one carrying the revelation is not a small thing.

ayat.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلٗا مِّن قَبۡلِكَ وَجَعَلۡنَا لَهُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجٗا وَذُرِّيَّةٗ وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأۡتِيَ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ لِكُلِّ أَجَلٖ كِتَابً
ayat.en: And We have already sent messengers before you and assigned to them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a decree
ayat.tr: Walaqad arsalna rusulan min qablika wajaAAalna lahum azwajan wathurriyyatan wama kana lirasoolin an yatiya biayatin illa biithni Allahi likulli ajalin kitabun
ayat.ibnKathir:
And indeed We sent Messengers before you, and made for them wives and offspring. And it was not for a Messenger to bring a sign except by Allah's leave. (For) every matter there is a decree (from Allah)(38)Allah blots out what He wills and confirms (what He wills). And with Him is the Mother of the Book (39)

All Prophets and Messengers were Humans

Allah says, 'Just as We have sent you O Muhammad, a Prophet and a human, We sent the Messengers before you from among mankind, that eat food, walk in the markets, and We gave them wives and offspring.' Allah said to the most honorable and Final Messenger,

قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ

(Say: "I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me.")[18:110] It is recorded in the Two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

أَمَّا أَنَا فَأَصُومُ وَأُفْطِرُ، وَأَقُومُ وَأَنَامُ، وَآكُلُ اللَّحْمَ، وَأَتَزَوَّجُ النِّسَاءَ، فَمَنْ رَغِبَ عَنْ سُنَّتِي فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي

(As for me, I fast and break the fast, stand in prayer at night and sleep, eat meat and marry women; so whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of mine.)

No Prophet can bring a Miracle except by Allah's Leave

Allah said,

وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ

(And it was not for a Messenger to bring a sign except by Allah's leave.) meaning, no Prophet could have brought a miracle to his people except by Allah's permission and will, for this matter is only decided by Allah the Exalted and Most Honored, not the Prophets; surely Allah does what He wills and decides what He wills.

لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتَابٌ

((For) every matter there is a decree (from Allah).) for every term appointed, there is a record (or decree) that keeps it, and everything has a specific due measure with Allah,

أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۗ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ فِي كِتَابٍ ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ

(Know you not that Allah knows all that is in the heaven and on the earth? Verily, it is (all) in the Book. Verily, that is easy for Allah.)[22:70]

Meaning of Allah blotting out what He wills and confirming what He wills of the Book

Allah said,

يَمْحُو اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ

(Allah blots out what He wills) of the divinely revealed Books,

وَيُثْبِتُ

(and confirms), until the Qur'an, revealed from Allah to His Messenger peace be upon him, abrogated them all. Mujahid commented;

يَمْحُو اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ

(Allah blots out what He wills and confirms (what He wills).) "Except life and death, misery and happiness [i.e., faith and disbelief], for they do not change." Mansur said that he asked Mujahid, "Some of us say in their supplication, 'O Allah! If my name is with those who are happy (believers), affirm my name among them, and if my name is among the miserable ones (disbelievers), remove it from among them and place it among the happy ones." Mujahid said. "This supplication is good." I met him a year or more later and repeated the same question to him and he recited these Ayat,

إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ

(We sent it (this Qur'an) down on a blessed night.) Mujahid commented next, "During Laylatul-Qadr (Night of the Decrees), Allah decides what provisions and disasters will occur in the next year of. He then brings forward or back (or blots out) whatever He wills. As for the Book containing the records of the happy (believers) and the miserable (disbelievers), it does not change." Al-A'mash narrated that Abu Wa'il, Shaqiq bin Salamah said that he used to recite this supplication often, "O Allah, if You wrote us among the wretched ones, remove this status from us and write us among the blessed ones. If You wrote us among the blessed ones, please let us stay that way, for surely, You blot out and confirm what You will, and with You is the Mother of the Book." Ibn Jarir At-Tabari collected this. Similar statements were collected from 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, indicating that Allah blots out (or abrogates) and affirms what He wills in the Book of Records. What further supports this meaning is that Imam Ahmad recorded that Thawban said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيُحْرَمُ الرِّزْقَ بِالذَّنْبِ يُصِيبُهُ، وَلَا يَرُدُّ الْقَدَرَ إِلَّا الدُّعَاءُ، وَلَا يَزِيدُ فِي الْعُمْرِ إِلَّا الْبِرُّ

(A man might be deprived of a provision (that was written for him) because of a sin that he commits; only supplication changes Al-Qadar (Predestination); and only Birr (righteousness) can increase the life span.")

An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah collected this Hadith. There is also a Hadith recorded in the Sahih that affirms that maintaining the ties of the womb increases the life span.

Al-'Awfi reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about Allah's statement,

يَمْحُو اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ ۖ وَعِندَهُ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ

(Allah blots out what He wills and confirms (what He wills). And with Him is the Mother of the Book.) "A man might work in Allah's obedience for a while but he reverts to the disobedience of Him and then dies while misguided. This is what Allah blots out, while what He confirms is a man who works in His disobedience, but since goodness was destined for him, he dies after reverting to the obedience of Allah. This is what Allah confirms." It was also reported that Sa'id bin Jubayr said that this Ayah is in the meaning of another Ayah,

فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَاءُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

(Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is able to do all things.)[2:284]
ayat.mukhtasar: We sent messengers before you, O Messenger, who were human - so you are nothing new among the messengers. We gave them wives and children like other human beings. We did not make them angels who do not marry and have children. You are one of these messengers who marry and have children. Why then are these idolaters surprised at this? No messenger can bring a miracle except if Allah gives permission for him to do so. For every matter decreed by Allah there is a Book in which it is mentioned and a time which will neither come too early nor too late.

note.title: He was a man with a family
note.text: Ibn Kathīr cites the report in the two Ṣaḥīḥs about the three men who came to the Prophet's ﷺ households and proposed celibacy, continual fasting and all-night prayer; he answered that he fasted and broke the fast, prayed and slept, and married women. This āyah makes the same point from the other direction: every messenger before him had wives and children. Āyah 38 is often quoted at those who treat the Prophet's ﷺ ordinary human life as a problem rather than the point.

ayat.ar: يَمۡحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثۡبِتُ وَعِندَهُُٓ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ
ayat.en: Allah eliminates what He wills or confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book
ayat.tr: Yamhoo Allahu ma yashao wayuthbitu waAAindahu ommu alkitabi
ayat.ibnKathir:
And indeed We sent Messengers before you, and made for them wives and offspring. And it was not for a Messenger to bring a sign except by Allah's leave. (For) every matter there is a decree (from Allah)(38)Allah blots out what He wills and confirms (what He wills). And with Him is the Mother of the Book (39)

All Prophets and Messengers were Humans

Allah says, 'Just as We have sent you O Muhammad, a Prophet and a human, We sent the Messengers before you from among mankind, that eat food, walk in the markets, and We gave them wives and offspring.' Allah said to the most honorable and Final Messenger,

قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ

(Say: "I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me.")[18:110] It is recorded in the Two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

أَمَّا أَنَا فَأَصُومُ وَأُفْطِرُ، وَأَقُومُ وَأَنَامُ، وَآكُلُ اللَّحْمَ، وَأَتَزَوَّجُ النِّسَاءَ، فَمَنْ رَغِبَ عَنْ سُنَّتِي فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي

(As for me, I fast and break the fast, stand in prayer at night and sleep, eat meat and marry women; so whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of mine.)

No Prophet can bring a Miracle except by Allah's Leave

Allah said,

وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ

(And it was not for a Messenger to bring a sign except by Allah's leave.) meaning, no Prophet could have brought a miracle to his people except by Allah's permission and will, for this matter is only decided by Allah the Exalted and Most Honored, not the Prophets; surely Allah does what He wills and decides what He wills.

لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتَابٌ

((For) every matter there is a decree (from Allah).) for every term appointed, there is a record (or decree) that keeps it, and everything has a specific due measure with Allah,

أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۗ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ فِي كِتَابٍ ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ

(Know you not that Allah knows all that is in the heaven and on the earth? Verily, it is (all) in the Book. Verily, that is easy for Allah.)[22:70]

Meaning of Allah blotting out what He wills and confirming what He wills of the Book

Allah said,

يَمْحُو اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ

(Allah blots out what He wills) of the divinely revealed Books,

وَيُثْبِتُ

(and confirms), until the Qur'an, revealed from Allah to His Messenger peace be upon him, abrogated them all. Mujahid commented;

يَمْحُو اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ

(Allah blots out what He wills and confirms (what He wills).) "Except life and death, misery and happiness [i.e., faith and disbelief], for they do not change." Mansur said that he asked Mujahid, "Some of us say in their supplication, 'O Allah! If my name is with those who are happy (believers), affirm my name among them, and if my name is among the miserable ones (disbelievers), remove it from among them and place it among the happy ones." Mujahid said. "This supplication is good." I met him a year or more later and repeated the same question to him and he recited these Ayat,

إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ

(We sent it (this Qur'an) down on a blessed night.) Mujahid commented next, "During Laylatul-Qadr (Night of the Decrees), Allah decides what provisions and disasters will occur in the next year of. He then brings forward or back (or blots out) whatever He wills. As for the Book containing the records of the happy (believers) and the miserable (disbelievers), it does not change." Al-A'mash narrated that Abu Wa'il, Shaqiq bin Salamah said that he used to recite this supplication often, "O Allah, if You wrote us among the wretched ones, remove this status from us and write us among the blessed ones. If You wrote us among the blessed ones, please let us stay that way, for surely, You blot out and confirm what You will, and with You is the Mother of the Book." Ibn Jarir At-Tabari collected this. Similar statements were collected from 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, indicating that Allah blots out (or abrogates) and affirms what He wills in the Book of Records. (A man might be deprived of a provision (that was written for him) because of a sin that he commits; only supplication changes Al-Qadar (Predestination); and only Birr (righteousness) can increase the life span.")

An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah collected this Hadith. There is also a Hadith recorded in the Sahih that affirms that maintaining the ties of the womb increases the life span.

Al-'Awfi reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about Allah's statement,

يَمْحُو اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ ۖ وَعِندَهُ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ

(Allah blots out what He wills and confirms (what He wills). And with Him is the Mother of the Book.) "A man might work in Allah's obedience for a while but he reverts to the disobedience of Him and then dies while misguided. This is what Allah blots out, while what He confirms is a man who works in His disobedience, but since goodness was destined for him, he dies after reverting to the obedience of Allah. This is what Allah confirms." It was also reported that Sa'id bin Jubayr said that this Ayah is in the meaning of another Ayah,

فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَاءُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

(Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is able to do all things.)[2:284]
ayat.mukhtasar: Allah removes whatever good, evil, fortune or misfortune He wills to remove and He confirms whatever He wills. With Him is the Preserved Tablet, which is the source of all of that, and any erasure or confirmation that appears conforms to what is in it.

note.title: Erasing and confirming
note.text: The āyah that steadied ʿUmar at Ḥudaybiyyah: Allah erases what He wills and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Al-Mukhtaṣar identifies the Mother of the Book with the Preserved Tablet, and reads erasure and confirmation as occurring in conformity with it. This is one of the āyāt that later theology argued over for centuries. This app does not adjudicate that argument; it shows what the āyah says and what the commentaries said it says.

ayat.ar: وَإِن مَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمۡ أَوۡ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَلَٰغُ وَعَلَيۡنَا ٱلۡحِسَابُ
ayat.en: And whether We show you part of what We promise them or take you in death, upon you is only the [duty of] notification, and upon Us is the account
ayat.tr: Wain ma nuriyannaka baAAda allathee naAAiduhum aw natawaffayannaka fainnama AAalayka albalaghu waAAalayna alhisabu
ayat.ibnKathir:
Whether We show you part of what We have promised them or cause you to die, your duty is only to convey (the Message) and on Us is the reckoning (40)See they not that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying borders. And Allah judges, there is none to put back His judgement, and He is swift at reckoning (41)

Punishment is by Allah, and the Messenger's Job is only to convey the Message

Allah said to His Messenger ﷺ,

وَإِن مَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ

(Whether We show you) O Muhammad, part of the disgrace and humiliation We have promised your enemies in this life,

أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ

(or cause you to die) before that,

فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ

(your duty is only to convey We have only sent you to convey to them Allah's Message, and by doing so, you will have fulfilled the mission that was ordained on you,

وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسَابُ

(and on Us is the reckoning), their reckoning and recompense is on Us.' Allah said in similar Ayat,

فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٌ - لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ - إِلَّا مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ - فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ - إِنَّ إِلَيْنَا إِيَابَهُمْ - ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا حِسَابَهُم

(So remind them - you are only one who reminds. You are not a dictator over them - Save the one who turns away and disbelieves. Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment. Verily, to Us will be their return, Then verily, for Us will be their reckoning.)[88:21-26] Allah said next,

أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا

(See they not that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying borders.) Ibn 'Abbas commented, "See they not that We are granting land after land to Muhammad ﷺ?" Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak commented that this Ayah refers to Muslims gaining the upper hand over idolators, just as Allah said in another Ayah,

وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا مَا حَوْلَكُم مِّنَ الْقُرَىٰ

(And indeed We have destroyed towns round about you.)[46:27]
ayat.mukhtasar: If I show you, O Prophet, some of the punishment that We promise them before your death, then that is My choice. If I cause you to die before showing you that, then your duty is only to convey what We have instructed you to convey. It is not your duty to recompense them or to take them to account - that is My duty.

note.title: Only the delivering
note.text: The Prophet's ﷺ duty is narrowed to one thing — conveying — and the account is handed back to Allah. Whether the punishment comes in his lifetime or after his death is not his to decide.

ayat.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا نَأۡتِي ٱلۡأَرۡضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنۡ أَطۡرَافِهَا وَٱللَّهُ يَحۡكُمُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكۡمِهِۦ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
ayat.en: Have they not seen that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders? And Allah decides; there is no adjuster of His decision. And He is swift in account
ayat.tr: Awalam yaraw anna natee alarda nanqusuha min atrafiha waAllahu yahkumu la muAAaqqiba lihukmihi wahuwa sareeAAu alhisabi
ayat.ibnKathir:
Whether We show you part of what We have promised them or cause you to die, your duty is only to convey (the Message) and on Us is the reckoning (40)See they not that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying borders. And Allah judges, there is none to put back His judgement, and He is swift at reckoning (41)

Punishment is by Allah, and the Messenger's Job is only to convey the Message

Allah said to His Messenger ﷺ,

وَإِن مَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ

(Whether We show you) O Muhammad, part of the disgrace and humiliation We have promised your enemies in this life,

أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ

(or cause you to die) before that,

فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ

(your duty is only to convey We have only sent you to convey to them Allah's Message, and by doing so, you will have fulfilled the mission that was ordained on you,

وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسَابُ

(and on Us is the reckoning), their reckoning and recompense is on Us.' Allah said in similar Ayat,

فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٌ - لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ - إِلَّا مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ - فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ - إِنَّ إِلَيْنَا إِيَابَهُمْ - ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا حِسَابَهُم

(So remind them - you are only one who reminds. You are not a dictator over them - Save the one who turns away and disbelieves. Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment. Verily, to Us will be their return, Then verily, for Us will be their reckoning.)[88:21-26] Allah said next,

أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا

(See they not that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying borders.) Ibn 'Abbas commented, "See they not that We are granting land after land to Muhammad ﷺ?" Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak commented that this Ayah refers to Muslims gaining the upper hand over idolators, just as Allah said in another Ayah,

وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا مَا حَوْلَكُم مِّنَ الْقُرَىٰ

(And indeed We have destroyed towns round about you.)[46:27]
ayat.mukhtasar: Have these disbelievers not seen that We come to the land of the disbelievers diminishing it from its borders by spreading Islam and by the Muslims conquering it? Allah decides and decrees whatever He wills amongst His servants. No one can reverse, amend or alter His decision. He, may He be glorified, is swift in reckoning and He will take the earlier people and the later ones to account within one day.

note.title: The land diminishing at its edges
note.text: Al-Mukhtaṣar reads the shrinking borders as the spread of Islam and the conquests. The classical readers also took it more generally: territory passing from one people to another, which is what happens to every power that thinks it is permanent.

ayat.ar: وَقَدۡ مَكَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ فَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡمَكۡرُ جَمِيعٗا يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَكۡسِبُ كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ وَسَيَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡكُفَّـٰرُ لِمَنۡ عُقۡبَى ٱلدَّارِ
ayat.en: And those before them had plotted, but to Allah belongs the plan entirely. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know for whom is the final home
ayat.tr: Waqad makara allatheena min qablihim falillahi almakru jameeAAan yaAAlamu ma taksibu kullu nafsin wasayaAAlamu alkuffaru liman AAuqba alddari
ayat.ibnKathir:
And verily, those before them did devise plots, but all planning is Allah's. He knows what every person earns, and the disbelievers will know who gets the good end (final destination)(42)

The Disbelievers plot, but the Believers gain the Good End

Allah says,

وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ

(And verily, those before them did devise plots,) against their Messengers, they wanted to expel them from their land, but Allah devised plots against the disbelievers and gave the good end to those who fear Him. Allah said in other Ayat,

وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ ۚ وَيَمْكُرُونَ وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ ۖ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ

(And (remember) when the disbelievers plotted against you to imprison you, or to kill you, or to get you out; they were plotting and Allah too was plotting; and Allah is the Best of those who plot.)[8:30], and,

وَمَكَرُوا مَكْرًا وَمَكَرْنَا مَكْرًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ - فَانظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ وَقَوْمَهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

(So they plotted a plot, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not. Then see how was the end of their plot! Verily, We destroyed them and their nation, all together.)[27:50-51] Allah said next,

يَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ

(He knows what every person earns,) meaning, He alone knows all secrets and concealed thoughts and will reckon each person according to his work,

(وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكَافِرُ)

and the Kafir (disbeliever) will know

الْكُفَّارُ

or the Kuffar (disbelievers) according to another way of reciting,

لِمَنْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ

(who gets the good end.) who will earn the ultimate and final victory, they or the followers of the Messengers. Indeed, the followers of the Messengers will earn the good end in this life and the Hereafter, all thanks and praise is due to Allah.
ayat.mukhtasar: The previous communities had plotted and devised schemes against their prophets and they rejected what they brought to them. What did they manage to do by such schemes? Nothing! This is because the effective plan is only that of Allah and no other. He, may He be glorified, is the One Who knows what their souls earn and He will recompense them for it. Then they will know how wrong they were in not having faith in Allah, and how right the believers were as they would have acquired Paradise and the best outcome.

note.title: The plan that wins
note.text: They plotted; the plan belongs entirely to Allah. The āyah is a summary of the whole sūrah's argument about which of the two efforts is going to remain.

ayat.ar: وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَسۡتَ مُرۡسَلٗا قُلۡ كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدَۢا بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكُمۡ وَمَنۡ عِندَهُُ عِلۡمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ
ayat.en: And those who have disbelieved say, "You are not a messenger." Say, [O Muhammad], "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and [the witness of] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture
ayat.tr: Wayaqoolu allatheena kafaroo lasta mursalan qul kafa biAllahi shaheedan baynee wabaynakum waman AAindahu AAilmu alkitabi
ayat.ibnKathir:
And those who disbelieved, say: "You are not a Messenger." Say: "Sufficient as a witness between me and you is Allah and those too who have knowledge of the Scripture. (43)

Allah and those who have Knowledge of the Scripture are Sufficient as Witness to the Message of the Prophet (ﷺ)

Allah says, the disbelievers reject you and say,

لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا

(You are not a Messenger.) from Allah,

قُلْ كَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ

(Say: "Sufficient as a witness between me and you is Allah...") meaning, say, 'Allah is sufficient for me and He is the witness over me and you. He is witness that I (Muhammad) have conveyed the Message from Him and over you, O rejecters, to the falsehood that you invent.' Allah said,

وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ

(and those too who have knowledge of the Scripture.) This refers to 'Abdullah bin Salam, according to Mujahid. However, this opinion is not plausible, since this Ayah was revealed in Makkah and 'Abdullah bin Salam embraced Islam soon after the Prophet ﷺ emigrated to Al-Madinah. A more suitable explanation is that narrated by Al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas that this Ayah refers to Jews and Christians. Qatadah said that among them are, 'Abdullah bin Salam, Salman (Al-Farisi) and Tamim Ad-Dari. The correct view is that this Ayah,

وَمَنْ عِندَهُ

(and those too who have...), refers to the scholars of the People of the Scriptures who find the description of Muhammad ﷺ in their Books and the good news of his advent that were conveyed to them by their Prophets. Allah said in other Ayat,

وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ ۚ فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَالَّذِينَ هُم بِآيَاتِنَا يُؤْمِنُونَ - الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِندَهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنجِيلِ

(And My mercy embraces all things. That (mercy) I shall ordain for those who have Taqwa, and give Zakah; and those who believe in Our Ayat; Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet who can neither read nor write whom they find written with them in the Tawrah and the Injil.)[7:156-157] and,

أَوَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ آيَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُ عُلَمَاءُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ

(It is not a sign to them that the learned scholars of the Children of Israel knew it (as true)?)[26:197]

There are similar Ayat that affirm that the scholars of the Children of Israel know this fact from their divinely revealed Books.

This is the end of Surat Ar-Ra'd, and all praise is due to Allah and all favors are from Him.
ayat.mukhtasar: Those who disbelieved in Allah say: You, O Muhammad, have not been sent by Allah. Tell them, O Messenger, Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you to the fact that I have been sent from my Lord to you, as well as those who have knowledge of the heavenly scriptures that contain my description. The one for whom Allah is a witness to His truthfulness, is not harmed by the rejection of those who deny him.

note.title: The last word is a witness
note.text: The sūrah ends with the accusation and its answer. 'You are not a messenger.' The reply is not a miracle. It is a witness: Allah, and whoever has knowledge of the Book. The magazine you are reading exists because that witness has been copied and carried for fourteen centuries.

أبو.summary: The root centers on fatherhood understood as nurturing, feeding, and raising: the father is one who sustains and brings up.
أبو.development: From this nurture-based orientation develop the noun for father and paternity, extensions to ancestors and broader kinship, verbs of fathering and rearing, and figurative compounds and idioms.

senses.definition: Father; the male parent.
senses.when: Used in ordinary kinship expressions and in the vocative form يا أبتِ, “O my father.”

senses.definition: Ancestor or forefather; a more remote male forebear.
senses.when: The term, especially in the plural آباء, may extend beyond the immediate father to earlier forebears in genealogical or traditional reference.

senses.definition: Paternal uncle, in an extended kinship use of father terminology.
senses.when: This is a broader kinship application distinct from the immediate-father sense; the lexical evidence explicitly attests it in a Quranic expression.

senses.definition: Father and mother together; parents.
senses.when: This collective meaning is expressed by the dual أَبَوَانِ and its inflected forms, which can refer to a person's father and mother as a pair.

cautions: The Quranic dual and plural groups are merged under the singular citation form أَبٌ; their collective and ancestral uses remain explicitly represented.
A historical Quran citation in the lexical material uses Roman-numeral notation and is not converted here into an unsupported modern verse location.

أتي.summary: The root centers on coming or reaching a point, with extensions to bringing something into presence, causing it to arrive, and giving or assigning it to another.
أتي.development: The lexical development runs from coming and arrival to approaching, bringing or producing, acting upon an affair, and Form IV giving or granting. Related derivatives also describe facilitated access, channels, and things or persons that come from elsewhere.

senses.definition: To come, arrive, or reach; of a person, event, thing, or message, to come to a person or place.
senses.when: Used both literally and of events, commands, punishment, and other things that arrive or become present. The imperative may mean “come” or, in a context involving an object, “bring.”

senses.definition: To bring, cause to come, or produce something for someone.
senses.when: Especially occurs with بِ or with a direct object; the construction can mean bringing a person or thing, producing evidence or a requested object, or bringing something back to its destination.

senses.definition: To undertake, engage in, do, perform, or commit an act or affair.
senses.when: Used with prayer, sin, foul conduct, and other actions; the translation may vary between “do,” “perform,” and “commit” according to the object.

senses.definition: To approach sexually or have sexual intercourse.
senses.when: A conventional construction for sexual approach; the lexical evidence supports the construction without restricting it to the gender or social relation of an illustrative object.

senses.definition: To come upon, overtake, and overwhelm; figuratively, to bring destruction or demolish.
senses.when: With عَلَى or comparable constructions, an enemy, time, or divine action may come upon a person or thing, overcome it, destroy it, or bring it to an end.

senses.definition: To bring, convey, present, or cause something to come to someone.
senses.when: The recipient may be expressed with إِلَى; the construction includes bringing or presenting an object and causing it to be present or conveyed.

cautions: Lane’s historical Quran references are not converted into modern verse locations unless independently confirmed by QAC; examples here use supplied QAC locations.
The Form IV requital sense reflects a reported Quran reading discussed under the Form III entry and is not represented by a separate standard QAC example.

The sexual specialization associated with مَأْتِيٌّ is Quran-referenced in the lexical evidence, but the supplied QAC occurrence of that public form is at 19:61 rather than at the cited sexual passage.

أجل.summary: The root presents several distinct lexical branches. Its central temporal branch concerns an appointed limit or endpoint, with related ideas of deferral, futurity, and assigning a term; other branches include affirmation, crime and causation, restraint, a wild-cattle herd, a neck ailment, and a water basin.
أجل.development: The temporal branch extends from a fixed endpoint or term to postponement, futurity, and the appointment of a term. The lexical sources also explicitly treat several other branches as independent rather than deriving every meaning from one root principle.

senses.definition: To assign, appoint, specify, or fix a term or time for something.
senses.when: The Quranic active occurrence concerns a term assigned by God; the assigned term may be understood as a death term or another eschatological endpoint.

senses.definition: To postpone or defer.
senses.when: The active and passive Quranic forms are represented together under the Form II verb: one occurrence presents postponement in the passive, while the lexical relation is that of causing something to be deferred.

senses.definition: An appointed or fixed term, period, endpoint, or due time.
senses.when: The broad temporal noun applies to a period allotted to a person, event, community, or undertaking. Quranic two-term constructions may contrast different appointed durations or endpoints; the contextual object determines whether the term concerns this life, an event, or the hereafter.

senses.definition: An allotted lifespan or appointed time of death.
senses.when: This sense is used of the duration or endpoint of human or communal life. Interpretive discussions of the Quranic term include death, the completion of life, and, in particular constructions, the interval before resurrection or other divinely appointed endpoints.

senses.definition: The prescribed waiting period after divorce.
senses.when: In the Quranic legal construction concerning divorced women, it denotes the interval ending when the waiting period is completed and remarriage becomes permissible.

senses.definition: Destruction or doom.
senses.when: A Quranic interpretation records the noun as meaning approaching destruction rather than merely approaching a chronological deadline. The reported citation is preserved without assigning it a modern verse location not supplied by QAC.

cautions: The temporal noun أَجَل has several Quranic interpretive applications, especially in the discussion of 6:2 and 6:128; these are grouped under the term and lifespan senses rather than treated as wholly separate lexical meanings.

Lane reports a destruction interpretation with a historical citation written as [vii. 184], and reports the passive-participle discussion with a citation to iii. 139. These historical references are not converted into modern verse locations; the QAC occurrence at 3:145 is used for the supplied passive-participle form.

The Maqayis discussion explicitly treats several branches of this root as distinct lexical origins, so the rare herd, neck-ailment, and water-basin meanings are not presented as developments of the temporal sense.

أخذ.summary: The root centers on taking possession of something by gathering, receiving, or grasping it.
أخذ.development: From physical taking and collecting, the lexical branches extend to receiving, retaining, overpowering, seizing, punishing, adopting or appointing, and the nouns denoting what is taken or a place of taking.

senses.definition: To take, receive, obtain, hold, or take away something.
senses.when: Used for ordinary taking or receiving, including taking something by hand, receiving something from someone, and taking or removing an object.

senses.definition: To accept, admit, or willingly receive something.
senses.when: Used for accepting a covenant, obligation, counsel, or something offered for acceptance; the object may be expressed directly or in a related construction.

senses.definition: To retain or detain someone or something.
senses.when: Used when a person or object is kept in place, including retaining someone in another's stead.

senses.definition: To seize, overpower, or affect someone or something.
senses.when: The subject may be a person, an event, a disease, a physical sensation, or another force; the result may be physical seizure, overpowering influence, or being affected by it.

senses.definition: To take someone captive.
senses.when: Used of taking a person as a captive or prisoner.

senses.definition: To gain mastery over and kill or slay someone.
senses.when: A forceful taking may culminate in overcoming and killing the person taken.

cautions: The historical Quran citations embedded in Lane are retained as lexical evidence but are not treated as modern verse locations unless independently confirmed by QAC.
The active participle آخذ is presented under its normalized singular citation form; Quranic contextual renderings vary between taking and grasping.

أخر.summary: The root expresses what is behind, later, or contrary to precedence.
أخر.development: From spatial or positional being behind, the root develops temporal lateness and postponement. آخَر denotes a non-first or additional item, while آخِر denotes what is last or subsequent and, when substantivized, the ultimate world or state of existence.

senses.definition: To put or leave someone or something behind, after, or later; to keep back.
senses.when: A transitive causative use: what is put behind may be spatially posterior or later in an ordered sequence.

senses.definition: To postpone, defer, or grant respite until a later time.
senses.when: A transitive temporal use, including delaying a person, an event, or an appointed term.

senses.definition: To be or become behind or later; to remain behind, lag, or be delayed.
senses.when: An intransitive use describing a person or thing that follows another, remains in the rear, or occurs later.

senses.definition: To seek or be able to remain behind or be delayed; to seek postponement.
senses.when: In the Quranic constructions, the form concerns remaining later or delaying an appointed occurrence, without changing its fixed term.

senses.definition: Another, other, or an additional one; one distinct from the first or from the one already mentioned.
senses.when: Used adjectivally or substantively, with masculine, feminine, singular, dual, and plural forms; it can identify the other member of a pair or an alternative item.

senses.definition: The remaining or last member of a group.
senses.when: A conventional use with a group or sequence, especially in expressions referring to the last of a people.

cautions: The Form X Lane entry is pointer-only; its Quranic sense is assigned through that pointer and the directly described linked Form V lexical branch, together with the supplied QAC morphology.

Lane's citation of the active participle as “Kur xv. 24” is treated as 15:24 only because QAC independently supplies 15:24:7 for this form; the historical citation itself is not independently modernized.

أذن.summary: The root develops from two closely related bases: the ear as the organ of hearing, and knowledge or information received through hearing.
أذن.development: From hearing come listening, heeding, and becoming informed; the same semantic field extends to informing or proclaiming, permission and authorization, and the ear or ear-shaped appendage.

senses.definition: to listen to, heed, and submit to what is heard
senses.when: Used of listening attentively or obediently; in the Quranic image of the earth listening to its Lord, the sense includes compliance and submission.

senses.definition: to know, become informed, or be apprised of something
senses.when: Constructed with بِـ for becoming informed or certain of a matter; the Quranic construction فَأْذَنُوا بِـ means to be informed or assured of the matter announced.

senses.definition: to permit, allow, or give leave
senses.when: Used with لِـ or فِي for granting permission. Passive forms express being granted permission. The related construction أَذِنَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِ can mean obtaining permission for someone from another person.

senses.definition: to announce, proclaim, or call out publicly
senses.when: The Form II causative/intensive usage makes information known publicly; it is used for proclaiming a matter among people, including proclaiming the pilgrimage.

senses.definition: to inform, notify, or announce something to someone
senses.when: A transitive informing construction, commonly with بِـ or a direct object; it makes a matter known to its addressee.

senses.definition: to declare or proclaim decisively
senses.when: Used for a forceful or assured pronouncement, especially a declaration presented as certain to take effect.

cautions: The Form I QAC group contains multiple grammatical voices, aspects, and surface spellings; the senses are distinguished by lexical construction rather than by English gloss alone.
Lane's historical Quran references, including bracketed Roman-numeral citations and alternate readings, are not converted into modern verse locations unless independently secured by QAC.

أرض.summary: The central orientation is the earth or ground: what is below and opposite the sky, including the terrestrial surface and what rests upon it.
أرض.development: From this basic notion, the lexicon develops descriptions of fertile, soft, productive land, lower parts, remaining fixed to the ground, and figurative submissiveness. Rheum and tremor are reported as separate, non-analogical lexical branches.

senses.definition: The earth, ground, or land; the terrestrial expanse or a tract of country.
senses.when: The noun may refer to the earth as opposed to heaven, to its surface or soil, or to an inhabited or cultivated land. In the expression “the earth after its death,” the physical image is extended to renewal after corruption and return after an initial state; it is also interpreted figuratively as the softening of hearts after hardness.

senses.definition: In دَابَّةُ الأَرْضِ, the earth-creature, identified in this Quranic attestation as a wood-eating insect.
senses.when: This is a conventional Quranic expression; the identification of the creature as the insect that consumed Solomon’s staff belongs to the lexical explanation of the expression, not to a general standalone meaning of أرض.

cautions: Lane's historical Quran citation for دَابَّةُ الأَرْضِ is not converted into a modern verse number; the example uses the independently supplied QAC location 34:14:11.
The Quranic form is a single noun group with 461 occurrences; case, definiteness, attached pronouns, and conjunctions are not separate lexical forms.

أصل.summary: The root encompasses distinct lexical branches centered on a foundation or base, a highly dangerous serpent, and the evening period.
أصل.development: The foundation branch extends from a thing's root or lowest support to establishment, permanence, origin, lineage, essential principles, and removal from the root. The time branch designates the period after the afternoon, while the serpent branch remains lexically distinct.

senses.definition: The evening period, from the afternoon prayer or late afternoon until sunset.
senses.when: Used both as a noun, including the plural آصال, and adverbially in expressions meaning “in the evening.”

senses.definition: The root, base, or lowest supporting part of a thing.
senses.when: In the Quran, it refers to the root or foundational lower part of a tree, including the root of the parable's tree, its bottom, and the roots of trees being cut.

cautions: The two QAC groups headed أَصِيل are presented together under the singular citation form أَصِيلٌ: the Quran uses both nominal plural آصال and an adverbial form أَصيلًا for the evening period.
The Classical rooted, established, noble, and serpent-related uses of أَصِيلٌ/أَصَلَةٌ are kept separate from the Quranic evening sense.

أكل.summary: The root centers on taking something in and thereby diminishing or consuming it.
أكل.development: From eating food, the semantic field extends to consuming property, wearing something away, devouring or destroying, and figuratively taking a person's reputation or livelihood.

senses.definition: To eat or consume food and other edible matter.
senses.when: The ordinary physical act of taking food into the body; grammatical tense, mood, person, and number vary across the Quranic occurrences.

senses.definition: To consume, appropriate, or expend wealth or property, especially wrongfully.
senses.when: A figurative extension of physical consumption used with wealth, property, or possessions; the Quran applies it particularly to unlawful appropriation and expenditure.

senses.definition: To defame or backbite someone, figuratively consuming the person's honor or flesh.
senses.when: An idiomatic use, especially for speaking against someone in their absence; the Quran expresses it through the image of eating a dead brother's flesh.

senses.definition: To enjoy abundant means of subsistence or prosperity.
senses.when: In the construction describing people eating from above and beneath them, the verb conveys the availability of plentiful provision and worldly sustenance.

senses.definition: One who eats; an eater or consumer.
senses.when: The Quranic form is plural and refers to those who eat, including those who consume the food described in the surrounding context.

senses.definition: Eating or consuming.
senses.when: The verbal noun denotes the act or process of eating, with context determining whether the object is food or something consumed figuratively.

cautions: Lane's historical Quran citation in the provision sense is not itself used as a modern verse coordinate; the example at 5:66 is included because that word location is independently supplied by QAC.
The active-participle and passive-participle public headwords are normalized singular citation forms, while the supplied Quran occurrences include plural or inflected forms.

أله.summary: The root's central semantic orientation is worship, devotion, and taking a being as an object of worship; إِلٰهٌ is therefore a deity or object of worship, while اللّٰهُ is the proper name of the one true God.
أله.development: The lexical system develops from worship and devotional practice to the deity or divinity associated with worship. Lane also records branches of seeking refuge, protection, and remaining in a place; the confusion and perplexity branch is explicitly related to وَلِهَ and is treated separately by the root evidence.

senses.definition: A deity or object of worship; a god, including a claimed or false god and, in the plural, a group of gods or idols.
senses.when: Used for whatever is treated as an object of worship. The plural آلهة is used for multiple deities and is often applied polemically to idols or other rejected objects of worship.

senses.definition: The God, the one true deity.
senses.when: Used in constructions that identify God as the sole deity, including expressions such as “your God,” “our God,” and “there is no deity but Him.” This sense is a contextual specification of the deity notion rather than a separate inflectional form.

senses.definition: Allah; the proper name of the one true God.
senses.when: The name is used as a proper name and is not restricted by case or by the prepositions and particles that precede it. In the Quranic formula إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ, it expresses belonging to God and eventual return to Him, especially in response to affliction.

senses.definition: O Allah; a fixed vocative form used in addressing God.
senses.when: This form functions as a vocative and is distinct from ordinary case-inflected uses of ٱللَّه.

cautions: The reported reading إِلَاهَتَكَ at 7:127 means “your worship or service”; the canonical QAC occurrence is the common reading آلهتك, “your gods.” The variant is therefore preserved as a distinct lexical item rather than silently assigned to the public headword إِلَٰه.
The derivation and historical analysis of ٱللَّه are disputed in the lexical sources; the Quranic form is presented securely as a proper name regardless of that derivational disagreement.
The confusion and perplexity branch is explicitly associated with وَلِهَ in the supplied evidence and should not be treated as the root's central worship meaning.

أمر.summary: The root centers on directing or determining—an order, command, or matter—while also preserving related branches for growth, markers, and extraordinary or grievous things.
أمر.development: Classical analysis distinguishes several lexical branches: أَمْرٌ as a matter or command, أَمَرَ as directing someone, and related formations for authority, consultation, abundance, signs, and wonder or severity. These branches should not be reduced to one direct meaning of every Quranic form.

senses.definition: To command, order, bid, or enjoin someone to do something.
senses.when: Used with a direct object and with constructions such as أَمَرَهُ بِهِ, أَمَرَهُ إِيَّاهُ, أَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَفْعَلَ, or أَمَرَهُ لِيَفْعَلَ. Voice, tense, and imperative forms do not create separate senses.

senses.definition: In reported variant readings or interpretations of Qur’an 17:16, to cause the inhabitants to multiply or to make them authorities.
senses.when: This is a reading- and interpretation-specific Quranic branch associated with أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا; the ordinary reading and interpretation mean that the inhabitants were commanded, after which they transgressed.

senses.definition: To consult or confer together, mutually direct one another, and settle on a course of action.
senses.when: In Quranic constructions with بِ, the participants may be understood as consulting one another, mutually commanding one another, or agreeing on a purpose; the surrounding matter determines the precise English rendering.

senses.definition: One who commands, orders, or enjoins.
senses.when: The Quranic form is plural in occurrence and is presented here under the singular active-participle citation form.

senses.definition: Grievous, terrible, abominable, or otherwise extraordinary.
senses.when: In the Quranic expression شَيْئًا إِمْرًا, it characterizes an act or event as exceptionally grave or shocking; the lexicons record several closely related renderings.

senses.definition: A matter, affair, case, state, concern, event, action, or thing at issue.
senses.when: This broad nominal sense includes a person’s or community’s affairs and an event or state of affairs; the plural is أُمُورٌ.

cautions: The interpretation of أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا in 17:16 includes reported variant readings or explanations involving multiplication and appointing authorities; the ordinary command interpretation remains separately stated.
Form VIII ائْتَمَرَ ranges between mutual consultation, mutual direction, and settling on a purpose in its two Quranic contexts.
The reported Form VIII sense “to give permission” is explicitly said by the source not to have been heard from an Arab and is therefore left unresolved.

أمم.summary: The root centers on the idea of an origin, reference point, or gathering center, extending to a community, shared way, exemplar, and directed movement toward a goal.
أمم.development: From the notions of source and reference arise the senses of mother, foundation, community or religious way, leader or model, nearness or what lies ahead, and purposeful direction. Classical evidence also preserves independent branches for time, stature, bodily injury, and related compounds.

senses.definition: An exemplar, guide, leader, or other person or authoritative thing followed as a model.
senses.when: Used for persons who lead or are taken as examples, and for an authoritative guide, record, or scripture whose direction or pattern is followed. Quranic contexts include both righteous leaders and leaders who lead toward error.

senses.definition: A book, register, or written record in which things are preserved or recorded.
senses.when: In Quranic constructions, the referent may be a record of deeds, a scripture or law associated with a people, or a comprehensive clear register.

senses.definition: A manifest road or way.
senses.when: Used of a route that is followed and clearly discernible, including a traveled highway.

senses.definition: Mother; a female parent.
senses.when: The Quran uses the word for a human mother and, in the plural, for mothers. It also occurs in relational expressions such as “mothers of the believers.”

senses.definition: The source, origin, foundation, or central basis of something.
senses.when: In Quranic compounds this includes the Mother of the Book, understood as its originating or preserved foundation, and the Mother of the Towns, a central metropolis. The sense may also denote what gathers or supports what is associated with it.

senses.definition: Abode or place of settlement.
senses.when: In the expression فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ, the word is interpreted as the place to which a person belongs or returns, namely the Fire.

cautions: The Lane material uses the contracted root spelling ام and includes several homonymous or derived branches; Classical-only specializations are kept separate from Quranic form senses.
The Quranic form آمّ is presented under its active-participle citation form; its Quranic plural occurrence means those heading toward the Sacred House, not a separate noun meaning.

The interpretations of أُمِّيّ as ‘unlettered’ and as ‘Gentile or belonging to a people without scripture’ overlap in some Quranic contexts and are preserved as distinct explanatory senses because the lexical evidence gives both.

أمن.summary: The root centers on security and freedom from fear, trustworthiness, and believing or affirming something as true.
أمن.development: The two closely related orientations are inward calm and safety on one side, and trust or confirmation on the other. From these develop meanings of being secure, granting or seeking protection, entrusting, faith, trustworthy character, and entrusted property or charge.

senses.definition: To be, become, or feel secure and free from fear.
senses.when: Used of a person or community, and with مِنْ for being secure from or free from fear of something. The Quran also uses it in rhetorical questions about assuming oneself safe from impending harm.

senses.definition: To trust or entrust someone with a person, matter, or charge.
senses.when: A transitive construction meaning to trust someone, give him charge over something, or confide a responsibility to him; it is distinct from the intransitive sense of feeling safe.

senses.definition: To render secure, protect, or grant security and safe-conduct.
senses.when: A causative construction: someone is made safe from a threat or granted protection, security, indemnity, or quarter.

senses.definition: To believe, affirm as true, or have faith in God, revelation, messengers, or a professed truth.
senses.when: The verb may be used transitively, with بِ, or with لِ; believing may involve inward assent and, in some Quranic contexts, is contrasted with merely acknowledging something verbally. The construction can also express giving credit to someone.

senses.definition: To be entrusted with a person, property, or charge; to be trusted with something.
senses.when: The Quran occurrence is passive: the subject is the person to whom a trust or responsibility is entrusted.

senses.definition: Secure, safe, and free from fear.
senses.when: An active participle used adjectivally or substantivally of a person, community, town, or other setting characterized by security.

cautions: آمَنَ as a Form IV verb and آمِن as the Form I active participle are distinct lexical forms despite their similar appearance; the former primarily concerns believing or granting security, while the latter means secure or safe.
The Form VIII Quran occurrence is passive and is therefore displayed under the normalized passive perfect citation form ائْتُمِنَ.
Some classical entries contain rare, contrasting, figurative, or attributed extensions; these are kept separate from the ordinary Quranic senses rather than generalized across all contexts.

أنث.summary: The root centers on the female or feminine as opposed to the male, with associated extensions involving softness, yieldingness, and the receptive or passive side.
أنث.development: The lexical development extends from sex and grammatical gender to soft iron, fertile and even land, and figurative applications to things treated as feminine or passive. Quran-focused interpretation also applies the term polemically to inanimate idols as non-agent beings.

senses.definition: A female; feminine as opposed to male, applied to a female being or to anything classed as feminine.
senses.when: In the Quran this includes human and animal females, the feminine gender, and the dual expression “two females.” The noun may also occur in plural usage as إِنَاثٌ.

senses.definition: A Quranic polemical designation of idols or other inanimate objects as “females.”
senses.when: In the relevant Quranic passages, this is interpreted either from the grammatically feminine names of the deities or from their being inanimate, passive, and incapable of hearing, seeing, or acting; it is not a claim that the objects possess biological sex.

cautions: The Quranic use in 4:117 and the related designation of deities has both a grammatical-feminine interpretation and a semantic interpretation based on inanimacy and lack of agency.

أنس.summary: The root centers on something becoming perceptible and on departure from estrangement or wildness: what appears, is recognized, or is encountered without alienation.
أنس.development: This orientation develops into perception and recognition, human beings as the visible or social counterpart of the jinn, and familiarity, companionship, ease, and sociability. Related derived uses extend to tameness, reassurance, inquiry, and the human-facing or near side of an object.

senses.definition: To perceive, notice, or see something present.
senses.when: In the Qur'an, this is used especially for perceiving a visible sign such as a fire, and may describe becoming aware of something through observation.

senses.definition: To recognize or ascertain a person's condition or quality.
senses.when: In the construction آنَسْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ رُشْدًا, it means recognizing sound judgment, maturity, or capability in them.

senses.definition: To inquire or seek permission before entering, seeking to ascertain whether entry is acceptable.
senses.when: In the Qur'anic construction تَسْتَأْنِسُوا, the verb is explained as asking permission or inquiring about the occupants' willingness before entering a house.

senses.definition: Human beings or humankind, collectively regarded as the counterpart of the jinn.
senses.when: A collective noun used for humanity, including male and female human beings; the Qur'an frequently contrasts it with الجنّ.

senses.definition: A human being; a person; humankind in the collective sense.
senses.when: The noun can refer to an individual or to human beings generally, without restriction to male or female.

senses.definition: A human being; a person of humankind.
senses.when: In the Qur'anic expression إِنْسِيًّا, it denotes a human person, in contrast with a nonhuman or supernatural being.

cautions: إِنْسٌ and إِنْسَانٌ overlap in their reference to human beings, but they remain distinct Quran-attested lexical forms.
The near-side meaning of إِنْسِيٌّ is supported, but Lane records a contrary directional attribution; the usual near/left-side interpretation is retained with that disagreement noted.
Form X usage varies between inquiry, looking to ascertain information, and asking permission; the Qur'anic construction in 24:27 makes the permission-seeking application explicit.

أوب.summary: The root centers on returning or turning back, especially a deliberate return toward a prior place, state, or direction.
أوب.development: From the basic notion of return, the evidence extends to restoring a hand or limb, repeated movement in travel, a destination or abode of return, repentance and repeated turning toward God, and echoing or repeating praise. The Quran-focused discussion distinguishes أَوْبٌ as a voluntary return by an agent with will from the broader notion of return.

senses.definition: To repeat or echo praises of God.
senses.when: Quranic imperative addressed to the mountains in conjunction with David. A transmitted alternative reading understands the construction as returning with him in repeated praise rather than echoing his praise.

senses.definition: Return; coming back.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence, the return of people to God is intended. The form denotes the act of returning rather than a place of return.

senses.definition: One who repeatedly turns back to God through repentance and obedience.
senses.when: The repeated return may involve leaving sin, resuming obedience, seeking forgiveness, and remaining mindful of God's ordinances.

senses.definition: One devoted to praising God.
senses.when: A transmitted religious explanation uses the form for a praiser of God, including in the expression صلاة الأوابين; this is distinct from the more general description of repeated repentance and obedience.

senses.definition: Return, or the place and destination to which one returns; a return-abode.
senses.when: In Quranic contexts it can denote an ultimate destination or final abode, whether favorable or unfavorable, as well as the act or prospect of return.

cautions: The Quranic imperative أَوِّبِ is normalized under the dictionary citation form أَوَّبَ; the supplied Quran surface form remains represented by its QAC location.

A Lane-reported opinion restricts إِيَاب to returning to one's family at night, but the Quran-focused evidence supports the broader meaning of return, so that restriction is not imposed on the Quranic sense.

أَوَّاب is transmitted with both the repentant-returner interpretation and a praiser-of-God interpretation; these are retained as separate Quran-attested senses rather than collapsed into contextual gloss variation.

أوي.summary: The root expresses gathering or movement toward a place of attachment, refuge, or shelter, alongside a distinct branch of compassionate concern.
أوي.development: The gathering-oriented branch yields repairing to a refuge, providing shelter, and the place of resort or abode. Related derived uses describe things gathering together, while the separate compassion branch yields pity and requests for mercy.

senses.definition: To withdraw or repair to a place, or to take refuge there; to betake oneself to shelter, lodging, or protection.
senses.when: Normally construed with إِلَى. In the cave passages, renderings such as “retreat” or “turn away” describe withdrawal toward a place of refuge, not a wholly separate generic sense.

senses.definition: To shelter, harbor, or take someone into one's care or abode; to provide lodging, protection, or refuge.
senses.when: A transitive causative use, including taking someone to oneself or bringing someone into a place of safety or lodging.

senses.definition: A place of resort, lodging, refuge, or abode.
senses.when: May denote an ordinary place of shelter or an ultimate destination and abode in eschatological contexts, including جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى.

cautions: Form I renderings such as “retreat” and “turn away” are treated as contextual realizations of withdrawing or repairing to a refuge; the evidence does not require a separate generic sense of turning away.
The Quranic expression جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى has differing classical interpretations concerning who or what repairs to it, while its lexical core remains a place of resort or abode.
The horse-call entry preserves a reported construction whose exact emphasis is variously described as calling the horses back or drawing them together.

أيي.summary: The root's semantic field centers on attending to or recognizing something, especially through an apparent marker that makes something otherwise hidden knowable.
أيي.development: The evidence also records related developments of pausing or awaiting, acting deliberately, and deliberately directing oneself toward a person or object. These root-level developments do not constitute meanings of every derived form.

senses.definition: An apparent sign, indication, evidence, or proof by which something otherwise not directly perceived is recognized.
senses.when: Applies to sensible or intelligible signs and to a sign regarded as inseparable from what it reveals.

senses.definition: A miraculous or wondrous sign, especially a divinely sent portent.
senses.when: Used of extraordinary signs and wonders, including signs sent to peoples as admonition or warning.

senses.definition: An instructive example or warning that serves as a lesson.
senses.when: May refer to a narrated person, event, or divinely presented case insofar as it functions as an exemplary warning; this is distinct from the bounded verse sense.

senses.definition: A verse or distinct bounded passage of Quranic revelation.
senses.when: Refers to a connected portion of the Quran at which recitation or speech may properly break; the plural commonly denotes the revealed verses collectively.

cautions: Lane matching uses a contracted/geminate root representation and therefore includes several homographic particles, derived verbs, and unrelated headwords; these have been kept separate by headword rather than assigned to آيَة.
Historical Quran citations appearing inside Lane's particle discussions are not converted into modern verse locations; the Quran examples shown here use only independently supplied QAC locations.

بأس.summary: A root of severity, force, and what approaches hardship or affliction; it extends from martial strength to distress, punishment, and severe blame.
بأس.development: The core orientation is intensity or harsh force: بَأْسٌ is strength in war, while related forms describe hardship in living, calamity, inflicted punishment, and inward grief. بِئْسَ develops as the conventional verb of emphatic dispraise.

senses.definition: To be utterly bad or wretched; an emphatic verb of dispraise or blame.
senses.when: A defective, conventionally inflected verb used for emphatic condemnation. With مَا it condemns an action or thing; with a definite noun it takes the praised or blamed subject in the usual بِئْسَ construction, while an indefinite noun may function as a specification.

senses.definition: To be distressed or grieved by something.
senses.when: Used with بِهِ or مِنْهُ for distress at an unwelcome matter. The lexical description includes humbling or abasing oneself in grief; it does not simply mean disliking or hating something.

senses.definition: Might, strength, or force, especially the force exercised in war or fighting.
senses.when: Depending on context, this martial force may be rendered as might, power, violence, battle, or the strength of a fighting group.

senses.definition: Punishment, torment, or severe punitive force inflicted upon someone.
senses.when: In Quranic contexts it can refer to divine punishment, wrath, or torment as an affliction imposed upon a people, rather than to their own military strength.

senses.definition: Adversity, hardship, suffering, or affliction.
senses.when: A state of severe difficulty or suffering; in the Quranic account of the trial of a people, it can include hunger or pressing material adversity, as in 6:42.

senses.definition: A distressed, needy, or miserable person; one suffering hardship.
senses.when: An active participle describing a person marked by distress, want, or suffering.

cautions: بِئْسَ is a defective conventional verb of emphatic dispraise; its Quranic translations such as “wretched” and “evil” do not represent the ordinary distress meaning of related forms.

The Quranic adjective بَئِيسٌ is attested in the construction عَذَابٌ بَئِيسٌ, where the supported sense is severe or vehement punishment; the contextual translation “wretched” should not obscure that construction.

برق.summary: The root centers on shining or flashing, with a second branch describing the combination of black and white or other contrasting colors.
برق.development: From the basic idea of gleaming come lightning, brilliance, shining objects, and related figurative uses. The color branch extends to variegated ropes, animals, eyes, mountains, and terrain; other derivatives develop specialized senses from these two orientations.

senses.definition: To become dazzled or confounded with fright, especially of the eye or sight, which becomes fixed, wide open, or unable to see clearly.
senses.when: Quran 75:7 uses the verb of the eye in a frightening scene. A variant reading of the same verse is explained as the eye shining or gleaming from the intensity of its fixed stare.

senses.definition: Lightning: the flash or luminous gleam associated with clouds.
senses.when: The Quranic noun denotes lightning in descriptions of storm clouds, fear, and divine signs. In the expression برق الخلب, the lightning is specifically without rain.

cautions: The verb in Quran 75:7 has a reported variant reading with a different vocalization and nuance; the displayed Quran form follows the authoritative QAC identification بَرِقَ.

Lane cites Quran passages for some distinct Arabicized or differently headed words, including إِبْرِيقٌ and إِسْتَبْرَقٌ. These are retained as their own Classical Arabic lexical entries because no corresponding QAC form group for those headwords is supplied.

بسط.summary: The root denotes the extension or spreading of something, whether in breadth or in another dimension.
بسط.development: From physical spreading and extension develop meanings of spaciousness, abundance, an outstretched or generous hand, expanded capacity, and things laid out or spread.

senses.definition: To spread, stretch, extend, or expand something.
senses.when: The basic physical meaning applies to objects, limbs, hands, and other things capable of being extended or spread.

senses.definition: To enlarge, increase, or make abundant the means of subsistence or provision.
senses.when: A figurative extension of the basic meaning, especially with رزق or comparable resources.

senses.definition: To stretch out the hand against someone in assault, violence, or hostile action.
senses.when: The hand construction can denote killing, striking, or otherwise directing hostile force toward another person.

senses.definition: To extend the hand in spending; to spend or give liberally.
senses.when: Used figuratively of expenditure or open-handed giving, especially in the construction involving the hand and spending.

senses.definition: Expanded excellence or ample capacity, especially in knowledge and understanding.
senses.when: In the Quranic expression concerning knowledge and body, the noun denotes an increase or superiority in capacity.

senses.definition: Physical largeness, height, or stature.
senses.when: Used of an expanded or outstanding bodily constitution; the Quranic context concerns physical stature.

بصر.summary: The root centers on clarity that enables perception: seeing with the eyes, understanding with the mind, and the evidence or insight that makes a matter clear.
بصر.development: One semantic branch develops from perceptive clarity into sight, knowledge, insight, proof, and manifestness. A second branch concerns thickness or joined edges, yielding terms for sewn hides, cloth seams, stones, and related material forms.

senses.definition: To see or become seeing; to perceive with the eyes.
senses.when: Form I can describe the acquisition or exercise of sight. In Quranic use, the physical act of watching can carry an accompanying sense of awareness.

senses.definition: To perceive mentally; to know or understand.
senses.when: Commonly construed with بِـ; the Quranic expression بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا بِهِ contrasts the speaker’s understanding with what others did not perceive.

senses.definition: To cause someone to perceive or recognize; to make aware.
senses.when: In the Quranic passive construction يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ, persons are made to perceive or recognize one another, including by recognizing their identifying features or consequences.

senses.definition: To see; to look at or behold.
senses.when: The ordinary Form IV verb of visual perception; it may take the person or thing seen as its object, or occur with a directional construction meaning to look toward someone.

senses.definition: To perceive or understand mentally.
senses.when: The form may extend from visual perception to apprehension and understanding, especially when the object is a matter rather than a visible thing.

senses.definition: How clearly one sees; to see clearly, in an emphatic exclamatory construction.
senses.when: The Quranic أَبْصِرْ بِهِ and أَسْمِعْ بِهِ constructions are idiomatic expressions of the clarity or completeness of seeing and hearing, not ordinary imperatives.

cautions: بَصَر and بَصِيرَة can denote either bodily sight or inner perception; the relevant construction and context determine the branch.
The classical epithet بَصِير for a blind person is an ironic or auspicious usage and should not be confused with the ordinary meaning “seeing.”
Lane’s Quran references use historical citation conventions; the modern verse locations in the examples are taken only from the supplied QAC occurrence data.

بطل.summary: The root centers on something passing away, lacking lasting reality, or ceasing to have effect; this yields the senses of nullity, falsehood, invalidation, and futility.
بطل.development: From the basic idea of disappearance or brief continuance, the root develops into describing what is false, void, ineffective, or unprofitable, and into causative uses meaning to annul or render something futile. The related sense of a hero is explained as one who exposes himself to destruction or makes danger and injury of no account.

senses.definition: To become void, futile, or without effect; to go for nothing.
senses.when: Used of an act, deed, assertion, or other thing that loses its efficacy or value and becomes of no account.

senses.definition: To nullify, annul, or render void and ineffectual; to make something go for nothing.
senses.when: A transitive causative use applying whether the object is true or false, valid or invalid. Quranic constructions include rendering deeds vain, proving a claim or practice false, and annulling falsehood.

senses.definition: Falsehood; that which is untrue, unfounded, unreal, invalid, futile, worthless, or without effective purpose.
senses.when: May describe or denote sayings, beliefs, claims, deeds, affairs, or things lacking truth, soundness, efficacy, or lasting value. In constructions with بِ, it can express acting by or with falsehood, wrongfully, or without legitimate basis.

senses.definition: In a reported Quranic interpretation, belief in a plurality of gods or polytheistic belief.
senses.when: This is a specialized interpretive application of الباطل and should not replace its general sense of falsehood or invalidity.

senses.definition: In certain Quranic interpretations, al-bāṭil denotes Iblīs; its plural may denote devils or enchanters.
senses.when: A specialized referential interpretation of الباطل in particular Quranic expressions, distinct from the ordinary abstract sense of falsehood.

senses.definition: One who utters or performs false or vain things; a falsifier.
senses.when: Used of a person whose speech or conduct has no truth or reality, including one who embellishes speech with lies or makes false claims.

cautions: Some specialized Quran interpretations in the lexical evidence are cited in Lane at locations that do not align cleanly with the supplied QAC occurrences, including references to 42:23 and 34:48. Those interpretations are retained as reported, but no unsupported modern location is assigned.

بعد.summary: The root expresses remoteness as the opposite of nearness, and succession as the counterpart of what comes before.
بعد.development: Its meanings extend from physical distance to conceptual remoteness, separation and estrangement, temporal succession, alienation, and—in particular constructions—perishing or imprecation.

senses.definition: to become distant, remote, or far away
senses.when: The Quranic group contains the surface forms بَعُدَتْ and بَعِدَتْ; the sense denotes becoming distant or removed.

senses.definition: to perish or die
senses.when: A distinct Quranic use, especially associated with the بَعِدَ form and the expression concerning Thamud; the lexical sources also report disagreement about using بَعُدَ in this sense.

senses.definition: to make distant, put far apart, or widen the separation between
senses.when: Used transitively for extending the distance or separation between persons, places, or journeys; the Quranic construction is an imperative request to make the spaces between journeys far apart.

senses.definition: far, distant, remote, or extended in spatial or temporal distance
senses.when: Used of physical distance and, by extension, of an extended interval, range, or remoteness from something.

senses.definition: far removed in an abstract or evaluative sense; far astray, remote from truth, or far-fetched
senses.when: May describe conceptual or moral remoteness, including a state from which return to guidance is difficult, or a saying far from what is correct.

senses.definition: after; subsequently; thereafter
senses.when: A temporal noun or adverb, often governing a following genitive complement or occurring with an understood complement, including after a person, event, statement, or action.

cautions: The Form I Quran group contains both بَعُدَتْ and بَعِدَتْ; the perishing sense is especially associated with the latter and is subject to classical disagreement about the two vocalisms.
The interpretation of بَعْدَ as “before” in the cited Quran passages is explicitly disputed and should not be treated as its ordinary meaning.
The public مُبْعَد citation is normalized to the singular passive participle although the supplied Quran occurrence is plural.

بعض.summary: The root centers on dividing a thing into portions: each portion of a whole is a بعض.
بعض.development: The central idea develops into the noun بَعْض for a part or some member of a whole, the causative بَعَّضَ for dividing into portions, and the inchoative تَبَعَّضَ for becoming divided. بَعُوضَة is treated lexically as a secondary formation associated with the small size of the mosquito.

senses.definition: A part or portion of a whole; some member or members of a group, person, or thing.
senses.when: Used in partitive and relational constructions such as “some of them,” “some of you,” and “some to or with another.” The portion may be small or large, even the greater part. In certain Quranic expressions, mentioning a part can pragmatically indicate the consequence or representative scope of a larger matter; this does not make “all” its ordinary lexical meaning.

senses.definition: A mosquito or gnat.
senses.when: The Quranic form is the singular noun; بعوض is used as its plural or collective form in the lexical evidence.

cautions: A reported interpretation of بعض in a Quranic construction as “all” is disputed; the supported ordinary sense is “a part” or “some,” with any wider implication treated as contextual or rhetorical.
A historical lexical citation using Roman-numeral notation is not converted here into an additional modern Quran location.

بغي.summary: The root has two principal semantic orientations: seeking or pursuing something, and a form of corruption expressed as exceeding proper bounds.
بغي.development: The seeking branch extends to purposeful or earnest pursuit and to seeking something on behalf of another. The second branch develops into envy, wrongful excess, oppression, and related specialized uses; the Form VII construction develops the sense of being suitable, possible, or proper.

senses.definition: To seek, pursue, desire, or endeavor to obtain something.
senses.when: The object may be something good or harmful. The verb may also express seeking or desiring a result, way, or object.

senses.definition: To seek something for another person, or to assist another person in seeking it.
