senses.when: The construction may use a benefactive complement, including the sense “seek for someone” or “help someone seek.”

senses.definition: To exceed the proper bounds and thereby act wrongfully, oppressively, or rebelliously toward another.
senses.when: The construction commonly takes عَلَى with the person or group wronged; passive usage expresses being subjected to such wrong.

senses.definition: To speak falsely, in the reported Quranic interpretation “we do not lie.”
senses.when: This interpretation is specifically reported for the expression مَا نَبْغِي in 12:65; the same expression is also understood as “what do we seek?”

senses.definition: To be suitable, fitting, proper, appropriate, allowable, or incumbent.
senses.when: Usually occurs in the impersonal construction يَنْبَغِي لِـ or يَنْبَغِي أَنْ, expressing what is proper or behooving for someone or something.

senses.definition: To be facilitated, possible, practicable, or manageable.
senses.when: This sense emphasizes whether an action can readily occur or be carried out, rather than merely whether it is normatively proper.

cautions: The expression مَا نَبْغِي in 12:65 has competing lexical interpretations in the supplied evidence: “what do we seek?” and “we do not lie”; both are retained under the Form I verb.
One Lane phrase under the Form III entry is retained as ambiguous because the evidence itself assigns it to other possible roots.

بلغ.summary: The root centers on reaching or arriving at something.
بلغ.development: From physical arrival, the usage extends to attaining a limit, stage, age, purpose, or degree; causing something to reach another; conveying something to a recipient; and having sufficient means to attain an end.

senses.definition: To reach, arrive at, or attain a destination, point, term, or intended stage.
senses.when: The construction may describe actual attainment or, with an appointed term, being near the point of completion.

senses.definition: To attain maturity, full growth, puberty, or a specified age or stage.
senses.when: Used of reaching a developed or appointed stage, including maturity, manly vigor, working ability, or a stated age.

senses.definition: To come to or reach someone, especially of old age or another condition coming upon a person.
senses.when: This is a recipient-oriented construction, as in old age reaching someone, rather than saying that the person reaches a place.

senses.definition: To cause to reach; to convey, deliver, or communicate something to a recipient.
senses.when: Used both of bringing a person or thing to a destination and of delivering a message, news, greeting, or divine communication.

senses.definition: To cause a person or thing to reach a destination or an intended outcome.
senses.when: The causative construction can describe bringing someone to a place of safety or bringing someone to a resulting condition.

senses.definition: To convey or communicate a message, statement, or information.
senses.when: Used of completing the delivery of what one has been charged to communicate.

cautions: بَلَغَ may describe completed attainment or, with an appointed term, being on the verge of completion; the construction determines which nuance applies.
The Form II and Form IV verbs overlap in conveying or causing something to reach, but remain separate public forms because QAC identifies distinct derived forms.

بوب.summary: The root centers on the bāb: a door or gate and the guarding or provision of that entrance.
بوب.development: The noun بَاب preserves an original wāw in its etymology. Derived uses extend from taking or serving as a gatekeeper to figurative access, organization under headings, and related lexical formations.

senses.definition: A door or gate; the physical entrance to a place.
senses.when: Used for an entrance or the door or gate that closes it, including entrances to houses, cities, and other places. The Quran uses both the singular بَاب and the broken plural أَبْوَاب.

senses.definition: A means or avenue of access to, or attainment of, something.
senses.when: A Quran-attested figurative or spiritually oriented use in which opening gates signifies access to what is granted, or gates associated with Paradise and Hell are understood as routes by which those realms are reached.

cautions: The QAC group combines the singular بَاب with its broken plural أَبْوَاب; the public headword is normalized to the singular citation form.
The access interpretation is explicitly attested in Quran-focused lexical discussion, but not every Quranic occurrence of أَبْوَاب is thereby figurative.

بين.summary: The root centers on separation or distance, and on the resulting disclosure of what is distinct, evident, or clear.
بين.development: From the notion of something being apart or at a distance developed the senses of becoming distinct, making something clear, expressing it plainly, and identifying the interval or relation between things.

senses.definition: To make distinct or clear; to explain, clarify, establish, or make something known.
senses.when: Transitive Form II usage, commonly taking a matter, ruling, sign, or explanation as its object.

senses.definition: To speak or express oneself clearly and distinctly.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb concerns intelligible speech or expression rather than causing another matter to become clear.

senses.definition: To become clear, evident, or distinct.
senses.when: Intransitive usage describing a matter whose reality or distinction becomes apparent.

senses.definition: To investigate or ascertain carefully until the matter becomes clear.
senses.when: Especially in commands and other contexts requiring deliberate verification rather than haste.

senses.definition: To become manifest or apparent; to become clearly discernible.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb is intransitive and describes something becoming manifest to perception or understanding.

senses.definition: Articulate expression or declaration that makes an intended meaning apparent.
senses.when: Includes speech or other expression by which what is in the mind is disclosed to others.

cautions: The two QAC groups for بَيْن are presented under one public headword because their nominal and locative functions are syntactic variants of the same lexical item.
The feminine and plural Quranic forms of مُبَيِّن are grouped under the normalized active-participle citation form مُبَيِّن.
Lane's historical Quran citation notation is not used as a modern verse location; modern locations in the examples come from QAC.

تبع.summary: The root centers on following, coming after, pursuing, or tracing something or someone.
تبع.development: The basic orientation is physical following or pursuit; related formations distinguish catching up or causing something to follow, adherence to a path or instruction, succession, followers, and claims pursued against another.

senses.definition: To follow, go behind or after, pursue, or overtake someone or something.
senses.when: Used for physical following or pursuit and for coming after another; the precise result may range from trailing behind to catching up.

senses.definition: To follow a person, model, path, teaching, or command in conduct; to imitate or act according to it.
senses.when: A figurative extension of physical following, including adherence to guidance and acting in accordance with what another has done or prescribed.

senses.definition: To follow after, pursue, or catch up with someone or something.
senses.when: Used where the subject comes after or reaches what has gone before; passive forms describe being followed or pursued.

senses.definition: To make someone or something follow, overtake, or come after another; to cause one thing to follow another.
senses.when: A causative construction may take a person or thing as the one made to follow, and may express successive placement or pursuit.

senses.definition: To follow, pursue, or go after a person, thing, course, or report.
senses.when: The following may be physical or figurative; the form is also used for pursuing desires, conjectures, or a chosen course.

senses.definition: To adhere to, obey, or follow a person, guidance, teaching, path, or instruction.
senses.when: A figurative use in which following means adopting a direction, belief, example, or command and acting in accordance with it.

cautions: Lane's Quran references use historical citation conventions and are not independently treated as modern verse locations; Quran examples here use only QAC-supplied locations.
تَبِيعٌ at 17:69 carries overlapping classical interpretations—claimant or avenger, and aider against an enemy—which are retained as separate senses.

تحت.summary: The root centers on the relation of being beneath or below, with extensions to lower rank and inferiority.
تحت.development: Its primary spatial orientation is contrasted with فوق and distinguished from أسفل, which describes the lower part of something united or integral. Classical usage also extends the notion of being beneath to authority, marital relation, and social lowliness.

senses.definition: The location beneath, below, or under another thing.
senses.when: Opposed to فوق. It is used for a relation to something spatially separate, whereas أسفل is used for the lower part of something united with or integral to another thing. It may function adverbially with an expressed complement or as a noun when the complement is suppressed.

cautions: The social-status and buried-treasure interpretations concern the classical form التُّحُوتُ, not the ordinary Quranic spatial use of تَحْت.

ترب.summary: The root has two principal semantic axes: dust or earth, and equality or being of the same age.
ترب.development: The dust axis yields meanings involving becoming dusty, poverty through clinging to the earth, wealth likened to the quantity of dust, and dust-bearing conditions. The equality axis yields peers or coevals and anatomical terms associated with aligned chest bones.

senses.definition: A peer, coeval, or equal in age and standing; a well-matched counterpart.
senses.when: The Quranic form is plural أَتْرَاب. It describes persons matched in age or likeness, including the women described in the Quranic passages, while the lexical term itself can be applied more broadly to male or female peers.

senses.definition: Poverty or need that leaves a person clinging to the dust or earth.
senses.when: A conventional abstract noun for severe poverty, especially in the Quranic expression ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ, one reduced to contact with the earth through want.

senses.definition: Dust or earth, especially the fine particles or material of the ground.
senses.when: The Quran uses the noun for earthly material in creation, human origin, resurrection imagery, and comparisons or parables. It can refer generally to earth as well as to dry dust.

senses.definition: The upper chest or breast area, including its bones or ribs.
senses.when: The Quranic form is the plural تَرَائِب in the expression between the ṣulb and the tarāʾib. Lexical descriptions variously delimit the term as the upper breast, the chest bones, the area near the collarbones, or ribs of the chest; these are related descriptions of the same anatomical region.

cautions: أَتْرَاب and تَرَائِب are Quranic plural forms; the public headwords are normalized to their directly attested singular citation forms تِرْب and تَرِيبَة.
The anatomical scope of تَرَائِب varies in classical descriptions between the upper chest, breast or chest bones, the collarbone region, and ribs.
The derivatives تَرِبَ and مُتْرِب are reported with contrary poverty and wealth senses; the artifact preserves both rather than collapsing them.

تلو.summary: The root centers on following or coming after something, whether physically, sequentially, imitatively, or by adherence.
تلو.development: From following and succession developed the usages for reciting a text in sequence, following revealed guidance in knowledge and action, and referring to what remains after something else.

senses.definition: To follow, come after, or succeed another in sequence, position, or rank.
senses.when: The Quranic usage includes following in a physical or figurative sense, as in the moon following the sun.

senses.definition: To read, recite, rehearse, or present a revealed text, passage, or account.
senses.when: Used especially with revealed scripture and with presenting or recounting a narrative; the form may be active or passive and may take a direct object or occur with عَلَى.

senses.definition: To follow revealed scripture by understanding it and acting according to its commands and guidance.
senses.when: This is the scripture-oriented sense of تلاوة: recitation is accompanied by faithful adherence, knowledge, and practice rather than being mere vocal reading.

senses.definition: Recitation of revealed scripture with attentive following and observance of its guidance.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction حَقَّ تِلَاوَتِهِ, the verbal noun includes following the scripture through knowledge and action, not only reading it aloud.

senses.definition: One who recites or rehearses praise.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence is the feminine plural تَالِيَات, interpreted as those who recite divine praise; the interpretation includes angels or angels and others.

cautions: The root has a documented Classical branch in which تَلَا means to hold back or leave someone; this contrary-looking usage is kept separate from following and recitation.
The animal terms مُتْلٍ and مُتْلِيَةٌ have divergent reported explanations, including late bearing, pregnancy, and being heavy with pregnancy; no narrower interpretation is imposed.
Mufradat records an alternate reading تَبْلُوا at 10:30. That reading is not treated as a تلو occurrence because 10:30 is absent from the supplied QAC locations for this root.

توب.summary: A return: turning back from a prior state, especially returning from sin toward God and obedience.
توب.development: The root develops from physical or general return into the religious sense of abandoning sin, regretting it, resolving not to resume it, and turning toward God; with God as subject, it denotes a merciful return toward the servant and acceptance of repentance.

senses.definition: To turn back from sin or disobedience and return to obedience; to repent.
senses.when: With a human subject, the verb denotes abandoning wrongdoing and turning toward God or obedience. It may be construed with مِنْ or عَنْ for what one turns away from, and with إِلَى for the direction of return.

senses.definition: To turn toward a servant with forgiveness, mercy, favor, or acceptance of repentance.
senses.when: With God as subject and the servant expressed with عَلَى, the verb describes divine restoration of favor and acceptance of the servant's repentance, rather than the servant's own act of repenting.

senses.definition: Repentance: abandoning sin because of its wrongness, regretting it, acknowledging responsibility, resolving not to return to it, and making amends where possible.
senses.when: The Quranic noun covers return from sin toward God. In the related form مَتَاب, it can be expressed as one's return or recourse to God; with righteous action, it may denote complete repentance that combines abandoning wrong with pursuing what is good.

senses.definition: One who repents often or repeatedly, continually returning from disobedience to obedience.
senses.when: Applied to human beings, the intensive form emphasizes repeated or habitual repentance rather than a single act.

senses.definition: One who repeatedly turns toward repentant servants with forgiveness, mercy, and acceptance of their repentance.
senses.when: When applied to God, the form describes the repeated acceptance of servants' repentance and the recurring return of favor toward those who turn to Him.

senses.definition: Repentant; one who turns away from sin and returns to obedience to God.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrences are plural masculine and feminine forms referring to people characterized by repentance; the singular citation form is تَائِب.

cautions: تَوَّاب has distinct Quranic human and divine subject uses: frequent repentance by a servant versus repeated acceptance of repentance by God.

The inclusion of تَابُوت under this root follows the supplied lexical root record, while the same discussion reports alternative etymological analysis and placement; its chest, box, and anatomical meanings are retained as Classical evidence rather than Quranic senses.

ثبت.summary: The root centers on the continuance, persistence, and firmness of something: what remains in place, endures, or becomes established.
ثبت.development: From remaining and being firm, the root develops meanings of steadfastness, making something firm, establishing or confirming it, and—by extension—immobilizing or securing it. Related derived usages include deliberate verification and seeking confirmation.

senses.definition: To be firm or stand fast.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence is an imperative exhortation to remain firm when encountering an opposing force.

senses.definition: To make firm, strengthen, or render steadfast.
senses.when: Used causatively of strengthening people, resolve, conviction, or the effective results of action; the Quranic discussions include strengthening believers and making knowledge or deeds more firmly established.

senses.definition: To immobilize, confine, or hinder someone so that he cannot proceed or move freely.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction concerning the plot against the Prophet, the verb is explained as confining him, rendering him unable to rise, and hindering or perplexing him.

senses.definition: To establish, affirm, or confirm something as valid or existent.
senses.when: This is the establishing or confirming sense, distinct from rendering a person immobile.

senses.definition: Strengthening, making firm, or securing steadfastness.
senses.when: In the Quranic discussions, this includes strengthening conviction by compelling proofs and making knowledge, conduct, or the fruits of action more firmly established.

senses.definition: Firm, established, or enduring.
senses.when: Used of something firmly rooted or established; the Quranic occurrences describe the firmly established word.

cautions: Form I is displayed under the normalized perfect citation form ثَبَتَ even though the supplied Quran occurrence is an imperative form.
The Form IV Quran occurrences exhibit two materially distinct uses—immobilizing or confining and establishing or confirming—and these are kept as separate senses.
The reported Form X meaning 'to make firm of heart' is retained as a qualified classical usage because the supplied evidence records a dispute about its immediate transitivity.

ثقل.summary: The root centers on heaviness as the opposite of lightness, extending to physical weight, burden, preponderance, gravity, and significance.
ثقل.development: Its basic physical sense develops into abstract heaviness and preponderance, burdens carried by people or the earth, moral burdens, and figurative gravity; derived forms express making heavy, being burdened, or hanging back under a weight.

senses.definition: To become heavy or weighty; to be preponderant.
senses.when: In the weighing of deeds, it describes the good deeds becoming preponderant in the scales.

senses.definition: To be momentous, formidable, or difficult to apprehend.
senses.when: Used of the Hour in the expression ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ; the usage conveys its gravity or formidable character, with an associated interpretation of its being difficult to know or apprehend.

senses.definition: To become heavy with pregnancy; to become gravid.
senses.when: Used of a pregnant female when the pregnancy becomes apparent or the burden in the womb becomes heavy.

senses.definition: To hang back heavily, become sluggish, or incline under a weight.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction with إِلَى, it describes holding back from action and inclining toward the earth or the present worldly life.

senses.definition: A weight or a quantity equal in weight; a measure used to express even a very small amount.
senses.when: Used in constructions measuring something by its equivalent weight, including the weight of a tiny particle or mustard seed.

senses.definition: Burdened, heavily laden, or overburdened.
senses.when: Used of one who bears a load or burden; the Quranic forms include a feminine singular and a masculine plural.

cautions: The QAC group v~aqalaAn combines the plural أَثْقَال with the distinct dual expression الثَّقَلَانِ; the public headword and usage conditions make both lexical identities explicit.
The alternatives attached to ثِقَالًا in the light-and-heavy construction are contextual interpretations of one contrast, not separate senses.
Some Lane Quran references use historical citation notation; the modern verse locations used here come only from the supplied QAC occurrence data.

ثمر.summary: Something generated from something else and gathered or formed, especially produce or fruit.
ثمر.development: The concrete sense of fruit extends to fruit-bearing, increase and wealth, benefit or result, and several figurative extensions based on resemblance in form or productive outcome. Some conventional extensions, such as the full-moon expression, are lexically exceptional.

senses.definition: To put forth, bear, or produce fruit.
senses.when: Used of a tree or other fruit-bearing thing; the Quranic occurrences express the general fruit-bearing event without specifying a separate ripeness stage.

senses.definition: Fruit or produce of trees, whether eaten or not.
senses.when: Includes the collective or uncountable noun ثَمَر, its plural ثَمَرَات, and the singulative ثَمَرَة as represented by the merged Quranic form groups.

senses.definition: Accumulated or acquired property and wealth.
senses.when: Reported as an interpretation of ثَمَر in a Quranic passage, alongside the concrete fruit sense; the interpretation is especially associated with the passage at 18:34 in the Quran-focused lexical discussion.

senses.definition: Gold and silver.
senses.when: An attributed Quranic interpretation in the lexical tradition, explicitly noted as not being ordinary usage in the proper language; no modern verse location is assigned to the historical citation.

senses.definition: Children, descendants, or offspring.
senses.when: An attributed interpretation of the plural ثَمَرَات in a Quranic passage, distinct from the ordinary concrete fruit reading; no modern verse location is assigned to the historical citation.

cautions: The wealth, gold-and-silver, and children/descendants senses for ثَمَر or ثَمَرَات are attributed Quranic interpretations alongside the ordinary fruit sense; the historical Lane citations have not been converted into modern verse keys unless independently supplied by QAC.
The phrase in lane-unit:vmr:27525:g1:sub3 has uncertain root and spelling assignment and is preserved as ambiguous rather than treated as a secure ثمر meaning.

ثني.summary: A root centered on repetition or doubling: making something twofold, placing one part upon another, or making two things paired.
ثني.development: From doubling and folding develop the meanings of repetition, pairing, bending or turning aside, ordinal succession, exception by separately repeating an item, and Quranic designation of repeatedly recited passages.

senses.definition: To fold or bend something, turning one part toward another; in the Quranic construction of folding the breast, to conceal what is within and turn oneself away.
senses.when: The Quranic usage is expressed with صُدُورَهُمْ, describing inward concealment, hostility, or turning away from the truth rather than merely a physical bend.

senses.definition: To exclude, except, or set something aside from what is otherwise included.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction, the verb describes making an exception or withholding an item from the general action or provision.

senses.definition: Two by two; in pairs; two at a time.
senses.when: It is an indeclinable numeral expression used for arranging people or things in pairs or successive groups of two.

senses.definition: Recurrently recited or reiterated Quranic passages; a designation for passages, sections, or the Quran whose meanings and recitation recur.
senses.when: The term is explained through repeated recitation, recurring narratives, promises and warnings, or renewed benefits. Classical explanations differ over whether particular occurrences refer to the whole Quran, the Fātiḥah, or a defined group of surahs.

senses.definition: The second; the one that makes another a pair or comes second among two.
senses.when: It may function as an ordinal or as the second member of a pair, as in ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ.

senses.definition: Bending, turning, or twisting aside.
senses.when: In ثَانِيَ عِطْفِهِ, the expression describes one turning or bending his side or neck away in proud rejection or aversion.

cautions: The Quranic designation مَثَانِي has several classical referential explanations, including the Quran as a whole, the Fātiḥah, and particular groups of surahs; the entry states the shared repeated-recitation basis without choosing among those referents.
The Lane citation attached to the exception noun ثُنْيَا uses historical citation notation and is preserved without converting it into a modern surah:ayah claim.
The derivation of ثِنَاءٌ meaning a house forecourt is disputed within the lexical evidence and is marked as such in its definition.

جبل.summary: The root centers on gathering or massing something into elevation: a mountain is an elevated mass, and related words extend this idea to large groups, substantial physical form, innate constitution, and fixedness.
جبل.development: The concrete sense of an elevated mass develops into meanings of magnitude, a great company, natural formation or disposition, bodily coarseness, and figurative immovability. Derived verbal uses also extend the root to creating someone with a disposition, entering or approaching a mountain, and encountering a hard obstruction.

senses.definition: A mountain; a substantial elevated or rocky mass.
senses.when: Used literally for a mountain or rocky elevation, in both singular and plural forms. Contextual renderings such as “hill” reflect the passage context rather than a separate lexical sense.

senses.definition: Innate constitution, natural disposition, or the created nature in which beings are formed.
senses.when: In 26:184, the expression refers to the earlier created beings or to beings constituted according to their innate dispositions.

senses.definition: A great company, multitude, or people.
senses.when: In 36:62, the form is understood through the related classical readings as a large company or multitude.

cautions: The QAC group for جِبِلَّةٌ includes the occurrence at 36:62, while the lexical evidence records several related classical readings there, including جِبِلٌّ; the multitude sense is therefore presented with an explicit reading/form caution rather than treated as identical to the constitution sense.
Lane's Quran citation for the multitude sense uses historical citation notation; the modern location used here is supplied independently by QAC.

جدد.summary: The root develops three principal semantic branches: greatness or exalted status, fortune or prosperity, and cutting or separation.
جدد.development: The cutting sense extends to what is newly cut or newly made, hence “new”; to visible stripes or paths marked off from their surroundings; and to dry or severed things such as a milkless udder. The branches of majesty and worldly fortune remain distinct lexical developments.

senses.definition: New; newly made, brought into existence, or restored.
senses.when: Used in the Quran for things characterized as newly made or newly constituted, including the renewed creation associated with resurrection.

senses.definition: Divine greatness, majesty, or exalted status.
senses.when: Used in the Quranic expression concerning the exalted status of the Lord in 72:3.

senses.definition: The divine effusion or bounty proceeding from God.
senses.when: An interpretive Quranic sense of جَدّ in 72:3, presented as a divine outpouring or beneficence rather than simply majesty.

senses.definition: A visible stripe, band, or tract distinguished from what surrounds it.
senses.when: The Quranic plural جُدَد in 35:27 describes conspicuous differently colored bands or tracts on mountains.

cautions: The noun جَدّ in 72:3 has both a majesty/greatness interpretation and a divine-effusion interpretation; these are retained as separate Quranic senses rather than collapsed into worldly fortune.
The Quranic form جُدَد in 35:27 is displayed under the supported singular citation form جُدَّة; the Classical evidence also records variant readings and related forms.

Several rare Classical entries preserve explicitly reported alternatives, including the contradictory descriptions of جُدّ as a well with abundant or scanty water and the uncertain reading of مُجِدّ in the quick-paced-camel phrase.

جدل.summary: The root centers on firm interweaving, compactness, and the extension of contention through repeated exchange of speech.
جدل.development: The concrete notion of twisting or making something firm develops into strength and compact construction, while the figurative idea of each disputant turning the other from an opinion yields the meanings of argumentation and contention. Related formations also retain notions of firmness, strong construction, and continuous extension.

senses.definition: To engage another in disputation or debate; to argue or contend with someone.
senses.when: An interactive construction used for arguing about a claim, doctrine, or matter with another party. The disputation may be forceful or competitive, or may be conducted in a prescribed good manner.

senses.definition: Contentious argumentation or disputation.
senses.when: A noun for argument carried on through contention or competition; in the Quran it can describe quarrelsome argument or something advanced for the sake of argument.

senses.definition: Disputation or argumentative contention.
senses.when: Used for engaging in dispute with another and for disputation generally, including the Quranic construction referring to disputation during pilgrimage.

cautions: The Quranic verb group is normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form جَادَلَ; its 25 occurrences include imperfect, perfect, and imperative inflections.
جَدَلٌ and جِدَالٌ overlap in the domain of disputation but are retained as distinct public forms because QAC supplies separate nominal form groups.

جري.summary: The root centers on a thing moving onward or flowing along a course.
جري.development: From the movement of water, the root extends to running or proceeding of ships, animals, celestial bodies, and other things; it also develops figurative senses of following a course, acting as another's agent, and adopting a customary way. The bird-crop term جِرِّيَّة is treated separately in the lexical evidence as probably involving substitution from قاف.

senses.definition: To run, flow, or move onward along a course.
senses.when: Used of flowing water and of things that proceed or travel, including ships and moving celestial bodies; the Quranic uses include both literal flowing and directed movement along a course.

senses.definition: Flowing or running.
senses.when: An active participle used adjectivally of something in motion; in the Quran it describes a flowing spring and, in plural forms, things that run or sail.

senses.definition: A ship or sailing vessel.
senses.when: A substantivized active participle, named for its movement upon the sea; the plural جَوَارِ is used for sailing vessels.

senses.definition: A course or route along which something runs.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction مَجْرَاهَا, it denotes the course of the ship; the broader noun can also refer to a physical channel or passage.

cautions: The QAC groups جَارِيَة, جَارِيَات, and جَوَارِ are presented under the singular citation form جَارِيَة; the Quranic contexts distinguish flowing things from sailing vessels and other runners.
The Quranic context for جَوَارِ at 81:16 is rendered as “those that run,” while other occurrences clearly refer to ships; the referent should not be made uniformly nautical.
جِرِّيَّة, the bird-crop term, is lexically distinguished in the supplied evidence from the ordinary running branch and is associated there with a possible قاف-to-جيم substitution.

جعل.summary: A broad root of making, bringing about, or assigning something a form, condition, place, or relation, alongside several unrelated lexical branches.
جعل.development: The lexical evidence presents جعل as broader than فعل and صنع, extending from making or creating to constituting, placing, appointing, judging, and assigning; separate nominal branches concern payment, insects, and related terms.

senses.definition: To make or bring something into existence; to create or bring about.
senses.when: A broad making or creation sense, including bringing a thing or state into being.

senses.definition: To make or provide something from, out of, or for something or someone.
senses.when: Used in constructions expressing the production or provision of one thing from a source, or the making of something available for a recipient.

senses.definition: To prepare, arrange, or bring about something for a particular purpose or result.
senses.when: Especially used of preparing a way, facility, or favorable outcome for someone.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to be or become a specified state, form, role, or status; to appoint or establish.
senses.when: Causative constructions may take a predicative complement, as in making someone a prophet or making something a light, bed, or other specified state. A Quranic expression is also interpreted as making the revelation known or revealing it as an Arabic Quran.

senses.definition: To change or turn something from one state or arrangement into another.
senses.when: Used where the resulting condition reverses or replaces the former condition, rather than merely describing creation or ordinary placement.

senses.definition: To judge, declare, designate, name, or attribute something as being something else.
senses.when: The judgment may be true or false. The construction can express naming, describing, believing, or attributing a quality, status, or share to someone or something.

cautions: The Quranic Form I verb has several constructionally distinct uses; English renderings such as make, place, appoint, assign, and attribute do not by themselves determine the sense.
The active participle جَاعِلٌ is presented as a Quranic form-level item, while its separate Classical specialization meaning a wage-giver is retained under broader Classical meanings.
Lane’s historical Quran citations have not been converted into modern verse locations unless the corresponding QAC location is supplied and secure.

جفأ.summary: The root centers on froth, scum, or refuse being cast off or swept away, with a Quranic figurative extension to what is worthless and discarded.
جفأ.development: The concrete image of torrent or cooking-pot scum develops into the evaluation of something as useless because it is carried away or thrown out. Related derived verbs extend the action to emptying, throwing down, and uprooting.

senses.definition: Froth, foam, or floating refuse cast off by a torrent or a boiling pot.
senses.when: In the Quranic expression فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَاءً, it denotes the scum carried away from the water.

senses.definition: Something worthless, useless, or unprofitable, fit to be cast away.
senses.when: A Quranic figurative interpretation of جُفَاءً in the construction فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَاءً, by analogy with foam and refuse that are discarded and pass away.

cautions: The Mufradat discussion notes that related meanings expressed by جفا and جفو, including lifting a saddle and shunning, properly belong to the wāw-root material rather than serving as direct meanings of the hamzated root جفأ.
The reported meaning “the foremost people” is textually disputed because an alternative reading is reported in its place.

جمع.summary: The root denotes bringing separate parts, persons, or things into mutual proximity or a unified whole.
جمع.development: From the basic idea of joining or drawing together, the root develops meanings of collecting, assembling, accumulation, union, comprehensive inclusion, resolution, and the state or place in which things come together.

senses.definition: To collect, gather, or bring separate persons or things together; to assemble or reunite them.
senses.when: Used transitively for people, objects, wealth, or other things that are brought together from a dispersed state; it can also describe bringing separated parties together.

senses.definition: To determine, resolve, or decide upon an affair; to settle one's plan for it.
senses.when: Especially used with an affair, opinion, stratagem, or undertaking as its object; agreement or unanimity may result from the resolution but is not required in every occurrence.

senses.definition: To combine all one's means, resources, or stratagems for an undertaking.
senses.when: A constructional extension in which the things brought together are the available devices or resources for a planned action; it is explicitly discussed for the Quranic command concerning stratagems.

senses.definition: To come together, gather together, unite, or coalesce.
senses.when: Intransitive or used with a companion or object of association; the subject may be a group, several things, or separate parties that become mutually joined.

senses.definition: All of them; altogether, as an emphatic corroborative of a preceding collective expression.
senses.when: Used with a definite noun or pronoun to reinforce total inclusion and collective unity; the Quranic form أَجْمَعُونَ/أَجْمَعِينَ is inflected according to its syntactic position.

senses.definition: Gathering or assembling; one who brings persons or things together.
senses.when: In the Quran it describes the divine gathering of people and may function as an active participle in a nominal predicate.

cautions: أَجْمَعَ is presented separately as the Form IV verb ‘to resolve or combine one’s means,’ while أَجْمَعُ/أَجْمَعِينَ is presented as an emphatic corroborative.

The Form II discussion of intensive accumulation is retained as a Classical meaning because the packet supplies no separate QAC Form II form group; its Quranic example should not be mistaken for a QAC Form II occurrence.
The Lane Quran citations use historical notation in places; Quran examples here use only independently supplied QAC locations.

جنن.summary: The root centers on veiling, concealment, and being hidden from perception.
جنن.development: From concealment develop the meanings of night-darkness, foliage-covered gardens, graves, embryos, protective coverings, unseen beings, and madness understood as reason being covered. Some figurative extensions describe dense vegetation, vigorous states, or collective bodies that conceal individuals.

senses.definition: To veil, conceal, or cover.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence, the night conceals a person with its darkness.

senses.definition: An embryo or fetus concealed in the womb.
senses.when: The Quranic form is the plural أَجِنَّة, referring to unborn children in their mothers' wombs.

senses.definition: The jinn, especially as a collective or species designation.
senses.when: Used for the unseen beings associated with the jinn; in the Quran it can refer to the jinn collectively.

senses.definition: A serpent, especially a small or white serpent in traditional descriptions.
senses.when: In Quranic descriptions of Moses' staff, the word denotes a serpent; the lexical explanations vary over the serpent's size and appearance.

senses.pos: Noun; proper noun in eschatological use
senses.definition: A garden or orchard, especially one whose trees conceal the ground.
senses.when: Used of earthly gardens, including cultivated or walled gardens and gardens of palms or other trees; the Quranic plural is جَنَّات.

senses.pos: Noun; proper noun in eschatological use
senses.definition: Paradise, the abode of recompense.
senses.when: In eschatological contexts, especially with the definite article, the word denotes the afterlife abode; this usage is associated with the concealing delights of its garden-like setting.

cautions: The homographs جَنَّة, جِنَّة, and جُنَّة have different vowel patterns and distinct meanings.
جَانّ is used in the Quran both for jinn and for a serpent; context determines the sense.
Classical descriptions of the category جِنّ vary concerning its relation to angels and devils.

جهر.summary: The root centers on making something perceptible by exposing, declaring, or raising it, especially through visible manifestation or audible speech.
جهر.development: The semantic range develops from becoming conspicuous or perceptible to public disclosure, loud utterance, direct visibility, prominence, and related notions of bringing something into the open or making it emerge.

senses.definition: To make something public, disclose it, or state it openly.
senses.when: In Quranic usage, the object is speech or an utterance, including what is publicly stated as opposed to what is concealed.

senses.definition: To utter aloud or raise the voice.
senses.when: Used of speech, prayer, recitation, or voice when it is made plainly audible or louder rather than kept quiet.

senses.definition: Public or open disclosure; what is made manifest or openly stated.
senses.when: In Quranic usage, it may denote publicly expressed speech or anything disclosed in contrast with what is hidden.

senses.definition: Loudness or raised audibility of speech.
senses.when: Used especially of speech or voice that is made plainly audible or louder.

senses.definition: Openly, plainly, or visibly, without concealment or an intervening veil.
senses.when: In Quranic usage, especially in the expression of seeing something directly or having it occur openly; the form is adverbial in these contexts.

senses.definition: Publicly or openly.
senses.when: An adverbial noun used with public speech or calling, contrasting with secrecy or concealment.

cautions: The Quranic جَهْرَة usage is associated with direct or unconcealed perception, while the lexical discussion also records alternative grammatical analyses of the form.

The reported Form III usage meaning to vie or strive to overcome is retained as a Classical branch because it is stated lexically, but the source text notes that its wording may reflect transcriptional corruption.
The etymology of جَوْهَر is disputed in the lexical evidence: it is connected by one account with this root and by another with Persian.

جوب.summary: The root has two principal semantic axes: making an opening or cutting through something, and answering or reciprocating in speech or response.
جوب.development: The opening-and-cutting axis extends to hollowing, traversing, gaps, and related implements or objects. A distinct communicative axis develops into replying, responding to a summons, answering a prayer, and reciprocal dialogue.

senses.definition: To cut through, perforate, hollow out, or excavate something.
senses.when: In the Quran, used of Thamūd cutting or hollowing the rocks to make dwellings.

senses.definition: To answer or respond to a question, saying, call, or summons, whether by giving a reply or by heeding it.
senses.when: With a caller or summons, the construction can mean to heed, obey, or comply; with a question or saying, the reply may be affirmative or negative.

senses.definition: To answer a prayer or request by granting what was sought.
senses.when: Used of God answering a supplication through gift, acceptance, or the granting of the requested matter.

senses.definition: To respond to, heed, or comply with a call, summons, or appeal.
senses.when: The form is explained as turning toward and preparing for a response, and is conventionally used for the resulting response or compliance.

senses.definition: To answer a prayer or request by granting it.
senses.when: Used when a supplication receives a favorable response or its requested outcome is granted.

senses.definition: An answer, reply, or response to a question, saying, letter, writing, or demand.
senses.when: The answer may be affirmative or negative; in Quranic usage it denotes the response returned by a people to a prophetic or angelic message.

cautions: The public headwords normalize inflected QAC lemma forms to dictionary citation forms, especially جَابَ, أَجَابَ, and اِسْتَجَابَ.
The derivation of جَيْبٌ, the shirt opening, is disputed in the supplied evidence; it is retained as a qualified Classical possibility rather than an unqualified root assignment.
The dialectal جَابَةُ المِدْرَى is left unresolved because the supplied evidence treats it as a variant of a form associated with another root and gives no secure derivation from جوب.

جور.summary: The root centers on turning aside from a course or right way, with extensions to crookedness, injustice, and related forms of deviation. Its neighboring and protection vocabulary reflects proximity and the security created by close association or covenant.
جور.development: The lexical development moves from physical proximity and neighboring to protective association, and from deviation from a path to moral or legal wrong. Heavy rain and related intensive senses are reported as exceptional or possibly separate developments.

senses.definition: To live near, neighbor, or remain in close proximity to someone.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence describes continued neighboring or proximity; the proximity sense may include a stranger who has become one's neighbor.

senses.definition: To grant protection, refuge, or safe-conduct; to preserve or rescue someone from feared harm or hostile treatment.
senses.when: The Quranic form includes active, imperative, and passive constructions, including protection from or against a threatening power. Voice and aspect do not create separate lexical senses.

senses.definition: To seek protection or refuge; to have recourse to someone for safety or rescue.
senses.when: The subject seeks protection from another, and the transitive construction may specify the person whose protection is sought.

senses.definition: Deviating from the right way; crooked or departing from a straight course.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence, the participle characterizes a route or course that departs from the straight way.

senses.definition: A neighbor: one who lives near another.
senses.when: The Quranic neighbor may be near by residence, kinship, or another recognized connection; the term is relational and carries an associated claim to regard and care.

senses.definition: A protector, guarantor, or one who grants refuge.
senses.when: In the Quranic expression جار لكم, the noun denotes someone who undertakes to protect or give security, rather than merely someone living nearby.

cautions: The proximity, neighbor, and protective-covenant branches are related but are not interchangeable in every construction.
The heavy-rain sense of جِوَرٌّ is treated as a reported lexical branch; its relation to the core root is described as exceptional or possibly separate in the root-level evidence.

جيأ.summary: No single unifying root principle is established in the supplied comparative evidence: the dominant lexical branch concerns coming and arriving, while a separate item denotes a place where water gathers.
جيأ.development: The coming branch extends from physical arrival and presence to the occurrence of events and the bringing or presentation of something. Quran-focused discussion also distinguishes actual arrival or attainment from mere intending.

senses.definition: To come, arrive, or be present; of an event, matter, time, command, or result, to come to pass or occur.
senses.when: Used intransitively for real or figurative arrival. With a goal or recipient, it means to come to or reach; with مِنْ, to come from. The subject may be a person, thing, or abstract matter.

senses.definition: To bring, present, or produce a person, thing, proof, report, or other matter for someone or before an audience.
senses.when: Commonly used with بِـ for the thing or person brought; the construction may describe bringing something along, presenting evidence, or producing a report or other matter.

senses.definition: To do, perform, execute, or effect something; also to utter or produce an act, saying, or novel expression.
senses.when: Used with a direct object or with بِـ. In Quranic usage the construction can describe committing or producing an act rather than physically coming.

senses.definition: In the causative shape أَجَاءَ, to cause someone or something to come, or to compel or drive someone to resort to a place or thing.
senses.when: This causative construction expresses being forced or driven to betake oneself somewhere, as in the Quranic account of the pangs of childbirth driving Mary to the palm-trunk.

cautions: The supplied QAC group reports all 278 tokens under the Form I identity and includes the surface form أَجَاءَ at 19:23, which the Classical lexical evidence identifies as a causative Form IV construction. That Quran-attested causative use is retained as a distinct sense because no separate QAC form group was supplied; this does not assert that أَجَاءَ is itself a Form I paradigm form.

حزب.summary: The root centers on gathering and coming together. Its principal noun denotes a collective body, party, or faction.
حزب.development: The idea of gathering develops into the senses of a party or faction and a portion set aside for a specified purpose. Related Classical branches extend the root to rugged ground, compact or coarse build, and emphatic descriptive formations.

senses.definition: A party, faction, or collective body united by common allegiance, opinion, or action.
senses.when: The group need not be physically assembled. Quranic constructions include parties aligned with a figure or cause, such as حزب الله and حزب الشيطان, as well as divided sects or factions.

senses.definition: A confederated force or coalition formed for warfare.
senses.when: Especially used in the plural, often with the article, for groups that combine against a prophet or an opposing community; this is the usage associated with the Qur'anic al-Ahzab and similar hostile coalitions.

cautions: The Quranic form group contains singular, dual, and broken-plural inflections but is presented under the normalized singular headword حِزْب.
The reported property-share meaning for حِزْبٌ is not treated as established because the lexical passage itself suggests that it may be a mistranscription for another root.
The plant identifications under حِنْزَابٌ and حُنْزُوبٌ are retained as reported Classical usages, while their precise identification or morphological relation is uncertain.

حسب.summary: The root centers on counting, reckoning, and assessing; related developments include supposing or deeming, determining what is sufficient, and reckoning something as belonging to one's account.
حسب.development: From counting and assessment arise the senses of calculation, accountability, expectation, and reckoning a matter as included or stored. A separate lexical branch concerns sufficiency, while other Classical branches concern support, honor, and distinctive color or disease terms.

senses.definition: To think, suppose, or deem something to be so.
senses.when: Often takes an object together with a predicate or complement, or introduces a proposition; the judgment may be mistaken or uncertain.

senses.definition: To reckon with someone; to call someone to account.
senses.when: Used for holding a person or community accountable for deeds, conduct, or an account.

senses.definition: To reckon upon, expect, or anticipate something.
senses.when: Used for an outcome or circumstance that one expects or takes as part of one's calculation.

senses.definition: To count something among one's reckonings; to take it into account or regard it as significant.
senses.when: A construction of inclusion in a calculation or assessment, rather than merely expecting an event.

senses.definition: One who reckons or takes accounts; a reckoner or accountant.
senses.when: The Quranic plural refers to those who reckon or account.

senses.definition: A reckoner, accountant, or one who takes account.
senses.when: In Quranic usage, the term can describe one who observes, assesses, and accounts for deeds or obligations.

cautions: Some Lane Quran citations use historical citation conventions and are not reproduced here as modern verse locations; modern examples follow independently supplied QAC locations.

حُسْبَانٌ in the Quranic sky-visitation expression has several reported interpretations, which are grouped under the broader destructive-visitation sense rather than treated as unrelated ordinary meanings.

حسن.summary: The root centers on goodness, beauty, and the pleasing quality that contrasts with ugliness or defect.
حسن.development: Its semantic range develops from perceptible beauty and comeliness to goodness recognized by judgment, beneficial conduct, excellence in action, favorable outcomes, and the best or most excellent state.

senses.definition: To be or become good, beautiful, comely, or pleasing.
senses.when: An intransitive description of a person, thing, or state possessing or acquiring the quality of ḥusn.

senses.definition: To do good, act well, or deal graciously and beneficially with someone.
senses.when: May be construed with إِلَى or بِ for good treatment toward another; the construction may also describe excellent conduct generally.

senses.definition: To make, render, or complete something well; to perfect it.
senses.when: A causative use in which an object is brought into a good, fitting, or complete condition.

senses.definition: Good treatment, beneficence, or kindness toward another.
senses.when: The outward exercise of goodness in which more is given than is strictly owed and less is taken than is due; it is broader than mere benefaction and exceeds strict justice.

senses.definition: Excellence in one's own action, conduct, or performance.
senses.when: Includes doing an act well, maintaining good obedience, and acting with moral or practical excellence; it may apply to one's own action as well as to treatment of others.

senses.definition: Sincerity, watchful obedience, and steadfast adherence to the righteous way.
senses.when: A Quran-attested theological and devotional use in which ihsān denotes inward sincerity together with vigilant, sound obedience and following the established path of the righteous.

cautions: The Quranic nominal group أَحْسَن is kept distinct from the Form IV verb أَحْسَنَ even though the uninflected spellings can coincide.

The Lane citation for the Form II make-good usage is retained as a Classical meaning because no Form II QAC group is supplied; its historical Quran notation is not converted into a modern verse location.

The interpretations of حُسْنَى in eschatological and theological contexts, and of مُحْسِنِينَ in 12:36, include explicitly reported interpretive alternatives rather than uniformly separate everyday senses.

حفظ.summary: The root centers on attentive care: holding something under regard so that it is not lost, damaged, neglected, or forgotten.
حفظ.development: From active watching and maintenance, the root develops meanings of protection, faithful observance, retention in memory, safekeeping and entrustment, and honor-based defensive anger. These related developments are not automatically meanings of every derived form.

senses.definition: To preserve, protect, guard, or take careful charge of something.
senses.when: The Quranic uses include guarding people or things against harm or loss and protecting something entrusted to one's care.

senses.definition: To keep or observe an oath, including refraining from using it for trivial or improper purposes.
senses.when: Quranic usage in the command concerning oaths supports both faithful observance and restraint in the use of an oath.

senses.definition: To maintain, observe, or attend to something persistently and carefully.
senses.when: In the Quran this construction is used especially of maintaining the prayers by observing their times, requirements, and performance with sustained care.

senses.definition: To charge or require someone to preserve, guard, or attend to something.
senses.when: The Quranic passive construction presents people as charged with preserving or maintaining what they received of the Book of God.

senses.definition: To entrust or place something with someone for safekeeping.
senses.when: The Quranic passive may also be understood as being entrusted with the thing placed under one's care.

senses.definition: A keeper, guardian, or protector; one who watches over a person, thing, or charge.
senses.when: The Quran also uses the plural for guardians assigned to record human deeds and for people mindful of divinely prescribed duties.

cautions: The Quranic use of حَفِيظٌ in 50:4 is explicitly open to both an active interpretation, “preserving or retaining,” and a passive interpretation, “preserved”; both are represented separately.
The Form X public headword is normalized to the active perfect اِسْتَحْفَظَ, while the supplied Quran occurrence is passive and is interpreted through its passive construction.

حقق.summary: The root centers on making something firm, sound, fitting, and established as true or right, in contrast to falsehood.
حقق.development: From the idea of sound correspondence and secure establishment develop the meanings of truth and reality, what is due or obligatory, verification and validation, entitlement, and disputing a claim. Other branches extend to fittingness, central joining or sockets, and things that have reached a settled condition.

senses.definition: To become established as true, certain, or a realized fact; to prove true or come to pass.
senses.when: Intransitive Form I usage, including expressions in which a saying, promise, judgment, or consequence becomes established or takes effect.

senses.definition: To become due, obligatory, incumbent, or justly deserved.
senses.when: Often construed with عَلَى; may describe an obligation, a deserved consequence, or a judgment that becomes binding and takes effect. The passive حُقَّتْ is included under this sense.

senses.definition: To establish, validate, or make the truth prevail.
senses.when: The Quranic construction إِحْقَاقُ الْحَقِّ includes establishing truth by manifesting its proofs and by completing and disseminating the revealed way.

senses.definition: To have, claim, or become entitled to a right or due; to deserve it.
senses.when: Used of a lawful claim or title, including a right established against another person.

senses.definition: To incur or deserve a blameworthy consequence, especially sin or punishment.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction concerning wrongdoing, the subject has done what makes the consequence deserved.

senses.definition: More entitled, deserving, worthy, or strongly possessed of a right or claim.
senses.when: A comparative expression: it may denote an exclusive right or a right shared with another but stronger in degree.

cautions: حَقِيقٌ عَلَى in 7:105 has reported readings and interpretations of obligation versus disposition or fitness; the form is therefore defined broadly enough to preserve both.
The interpretation of بِالْحَقِّ in 15:8 as a decreed or destined event is explicitly reported but is not the only interpretation.
The historical Lane notation for one reported death interpretation is not converted into a modern verse location.

حكم.summary: The root centers on restraint that prevents wrongdoing or disorder, extending to judgment, authoritative decision, wisdom, and sound or perfected ordering.
حكم.development: The semantic development runs from curbing an animal or restraining a person, to judging between parties or imposing a ruling, and to wisdom as knowledge that restrains ignorance and guides right action. The same orientation also yields the sense of making something firm, sound, and free from defect.

senses.definition: To judge, arbitrate, or decide between parties or concerning a matter.
senses.when: Used for judicial or arbitrating decisions, including deciding for or against someone and judging between people. Voice, tense, and subject vary across the Quranic occurrences.

senses.definition: To decree, ordain, or establish a binding ruling.
senses.when: Used when a decision is presented as an authoritative determination or ordinance, including divine decreeing.

senses.definition: To appoint, authorize, or make someone the judge or arbiter in a matter.
senses.when: The construction takes the person whose judgment is accepted or assigned, especially in a dispute or contested affair.

senses.definition: To make firm, sound, perfected, and secure from defect or corruption.
senses.when: In Quranic usage this includes making revealed verses firm or established; the passive form describes what has been made firm or perfected.

senses.definition: To seek judgment from a judge or authority and litigate with one another.
senses.when: The reciprocal construction describes disputing parties taking their case to an adjudicator or authority in order to obtain a judgment.

senses.definition: Most judicious, most just, or most qualified to judge.
senses.when: A superlative used of the one who possesses the attributes of sound judgment, wisdom, and justice to the highest degree, especially among judges.

cautions: حُكْم is lexically broader than حِكْمَة; the Quranic judgment, command, and wisdom-related uses are therefore kept as distinct senses rather than treated as interchangeable.
حَكِيم and مُحْكَم overlap in descriptions of revelation, but the former foregrounds wisdom or wise ordering while the latter foregrounds firmness, precision, and freedom from ambiguity.

The plural active participle حُكَّام and the feminine and plural passive-participle forms مُحْكَمَة and مُحْكَمَات are normalized under singular dictionary citation forms; QAC occurrence counts are preserved.

حلل.summary: The root centers on opening or releasing what is closed, bound, or restricted.
حلل.development: From untying a knot, the root develops meanings of release and permissibility, alighting or settling after being bound for travel, reaching an appointed place, and becoming free of a sacred or legal restriction.

senses.definition: To untie, loosen, or release what is bound.
senses.when: The Quranic imperative in the expression concerning the knot of the tongue preserves the concrete image of releasing a bond or impediment.

senses.definition: To alight, descend, settle, or come to rest in a place.
senses.when: Used of a person, group, or thing arriving and settling; the form may be translated simply as descend or settle according to context.

senses.definition: Of anger, punishment, or a threatened consequence: to descend upon, befall, or become due.
senses.when: This construction describes a consequence taking effect upon its object; it is distinct from merely settling in a place.

senses.definition: To become lawful, allowable, or free from a prohibition.
senses.when: Used of something becoming permissible, including marital and other legal permissions.

senses.definition: To leave the state of ihram or another consecrated restriction.
senses.when: In the pilgrimage context, the subject becomes free of the restrictions of ihram; this is a conventional extension of release from a bond.

senses.definition: To make lawful, permit, or declare free for use.
senses.when: With protected or prohibited things, making lawful can imply treating what is sacred or restricted as permissible; passive forms mean that something has been made lawful.

cautions: The Quranic Form I verb has distinct vocalized and constructional uses: untying, settling or descending, becoming due, becoming lawful, and leaving ihram should not be collapsed into one gloss.
The public headword حَلِيلَة is normalized from the Quranic plural حَلَائِل; the supplied occurrence itself is plural.
The public headword مُحِلّ is normalized from the Quranic active-participial form مُحِلِّى.

حلي.summary: The root centers on ornament and adornment, together with the visible qualities or appearance associated with ornament.
حلي.development: The lexical evidence extends from acquiring, applying, and wearing physical ornaments to describing a person’s qualities or appearance, with derived forms also expressing self-adornment and affectation.

senses.definition: To adorn or deck someone with ornaments.
senses.when: All supplied Quran occurrences are passive Form II forms, describing people as being adorned; the cited construction is transitive in the ornaments applied.

senses.definition: An ornament or adornment.
senses.when: In the supplied Quran occurrences, the term denotes physical ornaments or adornment; the related Quranic plural form حُلِيّ is included under this citation form.

cautions: The Quranic Form II verb occurrences are passive, while the public headword is normalized to the active perfect citation form حَلَّى.
The packet contains no Maqayis entry; the root-level orientation therefore reflects the supplied Lane and Mufradat evidence rather than an independent Maqayis formulation.
Rare botanical, agricultural, animal-related, and technical uses are kept as Classical Arabic meanings and are not folded into the Quranic ornament senses.

حمد.summary: The root denotes the opposite of blame: praise directed toward a praiseworthy quality, action, or object.
حمد.development: Its lexical range develops from praising or recognizing praiseworthiness to expressions for being praised, praising repeatedly, praiseworthy qualities, and the state or result of being commendable. Some fire-related terms in the transmitted lexicon are treated as transposed forms rather than part of this root principle.

senses.definition: To be praised, eulogized, or commended.
senses.when: The supplied Quran occurrence is the passive imperfect يُحْمَدُ, ‘they be praised’; the active lexical counterpart is to praise or commend.

senses.definition: One who praises.
senses.when: The Quranic form is plural, حَامِدُونَ; in the cited construction the praise is directed to God.

senses.definition: Praised or praiseworthy; possessing qualities for which praise is due.
senses.when: It is frequently an epithet of God, including the sense of one who is praiseworthy in every case.

senses.definition: Praising; one who praises.
senses.when: In the Quranic expression إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ, the lexical explanation allows حَمِيدٌ to be understood in the active sense الحامد, as well as in the passive or evaluative sense ‘praised, praiseworthy’.

senses.definition: Praise, eulogy, or commendation.
senses.when: In Quranic formulas it is especially praise directed to God. The lexical distinction supplied for this noun makes it narrower than generic مدح and broader than شكر: it is not restricted to gratitude for a received benefit. With بِحَمْدِكَ and related constructions, it can mean praising You or ‘praise be to You’.

senses.definition: Praised or praiseworthy.
senses.when: This is the passive-participial form of the root and may describe one who is praised or an object deserving praise.

cautions: حَمِيدٌ in 11:73 is explicitly open to both the passive/evaluative sense ‘praised, praiseworthy’ and the active sense ‘praising’.
The Form X evidence is textually uncertain: the transmitted imperative and the proposed reading اِسْتَحْمَدَ اللَّهُ yield different grammatical interpretations.
Fire-related entries such as حَمَدَةٌ and اِحْتَمَدَ are lexically reported as transpositions and should not be used to define the core praise meaning of the root.

حمل.summary: The root centers on bearing or lifting something, whether externally on a back or head, internally in a womb or tree, or figuratively as a burden, duty, or responsibility.
حمل.development: The lexical branches develop from physical carrying into pregnancy and fruit-bearing, transport, imposed obligations, endurance, surety, and things or persons carried from one place to another. The contrast between حَمْلٌ for an internal burden and حِمْلٌ for an external load is especially prominent.

senses.definition: To carry, bear, take up, convey, or transport something or someone.
senses.when: Includes active and passive Quranic constructions involving people, objects, animals, ships, the earth, mountains, and the divine throne.

senses.definition: To bear or assume a burden, wrongdoing, duty, trust, or responsibility.
senses.when: Used for bearing sins and obligations, and for accepting or taking upon oneself a trust; in some contexts the burden is figurative rather than physical.

senses.definition: To become pregnant, conceive, or carry a fetus.
senses.when: Said of a female; the Quran also uses the verb for the state or process of carrying a pregnancy.

senses.definition: To provide transport or a riding mount for someone.
senses.when: In the relevant construction, carrying a person means giving that person an animal or other means on which to ride.

senses.definition: To charge or attack in battle.
senses.when: This is the military construction حَمَلَ عَلَيْهِ; the Quranic contextual rendering identifies an attack, while the lexical construction is independently attested.

senses.definition: To provide or procure sustenance for oneself or another.
senses.when: In the Quranic statement that a beast does not carry its sustenance, the verb is explained as meaning that it does not provide or arrange its provision.

cautions: The vowel distinction between حَمْلٌ and حِمْلٌ is lexically significant: the former primarily concerns an internal burden or pregnancy, while the latter concerns an external load.
The Quranic interpretation of فَالْحَامِلَاتِ وِقْرًا is conventionally understood as clouds bearing water, while the active participle itself retains the broader meaning of bearer or carrier.
حَمُولَةٌ has a reported classical variant meaning 'loads themselves'; the Quranic occurrence is presented as transport animals.

حيي.summary: The root has two principal orientations: life and vitality, opposed to death; and shame or modest restraint, opposed to shamelessness.
حيي.development: The life branch extends to growth, sensation, intellect, enduring life, revival, and greetings originally phrased as prayers for life. The other branch concerns shrinking from what is improper, shame, and refraining.

senses.definition: To live; be alive.
senses.when: Used of continuing or coming to be in life, in contrast with dying.

senses.definition: To greet or salute; to offer a greeting.
senses.when: The greeting is historically a prayer for the recipient's life, preservation, or well-being.

senses.definition: To give life, bring to life, or revive.
senses.when: Includes restoring life to the dead and reviving lifeless land through growth.

senses.definition: To endow with intellectual or spiritual life.
senses.when: Used figuratively of one formerly described as dead being given understanding and guidance.

senses.definition: To preserve or save from destruction.
senses.when: Used where keeping a person alive is expressed as giving life.

senses.definition: To spare, leave alive, or refrain from killing.
senses.when: Used of allowing someone to live or leaving them unharmed.

cautions: The Form-X verb has two Quranic branches: sparing someone and feeling shame or refraining; the immediate construction determines the sense.
حَيَوَان in 29:64 is an intensive expression for abiding life, not merely the ordinary collective noun 'animals'.

خشي.summary: The root centers on fear and dread, with extensions into reverential awe and figurative apprehension or knowing.
خشي.development: The core meaning of fear may be intensified by awareness of what is feared and by reverence; the lexicon also records a figurative knowing use and separate branches concerning dryness or decay.

senses.definition: To fear or dread; to feel fear marked by reverence, awe, or veneration.
senses.when: Used with a direct object, مِنْ, عَلَى, or an أن-clause. The reverential nuance is especially prominent where the feared object is regarded with awe, while the Quran also uses the verb for apprehension of people or events.

senses.definition: To apprehend or anticipate that a consequence will occur; in a projected-outcome construction, to recognize or judge what may result.
senses.when: In فَخَشِينَا أَنْ يُرْهِقَهُمَا ... (18:80), the verb expresses apprehension of a harmful consequence. The same Quranic expression is also explained as “we disapproved” or “we knew” that it would happen.

senses.definition: Fear imbued with reverence, awe, or veneration.
senses.when: Often associated with knowledge or awareness of what is feared. It may occur in constructions expressing fear of a person, consequence, or divine judgment.

cautions: The Quranic construction in 18:80 has competing lexical renderings: fearing or apprehending a consequence, disapproving it, or knowing that it would occur; these readings should not be treated as unrelated ordinary meanings of every occurrence.

خَشْيَة may carry a pronounced nuance of reverence and knowledge, but the Quranic verb also occurs with ordinary feared persons or events, so that nuance should not be imposed uniformly on every context.

خفي.summary: The root has two opposed semantic orientations: concealment or imperceptibility, and manifestation or emergence from concealment.
خفي.development: The concealment branch develops into hiddenness, secrecy, self-concealment, covered things, and things imperceptible to the senses or mind. A contrasting branch denotes appearing, making apparent, bringing forth, or the faint flashing of lightning; the Quranic vocabulary chiefly represents the concealment branch.

senses.definition: To be hidden, imperceptible, or unapparent.
senses.when: Used of something that does not become apparent to perception or understanding; Quranic occurrences express hiddenness rather than an act of concealment by an agent.

senses.definition: To hide, conceal, or keep something secret.
senses.when: A transitive causative use, including concealing information, actions, objects, or inward matters; passive forms mean that something is hidden.

senses.definition: To make something apparent or bring it out from concealment.
senses.when: A divergent lexical reading or interpretation attested for the Quranic expression in 20:15; it should not be confused with the ordinary Quranic Form IV sense of concealing.

senses.definition: To seek to hide oneself or remain concealed.
senses.when: A reflexive or intransitive construction, commonly with مِنْ, expressing an attempt to conceal oneself from someone or something.

senses.definition: More hidden, more concealed, or less perceptible.
senses.when: A comparative adjective in the Quranic expression contrasting degrees of concealment or hiddenness.

senses.definition: Hiding himself; concealed from view.
senses.when: The active participle of اِسْتَخْفَى. In the Quranic passage, an alternative interpretation takes it in the opposite sense, “appearing,” as noted below.

cautions: The expression in 20:15 has divergent lexical readings and interpretations: making the Hour apparent, removing its covering, or concealing it. The Form IV senses distinguish the ordinary concealment use from this reported alternative.
For مُسْتَخْفٍ in 13:11, the direct sense is hiding by night, but a reported interpretation takes the form as appearing; this opposite sense is retained as a qualified Quran-attested alternative.
The report that اِخْتَفَى can mean being slain secretly is explicitly qualified in the lexical evidence as possibly reflecting a transcription of a passive form.

خلد.summary: The root centers on remaining firmly in a state or place and maintaining a condition without interruption.
خلد.development: From staying and continued adherence, the root develops meanings of prolonged or perpetual existence, attachment or reliance, unchanged youth, and things that remain fixed or attached.

senses.definition: To remain or abide indefinitely; to live forever.
senses.when: In the Quranic Form I occurrences, the imperfect denotes continued existence without an indicated end.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to remain or abide permanently; to make immortal.
senses.when: In 104:3, the verb describes wealth being imagined to make its possessor immortal.

senses.definition: To incline or attach oneself to, and rely upon, something.
senses.when: The Quranic construction أَخْلَدَ إِلَى describes turning toward and relying upon the earth or worldly life, rather than literal residence.

senses.definition: Perpetually youthful or unchanged in age; not subject to decrepitude.
senses.when: This is an interpretation of مُخَلَّدُونَ in the Quranic description of those whose age and condition do not deteriorate.

senses.definition: Adorned with earrings or other ear ornaments.
senses.when: This is the alternative Quranic interpretation of مُخَلَّدُونَ reported for the same passages.

senses.definition: One who abides or remains forever; everlasting or immortal.
senses.when: The Quranic active participle is used of beings or groups destined to remain perpetually in a stated condition or abode.

cautions: مُخَلَّدُونَ in 56:17 and 76:19 has two explicitly reported interpretations in the supplied lexical evidence: perpetually youthful or unchanged, and adorned with earrings or other ornaments; both are retained rather than collapsed.
أَخْلَدَ إِلَى is a conventional attachment-and-reliance construction and should not be read as merely the causative of physical residence.

خلف.summary: The root centers on what comes after or takes the place of something, on being behind or contrary, and on alteration or change.
خلف.development: The lexical branches develop from succession and replacement, spatial or temporal opposition to what is ahead, and change from an earlier state. These principles yield meanings such as succession, representation, remaining behind, disagreement, alternation, and deterioration.

senses.definition: To come after, follow, or succeed another.
senses.when: Used of a person or generation coming after another, whether the predecessor remains or has gone.

senses.definition: To take another’s place or act as his substitute.
senses.when: The construction may describe assuming someone’s position, duties, or place, either during his absence or after his departure.

senses.definition: To leave someone behind.
senses.when: The passive Quranic form describes people who were left behind rather than accompanying others.

senses.definition: To disagree with, oppose, or act contrary to someone or something.
senses.when: May be construed with a person, command, matter, or course of action; the opposition may be expressed in conduct or opinion.

senses.definition: To fail to fulfill or break a promise, undertaking, or appointed time.
senses.when: The promise-breaking sense concerns a future commitment or expected fulfillment; in the passive, the person or thing may be described as not being given what was promised.

senses.definition: To replace, restore, or provide a substitute for something that has gone.
