senses.when: Used with God or another agent as subject when something lost, spent, or absent is supplied by a replacement.

cautions: The Quranic form خَلْفٌ combines nominal and locative/adverbial QAC groups; the latter is merged under the normalized dictionary headword خَلْفٌ.
خَالِفٌ and خَالِفَةٌ are normalized from Quranic plural forms; the feminine form preserves the explicitly reported Quranic interpretation of people, especially women, remaining behind.
The Form IV branch includes both failure to fulfill a promise and provision of a replacement; these are distinct constructions rather than merely stylistic translations.

خلق.summary: The root centers on determining a thing's measure and proportion, and on smoothness or evenness.
خلق.development: From measuring and proportioning, the lexicon develops into forming or bringing something into existence, whether by originating it or producing it from an existing substance. It also extends to outward constitution, inner disposition, allotted share, fabrication, smoothness, and wearing out.

senses.definition: To measure, proportion, design, and form something according to a determined measure or pattern.
senses.when: This includes making a form from a material according to its proper proportions, as in the forming of a thing like a bird from clay. It can describe either the determining of the design or its execution.

senses.definition: To bring into existence, create, or produce a thing.
senses.when: The Quran uses this for originating beings and worlds, and for producing one thing from another. With God as subject it denotes creative origination and bringing into being according to wise determination; it is not restricted to creation from no preexisting material in every passage.

senses.definition: To fabricate or forge speech, a claim, falsehood, or other fiction.
senses.when: This is a figurative use for devising a false saying or falsehood, including the construction of creating falsehood.

senses.definition: In a Quranic euphemistic construction, to refer to the sexual organs or sexual relations made available for intercourse.
senses.when: This specialized construction occurs in the expression concerning what the Lord has created for them; the lexical explanation identifies it as a reference to women's sexual organs and the sexual practice being condemned in the verse.

senses.definition: Formed, fully formed, or having its bodily features become apparent.
senses.when: In the Quranic embryological construction it contrasts with an unformed lump and indicates a stage whose form is established or discernible.

senses.definition: One who creates, originates, or brings things into existence; the Creator.
senses.when: With the definite article as a divine epithet, it denotes the Creator. As an indefinite active participle it can describe an agent who is about to create or who creates in a particular act.

cautions: The root's two major orientations—proportioning and smoothness—should not be treated as one direct meaning in every derived form.
خَلْق and خُلُق are distinct Quranic headwords: the former concerns creation, created beings, and outward form, while the latter concerns custom and inner moral character.

خَالِق may be a general active participle in an indefinite construction, whereas the definite divine epithet الخَالِق denotes the Creator; comparative and plural contexts can emphasize proportioning or forming.

خلو.summary: The root denotes the removal or absence of one thing from another, leaving it bare, vacant, free, or unoccupied.
خلو.development: From physical emptiness and freedom from occupation, the meanings extend to passing away, being alone or privately separated, leaving something free, and related states of release or detachment.

senses.definition: To pass away, go by, or be gone.
senses.when: Used of earlier people, generations, events, or periods; the Quran also uses the form for what has gone before or passed out of the present situation.

senses.definition: To be alone with someone; to meet or converse in private.
senses.when: Occurs with a person or group as the companion, including the Quranic construction خَلَوْا إِلَىٰ شَيَاطِينِهِمْ, “they were alone with their devils.”

senses.definition: To become available exclusively to someone; to be free for that person.
senses.when: With لِـ, as in يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ, the construction expresses that a person or thing becomes exclusively available, bringing the relevant attention or favor to the beneficiary.

senses.definition: To release, let go, or leave free.
senses.when: A transitive causative use; in فَخَلُّوا سَبِيلَهُمْ it means to leave their way free, hence to release them.

senses.definition: To become vacant or empty; to be left free of what occupied it.
senses.when: An intransitive/reflexive use describing the subject as becoming cleared or emptied; the Quranic occurrence describes becoming empty.

senses.definition: Past; gone by.
senses.when: Used adjectivally of times or generations that have already passed, as in الْأَيَّامِ الْخَالِيَةِ, “past days.”

cautions: The phrase حُلْوُ الخَلَاءِ is retained as a tentative Classical item because the source reports uncertainty about its reading and whether it belongs to this root.

خوف.summary: The root centers on dread, fright, and apprehension in response to a feared possibility or danger.
خوف.development: From this core, the lexicon develops uses for apprehending a harmful possibility, reverent fear expressed through obedient restraint, causing fear, and warning. The Form V branch also has a distinct sense of diminishing or taking away little by little; this is treated as a consonantal development related to تنقّص.

senses.definition: To fear, be afraid of, or be concerned about; to fear for someone or something.
senses.when: May take a direct object for what is feared, مِنْ for the source or circumstance feared, and عَلَى for concern on behalf of someone or something. In reference to God, the fear is presented as reverent apprehension expressed through avoiding disobedience and choosing obedience rather than mere panic.

senses.definition: To know, recognize, or judge from indications that a harmful or improper condition exists.
senses.when: Especially attested in conditional constructions such as “if you fear,” where the verb can mean recognizing or becoming aware of a likely problem rather than experiencing fright.

senses.definition: To put fear into someone, frighten or threaten them, or make someone or something a source of fear to others.
senses.when: The causative relation may be understood as directly frightening someone or as causing people to fear through another person or thing. In divine discourse, the action may function as a warning intended to urge precaution.

senses.definition: Gradual diminution, wasting, or taking away little by little.
senses.when: Describes loss occurring progressively, including the reduction of bodies, possessions, livestock, or produce by stages.

senses.definition: The emergence or outward manifestation of fear in a person.
senses.when: A Quran-attested interpretation of the verbal noun distinct from the sense of gradual diminution.

senses.definition: The putting of someone into fear: frightening, threatening, or warning.
senses.when: In divine usage, the warning is intended to prompt people to guard themselves against danger or wrongdoing.

cautions: تَخَوُّفٌ in 16:47 has two explicitly attested interpretations in the supplied evidence: gradual diminution and the appearance of fear; these are retained as separate senses.
The interpretations of خَوْفٌ as slaughter and fighting are specialized Quran-attested uses of the noun rather than replacements for its ordinary meaning of fear.

دبر.summary: The root centers on what is behind, at the back, or at the end, in contrast with what is before or in front.
دبر.development: From spatial backness and following come meanings of retreating, coming after, reaching an outcome, considering an affair's consequences, managing it with forethought, and referring to its latter part or surviving remnant. Several specialized usages preserve the same back/end orientation.

senses.definition: To manage, arrange, regulate, or dispose of an affair with forethought.
senses.when: The construction concerns considering an affair's issues, consequences, or orderly execution; it may be used of divine governance and of deliberate human management.

senses.definition: To turn back, go away, retreat, or turn one's back.
senses.when: Used of a person or group moving away or backward, in contrast with advancing or approaching.

senses.definition: To depart or pass into its latter stage; to decline or recede.
senses.when: Used especially of night, day, a season, or another period or condition. Interpretations of the Quranic expression concerning night include its following the day and its retreating to depart.

senses.definition: To reflect on, examine, and seek to understand the meaning and consequences of something.
senses.when: In the Quran it is used of considering the Quran or revealed speech deeply and repeatedly in order to attain understanding.

senses.definition: The latter part, aftermath, or time after something; departure into what follows.
senses.when: Used as a temporal adverbial expression. In Quranic usage it can refer to what follows or to the latter parts of an act or period; it is related to the back or end of the thing.

senses.definition: The last remaining part, remnant, or root of a people or group.
senses.when: In the Quran it denotes the surviving end or stock of a people, especially in expressions about cutting them off or extirpating them.

cautions: The Lane discussion of the Quranic night expression includes alternate readings and interpretations; its bracketed historical citation notation has not been converted into an independently asserted modern location beyond the secure QAC occurrence for أَدْبَرَ at 74:33.

Some rare Classical branches are explicitly disputed or attributed to limited authorities, especially the Form I writing sense, the mountain sense of دَبْرٌ, the reported night reading, and certain specialized Form IV usages.
The Quranic participial group مُدَبِّرَات has been normalized to the singular citation form مُدَبِّرَةٌ; its Quranic occurrence remains the supplied feminine plural.

دخل.summary: The root centers on entering, penetrating, or passing within.
دخل.development: From physical entry, the lexicon develops senses of insertion, intermixture, inwardness, intrusion, and a hidden defect or foreign element.

senses.definition: To enter, go into, or come within a place or space.
senses.when: The ordinary intransitive sense; the destination may be expressed directly or through a preposition, and the verb may describe entering a physical place or realm.

senses.definition: To enter into, join, or become included in a community, religion, affair, or state.
senses.when: Used of coming within a social, religious, practical, or otherwise defined domain, including becoming part of a group or undertaking.

senses.definition: To go in to a woman sexually; to have sexual intercourse.
senses.when: A conventional euphemistic construction, especially دَخَلَ بِـ or دَخَلَ عَلَى, whose meaning is determined by the marital or sexual context.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to enter; to bring, put, introduce, or admit within.
senses.when: The causative counterpart of Form I, used transitively for bringing a person or thing into a place, state, or domain; passive occurrences mean “be admitted” or “be made to enter.”

senses.definition: Entering; one who enters.
senses.when: An active participle used substantivally for entrants or those who enter a place or domain.

senses.definition: Deceit, guile, or circumvention used covertly between people.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction concerning oaths, it denotes using them as a concealed means of deception or bad faith between parties.

cautions: The Quranic noun دَخَلٌ is restricted here to its explicitly attested sense of covert deceit; other defect, corruption, and foreign-element senses remain Classical Arabic meanings.
The Form I sexual sense is construction-specific and should not be inferred from ordinary physical-entry occurrences.
Some rare zoological, agricultural, and technical senses are attributed or variant in the lexical evidence but are retained because they state genuine lexical uses.

درأ.summary: The root centers on deflecting or pushing something to one side or away, yielding the ideas of warding off, defense, mutual repulsion, and related physical or figurative extensions.
درأ.development: From lateral deflection and pushing away, the lexical range develops into averting harm, contending by mutual repulsion, and extensions involving crookedness, projection, sudden emergence, and forceful outpouring.

senses.definition: To repel, ward off, avert, or defend against something.
senses.when: In the Quran, the object warded off may be evil, punishment, or death; the construction may express repelling one thing by means of another, as well as averting something from a person or group.

senses.definition: To contend or dispute with one another, each repelling the other or shifting responsibility onto the other.
senses.when: The Quranic form is the assimilated surface form ادَّارَأَ; the underlying Form VI construction is تَدَارَأَ, expressing mutual repulsion in a dispute.

cautions: No Maqayis entry was supplied; the root-level orientation is based on the supplied Mufradat and Lane evidence.
The Quranic Form VI surface ادَّارَأْتُمْ is an assimilated form related to the normalized citation form تَدَارَأَ.
The Lane discussion of كَوْكَبٌ دِرِّيءٌ records competing vocalizations and lexical analyses; it is retained as broader Classical evidence, not as a Quranic form of this QAC root.

دعو.summary: The root centers on drawing something toward oneself through speech or sound: calling, summoning, asking, or inviting.
دعو.development: From this central idea develop supplication and invocation, calling people toward a way, claims and asserted affiliation, reciprocal calling and assembly, and figurative senses of attraction, inducement, or successive collapse.

senses.definition: To call, summon, or invite someone or a group; to call people toward a way or course.
senses.when: The object may be a person, group, or course of action; the construction with إِلَى expresses calling or inviting toward something.

senses.definition: To pray to, supplicate, petition, or invoke God, seeking a benefit or relief.
senses.when: This includes humble petition and calling upon God in hardship; لِ may introduce a prayer for someone, while عَلَى may introduce an imprecation against someone.

senses.definition: To call upon someone or something for aid or support.
senses.when: In this use the object is summoned as an aid or witness, as in calling helpers to one's assistance.

senses.definition: To call out for, or utter a cry concerning, a named thing or outcome.
senses.when: The construction may express a lament or a cry for a specified fate, including calling for ruin or destruction; this is distinct from ordinary interpersonal summoning.

senses.definition: To call or draw someone away, with the resulting sense of bringing punishment, destruction, or an evil event upon him.
senses.when: This figurative Quran-attested use is interpreted in more than one closely related way: drawing away, bringing to punishment, or destroying.

senses.definition: To claim, assert, or maintain that something belongs to oneself, is true, or is due to oneself; to demand it as a claim.
senses.when: The claim may be true or false and may be directed against another person or concern a thing asserted as one's own.

cautions: The Form VIII Quranic passages admit closely related interpretive alternatives between claiming, desiring or demanding, and in one passage denying or disbelieving.

The figurative Form I use associated with calling away or destruction has divergent Classical explanations; the artifact preserves the shared draw-away/punitive branch without treating one interpretation as certain.

دنو.summary: The root centers on nearness: being close, drawing near, or bringing something near. Its comparative extensions describe what is nearer, lower, less, or more suitable.
دنو.development: Concrete spatial proximity extends to temporal, relational, and figurative closeness. The feminine comparative دُنْيَا develops the conventional sense of the present or nearer world, contrasted with the hereafter.

senses.definition: To draw near or approach.
senses.when: Used of physical, spatial, temporal, or otherwise apprehensible approach; the Quran includes an approach expressed without a direct object.

senses.definition: To bring or draw something near; to draw it down toward or over someone.
senses.when: A transitive construction; in the Quranic clothing expression, it denotes drawing part of an outer garment down over the body.

senses.definition: Nearer or nearest; closer in place, relation, time, or degree.
senses.when: A comparative or superlative adjective, opposed to أَقْصَى in spatial or relational comparison and used more broadly for what is closer.

senses.definition: More suitable, more apt, or more likely to achieve the intended result.
senses.when: A figurative comparative of closeness: what is nearer to the desired or appropriate outcome.

senses.definition: Less or smaller in amount, number, or degree.
senses.when: Used in comparison with what is greater or more; the Quran applies it to a lesser punishment and to a smaller amount of recitation.

senses.definition: Lower, inferior, worse, or of lesser worth.
senses.when: Opposed to خير or to what is better; it may be substantivized for what is lower or inferior, including the lower worldly life.

cautions: The QAC packet places the Quranic يُدْنِينَ occurrence in the دَنَا Form I group, while the supplied lexical discussion treats the transitive garment-drawing construction under أَدْنَى/Form IV; the public form follows QAC identity and records the constructional sense explicitly.

دور.summary: The root centers on enclosing or surrounding something from all around it, and hence on circular movement, turning, circulation, and what comes around or encompasses.
دور.development: From the basic idea of surrounding arise movement in a circle, recurrence and circulation, circumferential forms, adverse circumstances that envelop people, and places or communities understood as a dwelling or bounded domain.

senses.definition: To turn, revolve, or move around; to circle.
senses.when: Quranic Form I imperfect usage describing circular or revolving movement.

senses.definition: To circulate or pass something back and forth between people; to give and take it from hand to hand.
senses.when: In the Quranic commercial construction, the merchandise is present and exchanged between the parties without deferral.

senses.definition: A turn of fortune, especially an adverse turn, calamity, or misfortune that overtakes and envelops people.
senses.when: The Quranic expressions دائرة السوء and الدوائر refer to harmful circumstances or reversals of fortune; the plural form denotes such turns collectively.

senses.definition: A house, home, or place of residence; a dwelling or group of dwellings.
senses.when: Includes Quranic singular and plural forms, including دِيَار, when referring to people's houses or inhabited residences.

senses.definition: An abode, domain, or established dwelling-place, including a worldly or hereafter realm.
senses.when: Used in Quranic expressions such as the abode of this world, the Hereafter, peace, or the transgressors; the meaning is determined by the accompanying qualifier and context.

senses.definition: An inhabitant or resident; a person dwelling in a place.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence appears in a negative construction meaning that no inhabitant or resident is to be left.

cautions: The Quranic form دَيَّارٌ is presented with the general lexical sense inhabitant; its Quranic context is a negative construction, while broader Classical usage is not restricted to negation.
دَارٌ encompasses both concrete homes and qualified abodes or domains in Quranic usage; the plural forms دِيَارٌ and دُورٌ are included under the same public noun.

دوم.summary: The root centers on settling or remaining attached to something, yielding the ideas of continuity, persistence, and lasting duration.
دوم.development: From stillness and abiding, the lexicon develops meanings of enduring over time, making something lasting, continuous rain, and related derived senses such as apparent suspension or circling. Some derived usages extend metaphorically to moderation, waiting, and seeking continuance.

senses.definition: To continue, remain, or endure over a period of time.
senses.when: In the Quran, it occurs in ما دام temporal constructions, meaning “as long as,” “while,” or “for as long as” someone or something remains in a stated condition.

senses.definition: Continuing, enduring, lasting, or constant; perpetual or everlasting.
senses.when: Used adjectivally or predicatively for something enduring, as with everlasting fruit, and for persons constant in a sustained practice.

cautions: The Classical evidence preserves distinct, sometimes contrasting branches: duration and persistence, stillness, and circling or apparent suspension. The Quranic forms are restricted to the attested duration and constancy senses.

دون.summary: The root is oriented toward nearness and relative proximity: one thing is nearer, lower, or adjacent to another.
دون.development: From this relational notion, the lexicon develops expressions for being below or less than a reference point, beside or apart from it, approaching it, and urging someone to take hold of or approach something. These root-level developments do not apply uniformly to every Quranic occurrence.

senses.definition: Other than, besides, apart from, or instead of.
senses.when: Commonly used in constructions such as مِنْ دُونِ followed by a noun or pronoun, expressing exclusion, separation, or the selection of one thing instead of another. In some religious interpretations, the construction can describe entities regarded as means or intermediaries toward God; this is an interpretation of the relation, not a separate lexical sense.

senses.definition: Less than, below a specified amount, degree, or standard.
senses.when: Used comparatively or with a stated reference point, including constructions equivalent to “what is less than that.” The Quranic alternatives “less than” and “other than” are related through the notion of falling short of or lying outside a stated limit.

senses.definition: Lower or inferior in rank, estimation, or condition than another.
senses.when: May describe a party or person as below another in rank, religious standing, or another basis of comparison; it need not mean mere physical position.

senses.definition: Below, beneath, or beside a reference point.
senses.when: A spatial or relational use, especially in constructions with مِنْ, locating something below or beside another party. The sense is distinct from general exclusion when the relation is primarily positional.

senses.definition: Before or prior to in time.
senses.when: An adverbial use expressing precedence relative to a later event or stated reference.

cautions: دُونَ has Classical attestations with contrary evaluative values: lower or inferior, and in some usage higher or more eminent. The Quranic senses above are restricted to the usages supported for the relevant constructions.
The validity of the derived verbs دَانَ and أُدِينَ is disputed in the lexical evidence; the reported Classical meanings are retained without treating them as Quranic forms.
The Quran examples use only QAC-supplied modern locations; historical citation notation in the lexical evidence is not converted into additional modern verse locations.

ذرر.summary: The root centers on fineness joined with spreading or dispersal: minute particles, sprinkling, and things emerging in small dispersed forms.
ذرر.development: The semantic orientation extends from scattering salt, grain, or medicine to fine particles, dispersed light at sunrise, and the emergence of small shoots or parts. Some further usages are figurative or divergent extensions.

senses.definition: An atom-sized particle, mote, or speck.
senses.when: In Quranic expressions concerning the weight or effect of even the smallest amount, it denotes an exceedingly minute particle.

senses.definition: Offspring, children, or descendants.
senses.when: A collective family term that can refer to a person's children or continuing progeny; the Quranic form occurs in both singular and plural morphology.

cautions: The packet records an unresolved suggestion that ذُرِّيَّة may originally involve hamza; this artifact follows the canonical QAC root ذ ر ر.
The aversion branch has a reported etymological disagreement over whether it belongs with ذَرَّ or ذَأَرَ, but it is retained because it is directly included in the supplied lexical evidence.

ذكر.summary: The root centers on retaining or bringing something to mind, from which arise remembering, mentioning, reminding, revealed reminders, and honor through being remembered. A distinct branch concerns the male or masculine and extensions of that notion to strength and related qualities.
ذكر.development: The root principle is described as two main developments: remembering what was forgotten and the resulting remembrance or speech; and the male/masculine branch, with figurative extensions to vigor, hardness, and sharpness.

senses.definition: To remember, recall, or bring something to mind.
senses.when: Includes recollection after forgetting and keeping a person or thing mentally present.

senses.definition: To mention, tell, relate, or say something.
senses.when: May refer to mentioning a person, event, or matter aloud; the contextual force may be neutral, favorable, or reproachful.

senses.definition: To be mindful of something and not neglect it; to heed or attend to it.
senses.when: Used with a right, claim, favor, instruction, or revealed teaching, with the sense of bearing it in mind and acting accordingly. Devotional remembrance may also include praising and glorifying God.

senses.definition: To remind or cause someone to remember something.
senses.when: The object may be a person, event, teaching, or matter previously known or liable to be forgotten; in the testimony construction, one woman reminds the other.

senses.definition: To admonish, exhort, or give a reminder.
senses.when: Often involves urging obedience and recalling the consequences of conduct, including reward and punishment.

senses.definition: To remember, recall, or take heed.
senses.when: The form commonly presents remembering as an inward response to a sign, teaching, warning, or prior knowledge, and may therefore be rendered “take heed,” “learn a lesson,” or “receive admonition.”

cautions: Historical Lane Quran citations are retained only as lexical evidence; they have not been mechanically converted into modern verse locations.
The repentance interpretation of ذِكْرَىٰ is explicitly reported in the lexical evidence, but its historical citation does not securely identify a supplied modern word location.
The Quranic male noun is kept separate from Classical figurative uses such as strength, sharpness, and excellence.

ذهب.summary: The root combines the radiance and beauty associated with gold with the movement or passing-away of a thing.
ذهب.development: From these orientations develop the senses of going, departing, being removed, and taking something away, alongside derivatives for gold, gilding, routes or doctrines, and related figurative uses.

senses.definition: To go, pass along, proceed, travel, or depart.
senses.when: An intransitive verb of movement; it may take إِلَى for a destination and may describe movement in any manner or at any pace.

senses.definition: To go away, leave, or pass away; of an affliction, quality, or force, to cease or dissipate.
senses.when: With عَنْ, the subject goes away from or ceases to affect someone or something. The sense can also be figurative, as when a force or condition disappears.

senses.definition: With بِ, to go away with, carry off, take possession of, or appropriate something.
senses.when: The بِ construction may emphasize accompanying or carrying something away, or the resulting acquisition of it; in the Quran it can describe securing part of something previously given.

senses.definition: With بِ, to cause something to go away: to take away, remove, dispel, or make it cease.
senses.when: This transitive construction is used for physical or abstract objects, including light and other conditions; it need not mean that the agent accompanies the object.

senses.definition: To perish or be consumed, especially in the Quranic expression concerning one’s self being overcome by grief.
senses.when: A figurative idiom in which the going-away of the self is associated with death or ruin, rather than ordinary physical travel.

senses.definition: To make something or someone go away; to remove, dispel, or take away.
senses.when: A causative Form IV verb used for people, afflictions, sins, sorrow, ritual impurity, and other things that can be made to disappear or cease.

cautions: The Form I construction ذَهَبَ بِهِ has overlapping senses of accompanying or carrying something away and causing it to disappear; the Quranic examples support both acquisition/carrying-off and removal contexts.
The devil-related use of مُذْهِبٌ is attributed in the lexical record and its status as genuine Arabic is disputed.

رأي.summary: A root centered on seeing and perceiving, whether by the eye or by understanding and discernment.
رأي.development: The lexical branches extend from visual perception to mental apprehension, judgment, reciprocal visibility, outward appearance, ostentatious display, and visions in sleep. These developments are related but are not identical meanings of every derived form.

senses.definition: To see or perceive with the eye, or through an analogous means of perception.
senses.when: Includes ordinary visual perception and expressions in which seeing is attributed analogically to one whose perception is not bodily.

senses.definition: To suppose, imagine, or envisage something as being the case.
senses.when: A mental or imaginative apprehension rather than direct physical sight; tense and mood may make the sense hypothetical or prospective.

senses.definition: To discern through reflection or deliberate consideration.
senses.when: Used when the act of seeing denotes attentive reflection that brings something to perception or understanding.

senses.definition: To mentally perceive, know, or judge something to be so.
senses.when: With two objects, the construction presents a person or thing as possessing a stated quality; this branch also covers the Quranic use meaning that something has been made known or taught.

senses.definition: To consider a matter attentively so as to take warning or draw an admonition.
senses.when: Especially occurs with إِلَى in the construction أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى, which directs attention toward a case and its significance rather than merely asking about visual sight.

senses.definition: In أَرَأَيْتَ and related expressions, to call for an account of a matter: “tell me” or “have you considered?”
senses.when: A conventional attention-arousing construction; the attached ك may function as an allocutive particle, while the verb retains its person and number marking.

cautions: Lane's printed Quran citations use historical conventions and are not treated as modern verse locations unless the corresponding QAC location independently identifies the passage.

Several homographic branches concern the lungs, banners, mirrors, appearance, pregnancy signs, and ostentation; they are kept separate from the Quranic Form I seeing branch unless the lexical evidence explicitly connects the use.

The Quranic form group for رأَى is authoritative for identifying inflected forms such as أَرَاكَ; related causative interpretations are therefore assigned to the QAC form group in which the occurrence is classified.

ربب.summary: The root centers on taking charge of something, caring for it, possessing or governing it, and bringing it toward completion.
ربب.development: Related branches extend this orientation to remaining with something, causing increase, joining or gathering things together, and forming bonds or covenants.

senses.definition: Lord: the creator, possessor, sustainer, and disposer of creatures, who cares for their affairs and brings them toward completion.
senses.when: With the definite article, رَبّ is properly used of God; in Quranic possessive and related constructions it denotes God's lordship over a domain or creature.

senses.definition: Lord, master, owner, or person exercising authority over another person or thing.
senses.when: This human or worldly use occurs chiefly in an annexed construction or a context that identifies the person as a master, owner, or authority; in the Quran it includes the master addressed in the story of Joseph.

senses.definition: Stepdaughter: a woman's daughter by another husband, regarded as a daughter because she is reared or cared for in the household.
senses.when: The Quranic plural occurs in the construction رَبَائِبُكُمُ الَّلاتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ, referring to stepdaughters in the household context.

senses.definition: A person devoted to God and religious learning: deeply learned, grounded in religious knowledge, and able to teach and nurture others in it.
senses.when: The Quranic plural refers to religious authorities or scholars whose learning, devotion, practice, and instruction are associated with the Lord; the evidence allows emphasis on devotion, knowledge, or teaching.

senses.definition: A learned, pious, steadfast religious person or scholar devoted to the Lord.
senses.when: In the Quranic plural, the word may describe people characterized by religious learning, devotion, and steadfastness; it is treated in the evidence as closely related to رَبَّانِيٌّ.

senses.definition: A numerous company or multitude of people.
senses.when: This interpretation belongs to the Quran-attested lexical discussion of the plural رِبِّيُّونَ; related readings and explanations connect it with a large company or thousands of people.

cautions: The Quranic group رِبِّيُّونَ has two lexically reported interpretations in the supplied evidence: learned or religiously devoted people, and a numerous company; the Quran Foundation gloss supports the former but does not eliminate the latter.
رَبٌّ is divine when used absolutely with the definite article, while Quranic contexts also attest its use for a human master or owner in an annexed construction, especially in the story of Joseph.
The Quranic plural رَبَّانِيُّونَ is normalized under the singular citation form رَبَّانِيٌّ; related vocalized forms and etymologies are disputed in the classical evidence.

ربو.summary: The supplied evidence centers on increase, growth, swelling, and elevation.
ربو.development: The lexical field extends from something becoming larger or higher to rearing and cultivation, elevated land, increasing or excessive returns, and states of bodily inflation or breathlessness. These are related developments, not a single meaning of every form.

senses.definition: To increase, grow, or swell.
senses.when: In the Quran this describes the earth swelling and growing after rain, and an increase sought in people's property. The physical and economic contexts instantiate the same intransitive notion of becoming greater.

senses.definition: To rear, foster, nourish, or bring up.
senses.when: A transitive causative verb used in the Quran for bringing up a person. The broader lexical range also includes nourishing or cultivating a growing thing.

senses.definition: To increase, augment, or become more numerous.
senses.when: In the Quran the verb is used for multiplying or increasing the recompense of alms and for being more numerous or abundant. The construction may therefore express either augmentation of something or comparative numerical excess.

senses.definition: An elevated piece of ground; a hill or high ground.
senses.when: The Quran uses the noun for elevated terrain, including the elevated site associated with a garden and the elevated place where Jesus and his mother were settled.

senses.definition: Rising, swelling, or exceeding in extent or intensity.
senses.when: This active-participle adjective is used in the Quran for foam rising above a flood and for a punishment exceeding other punishments. The feminine Quran form رَابِيَة is included under the same citation form.

senses.definition: An increase taken or stipulated in lending or exchange; usury.
senses.when: In Quranic usage the noun denotes the legally specified usurious increase, especially an added return in lending or transactions, rather than ordinary beneficial increase. The Quran contrasts this gain with divinely blessed charity.

cautions: Lane's printed Quran references use historical citation conventions; modern verse locations in the examples are taken from QAC rather than reconstructed from Lane's notation.

The Quranic form رَابِيَة is presented under the normalized active-participle citation form رَابٍ, while its Classical-only breathlessness specialization remains separate from the Quranic rising-or-exceeding sense.
The broader Classical discussion of رِبًا includes forms of excess or added return that should not automatically be equated with the Quranic legal sense of usury.

رحم.summary: A root oriented toward tenderness, compassion, and beneficent favor.
رحم.development: The semantic field develops from compassionate feeling to enacted beneficence, while the womb and kinship are connected through the origin and bonds of birth. The divine names الرَّحْمَٰن and الرَّحِيم express this field as encompassing and abundant mercy, respectively, though the sources also record some synonymy between them.

senses.definition: To show mercy, compassionate favor, or beneficent care toward someone.
senses.when: Used of human or divine action. With God as subject, it denotes beneficent action rather than human emotional tenderness; Quranic forms include active, passive, and imperative constructions.

senses.definition: Womb: the bodily place and receptacle in which offspring originate and develop.
senses.when: The Quranic form is the plural أَرْحَام, used for wombs in contexts concerning gestation and birth.

senses.definition: Kinship, a family relationship, or ties of blood relationship.
senses.when: In أولو الأرحام and related constructions, it denotes kin relations. Legal usage can include relations without a prescribed inheritance share or agnatic status, and ذُو رَحِمٍ مَحْرَمٍ denotes a relation whom it is unlawful to marry.

senses.definition: More merciful; most merciful.
senses.when: Used comparatively and in the superlative expression أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ, “the most merciful of those who show mercy.”

senses.definition: Compassion; merciful concern expressed toward another.
senses.when: A noun of the mercy-and-compassion branch, used in the Quran in the construction بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ.

senses.definition: Mercy: compassionate favor or beneficent care.
senses.when: The ordinary Quranic abstract noun; when attributed to God, it denotes enacted beneficence rather than a human emotional state. It may be possessed, bestowed, received, or sought.

cautions: The distinction between رَحْمَٰن and رَحِيم is presented as a supported usage distinction, not an absolute etymological rule; the lexical evidence also records authorities who treat them as synonymous.

Several Lane Quran citations use historical citation conventions. Specialized interpretations have been represented where supported, but modern verse locations are given only where the QAC packet independently supplies the location securely.

ردد.summary: The root centers on returning, sending something back, or causing it to revert from a course or state.
ردد.development: From the core notion of return, the lexical family extends to restoration, repulsion, reversal, repeated movement, support that prevents falling, apostasy as a return to unbelief, and several specialized bodily and figurative uses.

senses.definition: To return, restore, send back, or bring something or someone back to a former place, holder, condition, or advantage.
senses.when: May take a direct object or occur with إلى for return to a destination or authority. The Quranic expression about putting hands into mouths describes putting them back there, with the surrounding context indicating repeated action.

senses.definition: To turn someone or something back, repel it, avert it, or prevent it from proceeding toward an outcome.
senses.when: Includes turning a person back from a course or former state and averting an event, benefit, or punishment. The object need not be a physical entity.

senses.definition: To refer an affair, dispute, or judgment to an authority for consideration or decision.
senses.when: Constructed with إلى for referring the matter to a person or authority; this is a conventional extension of returning an affair to its proper source.

senses.definition: To waver, hesitate, or vacillate in uncertainty, being unable to settle on a course.
senses.when: The Quranic usage describes inward hesitation and perplexity rather than merely repeated physical movement.

senses.definition: To return, go back, retrace one's route, or revert to a former state.
senses.when: May describe ordinary movement back, the return of a faculty such as sight, or turning away from a prior course without necessarily referring to religion.

senses.definition: To turn away from Islam and return to unbelief; to apostatize.
senses.when: This religious sense is a specialized use of returning from one state or allegiance to another and is explicitly associated with turning away from one's religion.

cautions: رَآدِّي is treated as an inflected sound masculine plural active participle in a possessive construction and is therefore merged under the citation form رَادّ.

The Lane entry رِدٌّ reports a Quran reading variant meaning support or refuge, but no corresponding QAC form group or secure QAC word location is supplied; it is retained as a Classical lexical meaning rather than assigned to a Quranic form.
Lane's historical Quran citation notation is not used to generate modern verse locations; all Quran examples use only locations supplied by QAC.

رزق.summary: A root centered on giving or assigning a beneficial provision that reaches a recipient.
رزق.development: The basic idea is an allotted gift, originally associated with a provision assigned for a time, and extended to material sustenance, other benefits, and non-time-bound divine bounty.

senses.definition: To bestow, grant, or provide someone with sustenance or another beneficial endowment.
senses.when: A transitive verb that may take a recipient and the provision or benefit supplied as its object; Quranic active and passive forms include providing people with material or other beneficial gifts and being provided with them.

senses.definition: An ongoing provision, gift, or beneficial endowment that reaches a recipient, whether worldly or eschatological.
senses.when: May refer to material sustenance, wealth, status, knowledge, or other beneficial bounty; the Quranic use is not restricted to food.

senses.definition: Food or nourishment taken into the body.
senses.when: Used for a concrete edible provision or what sustains a person through eating.

senses.definition: Rain understood as provision.
senses.when: A Quranic figurative use in which rain, especially rain that sustains life, is called provision; this sense should not be generalized to every occurrence of the noun.

senses.definition: An allotted share of blessing; by a Quranic interpretation, the acknowledgment or thanksgiving due for a bestowed blessing.
senses.when: In the expression associated with 56:82, the share or response to blessing is portrayed as being replaced by denial rather than gratitude.

senses.definition: A provider: one who gives provision or serves as a means by which provision reaches others.
senses.when: The Quranic plural can refer to providers generally while affirming that God is the best or ultimate provider; the lexical use includes a causal intermediary as well as a giver.

cautions: Lane’s printed citation for the thanksgiving interpretation uses historical notation; the modern example 56:82 is used because that location is independently supplied by QAC, not by converting Lane’s bracketed citation mechanically.

رسل.summary: The root centers on being sent forth and extending outward, especially in an easy, unforced manner.
رسل.development: From easy movement and gradual extension develop the ideas of release, dispatch, successive company, communication, and the messenger who conveys a message.

senses.definition: To send, dispatch, or cause someone or something to go or arrive.
senses.when: Used for sending prophets, messengers, people, angels, forces, rain, wind, and other things; the construction may express sending down, upon, against, or with a message. Active, passive, and imperative forms occur in the Quran.

senses.definition: To release, let loose, or leave unrestrained; hence, to set or turn something against others.
senses.when: A distinct Quranic use in which sending involves releasing or appointing something with power over others, especially in the passage about the devils sent against the unbelievers.

senses.definition: Those sent forth: winds sent forth.
senses.when: One interpretation of the feminine plural passive participle in 77:1; the form is used substantively and occurs only in this Quranic expression.

senses.definition: Those sent forth: angels sent forth.
senses.when: An alternative interpretation of the same Quranic expression in 77:1.

senses.definition: Those sent forth: horses started successively in a race.
senses.when: An alternative interpretation of the same Quranic expression, emphasizing successive release in the racecourse.

senses.definition: One who sends, dispatches, or releases.
senses.when: An active participle of أَرْسَلَ, used substantively for a sender and in contexts where sending has the sense of releasing or setting something forth.

cautions: The Quranic expression المُرْسَلَاتِ in 77:1 has several transmitted lexical interpretations—winds, angels, or horses sent successively—and these are kept as distinct senses rather than collapsed.
رَسُول can denote either the bearer of a message or, in a specifically discussed Quranic construction, the conveyed message itself.

Several Classical Arabic entries distinguish ordinary message, written letter, treatise, and apostolic office; only the message sense supported for the Quranic رِسَالَة forms is placed in the Quranic form entry.

رسو.summary: The root centers on being fixed, stationary, or firmly established, and on causing something to become so.
رسو.development: Its lexical development extends from remaining firm or settled to anchoring ships, fixing objects, designating places or times of anchoring, and figurative settling or remaining.

senses.definition: To make firm, fixed, or firmly established.
senses.when: A transitive use whose Quranic object is the mountains; the sense concerns causing them to be firmly set.

senses.definition: The place or state of anchoring; an anchorage or place where something comes to rest.
senses.when: In the Quranic expression concerning the ship, it denotes its anchorage or being brought to rest.

senses.definition: The appointed time of being established or of an event taking place.
senses.when: Used of the appointed time or arrival of an event, especially the eschatological Hour.

senses.definition: Firmly fixed, stationary, or immovable; in the Quran, firmly set mountains and fixed cooking pots.
senses.when: The Quranic group is chiefly the plural رَوَاسِي and also includes رَاسِيَات; the same fixedness is applied to mountains and, in one passage, to large cooking pots that remain in place.

cautions: The supplied QAC metadata labels the أَرْسَىٰ group as Form I, while its Arabic shape and the matched lexical evidence identify the citation form conventionally as Form IV; the public morphology label follows the supplied QAC metadata.
مُرْسًى is a substantivized passive-participial form whose Quranic contexts support both place/state and appointed-time readings.

رعد.summary: The root centers on movement, agitation, and trembling.
رعد.development: From the basic idea of motion and disturbance, the root develops into thunder and the trembling it causes, as well as figurative threatening speech and several extensions describing quivering or shaken things.

senses.definition: Thunder: the sound associated with clouds or the sky.
senses.when: The direct Quranic contextual use denotes the audible phenomenon of thunder.

senses.definition: The angel understood in a reported interpretation as driving the clouds.
senses.when: This is a reported interpretation of the Quranic term alongside the direct sense “thunder,” not an interpretation that must replace the meteorological sense in every occurrence.

cautions: The two Quranic occurrences are contextually rendered as thunder; the angel identification is preserved as a reported interpretation rather than treated as the only meaning.

رفع.summary: The root denotes raising or elevating, as opposed to lowering or putting down.
رفع.development: From physical elevation, the lexical field extends to making something high in rank or esteem, bringing it forward or near, making it known or attributing it to a source, and in some constructions removing or withdrawing it.

senses.definition: To raise, elevate, or lift a physical thing or person, including to rear or make a structure high.
senses.when: Used for raising something from its resting place, making it high, and in constructions with an object raised above or toward a higher place.

senses.definition: To elevate in rank, dignity, esteem, or fame; to raise someone's standing or renown.
senses.when: A figurative use for elevation of status, degrees, honor, or mention; it can also express holding someone or something above a lower matter.

senses.definition: To accept and honor a righteous work, or to cause good speech to ascend toward acceptance.
senses.when: A Quranic construction in which يَرْفَعُهُ is interpreted either as divine acceptance of righteous work or as righteous work raising good speech to acceptance.

senses.definition: Raised, elevated, or set high.
senses.when: Used of things physically elevated or placed above others, including the raised heavens and elevated furnishings.

senses.definition: Honored, exalted, or high in estimation.
senses.when: A figurative interpretation in which elevation denotes distinction, honor, or elevated status.

senses.definition: Brought near or made readily presented to those concerned.
senses.when: Especially in the interpretation of مَرْفُوعَةٍ in the expression وَفُرُشٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ; this is a conventional extension of raising to bringing near.

cautions: The Quranic phrase بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ is explicitly presented with both physical-elevation and honor-based interpretations; it is therefore represented under both corresponding verb senses.
The interpretations of وَفُرُشٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ include physical elevation, honor, and bringing near; these alternatives are retained as distinct but related senses.

رود.summary: The root is centered on going to and fro in pursuit of something, especially moving through a field or direction while searching; from this develop meanings of seeking, gently approaching or inducing, and willing or intending.
رود.development: The semantic path runs from movement and roaming to searching and selecting, then to the gentleness associated with careful seeking. The Form IV meaning of willing or intending is treated as a developed lexical branch, while the Quranic Form III meaning retains the sense of trying to turn or induce another.

senses.definition: To try to turn, induce, or persuade someone toward or away from something, using persistent effort, blandishment, or artifice.
senses.when: Commonly followed by عن or على. The construction presents an effort to alter another person's decision, stance, or compliance.

senses.definition: To seek sexual intercourse with someone by enticement or persuasion.
senses.when: In the construction راوده عن نفسه, the object of the attempted persuasion is sexual access or intercourse; this is a specific Quran-attested use of the broader inducing construction.

senses.definition: To want, wish, will, or choose an object or action.
senses.when: The ordinary agentive use expresses a person's or other capable subject's inclination or decision concerning an object, action, or outcome.

senses.definition: To intend, mean, aim at, or pursue an outcome.
senses.when: This use emphasizes directed purpose or what a person seeks to bring about, including an intended result or goal; it can overlap with ordinary wishing without being limited to an inward desire.

senses.definition: Of God, to will an outcome by determining, prescribing, or decreeing it.
senses.when: When the subject is God, the Quranic use is not a human-like psychological inclination; it denotes the determined or normative divine will, including what God prescribes or brings about.

senses.definition: To be about or ready to do something, especially of an inanimate thing approaching a state or event.
senses.when: In the construction أراد أن followed by an event, an inanimate subject may be described as tending or being ready to undergo that event, as with a wall about to fall.

cautions: The Quranic Form III and Form IV verbs are separate lexical forms: رَاوَدَ concerns trying to turn or induce another person, while أَرَادَ primarily concerns willing, intending, or pursuing an outcome.
The Form IV Quranic uses include divine, normative, and inanimate constructions; these should not all be reduced to a single human psychological sense.

زبد.summary: The root denotes something generated or produced from something else, especially foam or froth arising on a liquid.
زبد.development: From the production of foam, related usages extend to churned butter, white blossom, intense whiteness, gifts, and other things understood as produced or brought forth.

senses.definition: Foam or froth formed on water.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence denotes the foam produced or carried by water; related Classical applications to other substances are listed separately.

cautions: The Quranic noun زَبَدٌ denotes foam in the water passage; butter, gifts, perfume, and the derived verbal forms are distinct Classical lexical uses rather than additional Quranic senses.

Several Classical attestations preserve explicitly qualified alternatives, including the milk-froth reading under زُبْدٌ, the thin-milk reading under زُبَادٌ, and the alternative interpretation of the sawīq construction.

زرع.summary: The root centers on bringing something into growth or development, concretely through sowing and the emergence of cultivated produce.
زرع.development: Its semantic field extends from casting seed and the crop that results to cultivation, growers, offspring, and figurative harvests, while these developments are not automatically meanings of every derived form.

senses.definition: To sow or plant by casting seed.
senses.when: The Quranic use describes human sowing or planting, including the sowing of a crop; the form may also be transitive with the plant or produce concerned.

senses.definition: To cause seed-produce to grow, vegetate, or germinate.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction, human beings are associated with sowing as a means, while the actual causing of growth is attributed to God.

senses.definition: Sown produce or crops; cultivated growth, whether standing or reaped, and often the sown field itself.
senses.when: The term predominantly applies to grain such as wheat and barley but can also denote plants or herbage raised by sowing. Quranic contexts include crops, cultivation, and cultivated fields.

senses.definition: A sower or cultivator; figuratively, one who cultivates and advances a cause.
senses.when: In the Quranic plural زُرَّاعٌ in 48:29, the expression refers figuratively to Muhammad and his Companions as inviters to Islam.

senses.definition: One who causes seed-produce to grow, or serves as the human agent or means of its growth.
senses.when: The Quranic plural in 56:64 occurs in a contrast between human sowing and the ultimate causing of growth.

cautions: The Form I Quranic verb is displayed under the normalized perfect citation form زَرَعَ, although the supplied occurrences are imperfect second-person plural forms.

The Quranic زُرَّاعٌ group is merged into the active-participle entry زَارِعٌ because the lexical evidence explicitly identifies it as that lexeme's plural. The contextual English renderings are used only as examples, not as independent sense evidence.

زوج.summary: Pairing or joining one thing with another as its counterpart, associate, or complement.
زوج.development: The pairing principle extends to spouses, paired or contrasting entities, associated groups, and kinds understood as related classes. It can also describe a covering or furnishing associated with what it is placed upon.

senses.definition: To pair, couple, or unite one thing or person with another as its counterpart.
senses.when: In Quranic pairing constructions, the counterparts may be male and female, spouses or mate-like partners, or souls joined with corresponding bodies, records, works, groups, or followers. This use is distinct from ordinary human marriage.

senses.definition: To give one person in marriage to another; to marry one person to another.
senses.when: Used in the conventional marriage construction, as in marrying a woman to a man. This is distinguished from pairing people with houris or other counterparts in the non-marital sense.

senses.definition: A pair or coupled counterpart; one of two things joined as a pair, and sometimes the pair or couple collectively.
senses.when: The paired things may be alike or contrasting. The noun can refer to a fellow or like, or to the two paired things together; number and context determine which reading is intended.

senses.definition: A spouse: a husband or wife regarded as the partner of the other.
senses.when: The same noun can refer to either sex; the surrounding context determines whether husband or wife is intended.

senses.definition: An associate, consociate, comrade, or peer joined to others by companionship, allegiance, or shared conduct.
senses.when: In Quranic plural constructions, the term can denote associates or like-minded counterparts rather than marital spouses.

senses.definition: A kind, sort, species, or category.
senses.when: This use denotes a class or variety understood as related to other classes or varieties, including kinds of created things and kinds of punishment.

cautions: The Form II occurrences translated with marriage in 44:54 and 52:20 are classified under pairing rather than conventional human marriage because the lexical evidence explicitly distinguishes that construction.
Historical citation notation in the Classical source is not used as a modern Quran location; Quran examples here use independently supplied QAC word locations.

زيد.summary: A root oriented toward surplus: something becomes greater than its prior amount or state, or an addition is made to it.
زيد.development: The lexical range develops from increase and excess to addition, augmentation, self-increase, gradual escalation, outbidding, and seeking more. These developments are distributed across distinct derived forms and nouns.

senses.definition: To increase, grow, or become greater in amount or degree.
senses.when: Used intransitively for an amount, state, quality, or condition that increases; grammatical voice and tense vary across the Quranic occurrences.

senses.definition: To increase, augment, or add to something or someone; to give more.
senses.when: Used transitively with the thing increased and, in some constructions, with a person who receives an increase or addition.

senses.definition: To exceed or be more than a reference amount or standard.
senses.when: Especially associated with comparative constructions using عَلَى and with expressions of numerical or relative excess.

senses.definition: To increase, grow, or become greater; to take on an increase.
senses.when: The Form VIII subject undergoes or takes the increase itself, rather than simply causing another object to increase.

senses.definition: More, additional; an amount added beyond what is already present.
senses.when: A passive-participle form used substantivally in Quranic expressions asking whether more is available or stating that more is present.

senses.definition: An increase, addition, or amount beyond the original or existing measure.
senses.when: A verbal noun used for an added amount or further increment; the Quranic contexts include both general addition and a further gift or benefit.

cautions: The supplied Mufradat row is explicitly shared between the roots زود and زيد; its composite discussion was not treated as unique evidence for this root. The form-level Quranic senses are supported directly by Lane evidence.
The etymology of تَزِيدِيَّةٌ is disputed in the lexical evidence, although its garment sense is clear.

زيل.summary: The root's semantic orientation is separation, divergence, and being set apart.
زيل.development: The lexical development runs from putting things apart and removing them to mutual separation, dispersion, physical spacing, and figurative withdrawal or reserve. The root lexicographic tradition also treats the ياء as historically related to a واو.

senses.definition: In the Quranic negative construction, not to cease; to continue or remain.
senses.when: Used with negative particles such as مَا, لَا, or لَمْ as an incomplete verb. The negated construction conveys continuation or persistence and may govern a subject and predicate.

senses.definition: To separate widely; to disperse or set apart from one another.
senses.when: A transitive causative/intensive separation verb; the Quranic construction uses بَيْنَ to express separation between parties.

senses.definition: To become separated from one another; to become widely apart or dispersed.
senses.when: A reflexive or quasi-passive separation verb, used for parties becoming distinct from one another.

cautions: The Quranic Form I occurrences are used in negative continuation constructions; the supplied word-level contextual glosses may omit the force of the surrounding negative particle.
The root discussion treats the ياء as historically related to a واو; supplemental entries under زول have therefore not been imported as independent direct evidence for this QAC root.
The supplied phrase-level Lane headword contains an apparent transcription error; it is normalized here as الحبيب المُزَايِلُ in accordance with the accompanying explanation.

زين.summary: An orientation toward the beauty of a thing and making it beautiful; zayn is opposed to shayn, ugliness or defect.
زين.development: The root extends from beauty and beautification to adornment as an external means or result, attractive presentation or commendation, worldly display, and becoming adorned. These developments belong to particular derived forms and are not interchangeable in every usage.

senses.definition: To adorn, beautify, decorate, or make the beauty of something apparent.
senses.when: Used for visible or perceptible beautification of things, places, qualities, or circumstances. The Quran uses both active and passive constructions; the agent may be stated or left unspecified.

senses.definition: To make something seem attractive, good, or commendable to someone; to commend or present it favorably.
senses.when: Often constructed with لِ and an intended perceiver. The object may be a deed, desire, belief, or other matter, including something morally bad; the agent may be God, Satan, people, or unspecified.

senses.definition: To become adorned or beautified; to come into a visibly attractive state.
senses.when: An intransitive or quasi-reflexive use. In its Quranic occurrence it describes the earth becoming adorned with vegetation.

senses.definition: Adornment, ornament, or embellishment: something by which a person, thing, place, or scene is made attractive.
senses.when: May refer to ornaments, clothing, bodily or natural beauty, and valued worldly display such as wealth and children. Quranic contexts include the adornment of the earth, the heavens, people, and worldly life.

senses.definition: In the expression يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ, a festival or holiday, literally a day of adornment.
senses.when: A conventional expression for a festal day on which people adorn themselves and appear in good clothing.

cautions: The Form V Quranic occurrence is an intransitive or quasi-reflexive use meaning ‘become adorned’; it should not be treated as identical in construction to the transitive Form II verb.
زِينَةٌ ranges from concrete ornaments and natural beauty to valued worldly display; the immediate object and construction determine the intended nuance.

سبح.summary: The root has two closely related semantic orientations: worshipful purification and swift movement or striving.
سبح.development: The movement branch denotes swimming, gliding, rapid travel, and active occupation; the worship branch develops into declaring God free from every imperfection, glorifying Him, and associated acts of prayer and devotion.

senses.definition: To swim, float, or glide swiftly along a course.
senses.when: In the Quran, the subject is celestial bodies moving through their orbits; the image is based on swimming or gliding through water or air.

senses.definition: To declare God free from every imperfection and to glorify, magnify, praise, or celebrate Him.
senses.when: The Quranic construction may occur with or without a preposition and may include praise of God as an accompanying expression; it includes the glorification of God by human beings and by created things.

senses.definition: To pray or perform worship.
senses.when: This is an explicitly attested Quranic interpretation of the verb, including prayer that may be obligatory or supererogatory; the broader devotional sense may include acts beyond formal prayer.

senses.definition: To make an exception by saying “if God wills.”
senses.when: This conventional construction is explicitly applied to the Quranic passage concerning the owners of the garden who failed to qualify their oath.

senses.definition: One who glorifies or praises God; one engaged in tasbih.
senses.when: The participle can describe worship expressed in word, deed, or intention, and applies in the Quran to those characterized by glorification.

senses.definition: One devoted to worship, including prayer.
senses.when: In the account of Jonah, the expression is also interpreted as referring to those who pray; this is a reported interpretation within the broader devotional sense.

cautions: The Quranic expression سَابِحَاتِ has several reported referents—ships, believing souls, angels, or stars—while retaining the common sense of swift gliding.
The Quranic سَبْحًا in 73:7 has several closely related interpretations, including daytime freedom, coming and going, and occupation in one's affairs.
Prayer and the making of an exception are specialized Quranic constructions of سَبَّحَ; they should not be reduced to the ordinary English gloss “glorify.”

سبل.summary: The root centers on sending or extending something downward or outward, and on an extended route or course.
سبل.development: The downward-extension idea appears in hanging garments, falling rain, flowing hair, and vessel edges; extension in length develops into سَبِيلٌ, a way or path, and related travel and grain-ear usages.

senses.definition: A way, road, path, or route; a traversable course.
senses.when: Used literally for a road or route and, in the plural سُبُلٌ, for ways or paths. The term can also denote a clear, open, or easy route.

senses.definition: A course, way, or cause of action, whether good or evil; especially the way of God, religion, truth, guidance, or righteous action.
senses.when: Common in expressions such as سَبِيلُ اللَّهِ, سَبِيلُ رَبِّكَ, سُبُلُ السَّلَامِ, and related constructions. In religious usage it may refer to the cause or way by which one seeks divine favor, and it is often associated with striving or good works.

senses.definition: A means of access, connection, or approach to an end; an avenue to safety or salvation.
senses.when: A figurative use for a means by which one reaches something, including a way to safety or Paradise. It is attested in the construction of taking or finding a سَبِيلٌ with or toward someone or something.

senses.definition: A wayfarer or traveler, especially one stranded away from home, in the expression ابنُ السَّبِيلِ.
senses.when: The phrase literally presents the traveler as the “son of the road.” Quranic usage includes a traveler whose journey or access to resources has been cut off, and who therefore requires assistance.

senses.definition: A ground for blame, reproach, or liability.
senses.when: In constructions such as ما عَلَى ... مِنْ سَبِيلٍ, it denotes no basis for blame or liability; in إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى ..., it denotes the liability or blame that does apply.

senses.definition: In the Quranic construction تَقْطَعُونَ السَّبِيلَ, to cut off or obstruct the way.
senses.when: The passage is interpreted either as preventing offspring through unnatural sexual conduct or as confronting travelers on the roads for an obscene purpose. These are interpretations of the cited construction, not general restrictions on the noun سَبِيلٌ.

cautions: The public Quranic form is normalized to the dictionary citation form سَبِيلٌ; inflection, definiteness, attached pronouns, and the plural سُبُلٌ are not separate public forms.
سَلْسَبِيلُ is retained as a distinct lexical proper name rather than merged into the Quranic form سَبِيلٌ.

Lane's printed Quran references use historical citation conventions. The interpretation associated with its citation of the access sense is preserved without inventing a modern verse location not securely supplied for that occurrence.

سجد.summary: The root centers on lowering oneself with humility and submission, especially by bending down or prostrating.
سجد.development: The basic notion of lowering and humbling develops into physical prostration, voluntary worshipful submission, compelled subjection to divine ordering, and related figurative uses of bending or lowered gaze.

senses.definition: To prostrate oneself: to lower or bend oneself and place the forehead on the ground in worship.
senses.when: Used of voluntary human prostration, including commands and acts of worship; the physical act may also express submission to God or to a commanded object.

senses.definition: To submit humbly or be subjected in obedience to God’s ordering.
senses.when: Used of voluntary human submission and of the involuntary subjection of angels, celestial bodies, plants, shadows, animals, and other created things; it need not denote a voluntary ritual act in nonhuman subjects.

senses.definition: A place of prostration, prayer, or worship; especially a mosque or house of prayer.
senses.when: The term can denote a particular mosque or any place used for worship; in a Quranic interpretation of al-masājid, it may extend to the earth as a whole as a place made available for worship.

senses.definition: A bodily part or point used in prostration; in the plural, the bodily prostration-points.
senses.when: This is a reported Quranic interpretation of al-masājid, with variant enumerations including the forehead, nose, hands, knees, and feet.

senses.definition: Prostrating or bending low in submission; one who performs the act of prostration.
senses.when: An active participle used of people who prostrate in worship and, in the expression for entering the gate, of people who enter with their heads bowed.

senses.definition: Humbly or subserviently subject to God’s command; prostrating in the non-voluntary sense.
senses.when: Used of shadows, plants, and other nonhuman or cosmic entities whose subjection is imposed by their created nature or by divine ordering rather than chosen as human worship.

cautions: The plural al-masājid in 72:18 has both the ordinary place-of-worship interpretation and a reported interpretation as bodily prostration-points; both are retained.
The QAC sujūd group combines verbal-noun uses with adjectival or plural active-participle uses, so these functions are separated as senses under one normalized headword.
Several Lane Quran references use historical citation conventions; the modern verse locations shown here come only from the supplied QAC occurrence data.

سحب.summary: The root centers on dragging or drawing an extended thing along.
سحب.development: From the image of something being drawn along, سحاب is explained as cloud or clouds drawn through the air, or drawing water or one another. Figurative extensions include pressing boldly upon someone. A branch meaning to eat and drink voraciously is also reported, though its derivation is disputed.

senses.definition: To drag or draw along; in the Quranic passive, to be dragged.
senses.when: The supplied Quranic form is a passive imperfect plural. The cited uses describe people being dragged on their faces or into boiling water.

senses.definition: Cloud or clouds, whether rain-bearing or not.
senses.when: The Quranic noun denotes atmospheric cloud or a collection of clouds; singular and collective reference are both compatible with the lexical usage.

senses.definition: By analogy, a cloud-like covering associated with shade and darkness.
senses.when: This figurative interpretation is explicitly applied to the layered-darkness image in the Quranic passage at 24:40.

cautions: The Quranic verb group is attested only as the passive imperfect يُسْحَبُ/يُسْحَبُونَ; the public headword is normalized to the active perfect citation form سَحَبَ.
The voracious-eating branch is independently reported in the classical evidence but is questioned in the root-level discussion as possibly belonging to سَحْت rather than سَحْب.
The eye-cover sense of سُحْبَةٌ is presented cautiously because the evidence gives it as an approximate equivalence with غِشَاوَةٌ.

سخر.summary: The root centers on lowering or bringing under control: contempt and derision in one branch, and subjection or manageable service in another.
سخر.development: From the underlying notion of treating something as low or submissive, Form I develops the meaning “to mock,” while the causative Form II develops the meaning “to subject, render subservient, or make operate according to an intended purpose.” Related nouns denote mockery, a laughingstock, forced service, and obedient ships.

senses.definition: To mock, scoff at, deride, or ridicule someone.
senses.when: The Quranic construction commonly takes مِنْ or بِـ; reciprocal usage can express treating the other as ignorant or foolish in return.

senses.definition: To subject, bring under control, or render subservient or manageable, directing a person, thing, or natural force to an intended purpose.
senses.when: In the Quran this is used of celestial bodies, natural phenomena, animals, ships, and other created things made to serve an appointed order or purpose.

senses.definition: To make a force prevail against someone, sending it upon them with overpowering force.
senses.when: A result-focused causative use, explicitly applied to the wind imposed upon a people.

senses.definition: To invite or induce one another to mock, scoff at, or ridicule.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence has a reciprocal construction in which people encourage each other to engage in mockery.

senses.definition: Made subservient, controlled, or appointed to operate under command.
senses.when: The Quranic uses describe created things, including stars and other natural phenomena, as operating in an ordered course under divine control.

senses.definition: Mockery, scoffing, derision; in the construction of taking people as objects of ridicule or laughingstocks.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrences are in a context of derision. The occurrence in 23:110 is also associated with an alternative interpretation of subjection or forced service.

cautions: سِخْرِيّ in 23:110 is explicitly reported with two interpretations: mockery and subjection or forced service; the examples and senses preserve both rather than forcing a single reading.

The vocalized forms سِخْرِيّ and سُخْرِيّ overlap in broader Classical Arabic evidence, while the Quranic contexts supplied here favor mockery for 23:110 and 38:63 and service or subjection for 43:32.

سرب.summary: The root centers on going forth or extending through open space, especially movement across the land.
سرب.development: From movement through the land, the vocabulary develops into terms for herds and groups, roads and passages, flowing or leaking water, and things that extend or run along a surface.

senses.definition: Going forth or moving along one's way; in the Quranic expression, one who is out or appearing by day.
senses.when: In 13:10, it is contrasted with one who hides by night. The expression is also understood as going along the roads or course by day.

senses.definition: A mirage: a bright semblance of water seen across the land, especially a midday appearance that has no actual water.
senses.when: In 24:39 it occurs in a simile for an apparent but unreal object of expectation; in 78:20 it describes the mountains when they are made to appear as a mirage.

senses.definition: A hidden or subterranean passage or place, such as a burrow or an underground way.
senses.when: In 18:61, the fish's route into the sea is interpreted as a passage or place resembling a subterranean excavation or hidden way.

senses.definition: Going away or taking a downward or onward course; a way taken through a place.
senses.when: In 18:61, the word is also explained as the fish's going away or taking its way into the sea. This is a verbal-noun use rather than the name of a physical passage.

cautions: The Quranic use of سَرَبٌ in 18:61 has closely related but materially different lexical interpretations: a hidden or subterranean passage and the act of going away or taking a course. These are retained as separate senses.
Some Classical entries preserve reported vowel or reading uncertainty, especially سَرْبَةٌ in the stitch-hole sense; that uncertainty is stated in the relevant usage conditions.

سرر.summary: A semantic orientation toward what is hidden, inward, concentrated, or settled in its core.
سرر.development: The root develops from concealment and inwardness to confidential communication, inner or pure substance, the navel and interior, lunar concealment, joy free from grief, and the settled couch or seat.

senses.definition: To please, gladden, or make happy.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence is transitive, with people as those affected by the pleasing action.

senses.definition: To conceal, suppress, or keep something secret.
