senses.when: Used of a matter, statement, feeling, person, or other object kept hidden; the Quranic evidence also includes concealing a person or reciting something privately or inaudibly.

senses.definition: To disclose or confide something privately to an addressee.
senses.when: The construction with إِلَى or a comparable recipient expresses revealing a secret to that person while keeping it from others; the object may be a report, affection, or other confidential matter.

senses.definition: To manifest, publish, or make something known.
senses.when: This contrary interpretation is explicitly reported for the Quranic expression concerning concealing or manifesting regret. It is a disputed reading; concealment is also, and generally more strongly, reported for that expression.

senses.definition: Concealment or secrecy.
senses.when: The verbal noun may describe keeping a matter hidden or conducting it privately.

senses.definition: Private disclosure or confidential communication.
senses.when: With an addressee, إِسْرَار expresses imparting something secretly to that person, while its secrecy is maintained from others.

cautions: أَسَرَّ has a reported but disputed contrary interpretation meaning “manifest” or “publish” in the expression about regret; the concealment interpretation is also explicitly supported and is generally preferred.

The Quranic marriage-related use of سِرّ in 2:235 has varying classical interpretations, including discreet marriage proposal, private sexual union, and—according to some authorities—illicit intercourse.
The public headwords سَرِير and سَرِيرَة are normalized singular citation forms for Quranic plural forms سُرُر and سَرَائِر.

سرع.summary: The root denotes speed and quickness, in opposition to slowness.
سرع.development: Its semantic range develops from rapid movement or action to hastening toward a goal, striving to get ahead, precedence, and idioms expressing exceptional immediacy.

senses.definition: To hasten toward or into something; to make haste to reach or undertake it.
senses.when: With إِلَى, the construction expresses hastening toward a goal. With فِي, it can express rushing into a course or condition, including good works, unbelief, or wrongdoing.

senses.definition: To vie with another or others in hastening, striving to arrive first or get ahead.
senses.when: This is the competitive or reciprocal use of Form III; the goal of the striving may be expressed with إِلَى.

senses.definition: Swift, quick, or rapid.
senses.when: The Quranic form occurs in predicates describing the speed or promptness of an action, especially in expressions concerning reckoning and punishment.

senses.definition: Prompt and not delayed in reckoning or punishment.
senses.when: In the predicates سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ and سَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ, the adjective conveys the immediate and inevitable execution of divine reckoning or punishment, rather than physical speed.

senses.definition: Swifter, quickest, or most rapid.
senses.when: This elative adjective expresses comparison or superlative degree; in the Quran it is used of the one quickest in reckoning and of something more swift in response or outcome.

senses.definition: Hastening; rapid movement, used adverbially as “swiftly” or “rapidly.”
senses.when: The Quranic occurrences are accusative adverbial expressions describing coming forth or emerging with haste.

cautions: A Lane citation rendered in historical form such as “iii. 170” has not been converted into a modern verse key; Quran examples use only QAC-secure locations.
The Quranic سِرَاعٌ group is classified in the supplied QAC morphology as a verbal noun, while Classical evidence also attests سِرَاعٌ as a plural of سَرِيعٌ; these uses are kept distinct.

سقي.summary: The root centers on making something absorb water or a comparable liquid, especially giving drink or supplying water.
سقي.development: From the basic act of giving water, the lexicon develops distinctions between directly giving drink, making drink or a water source available, irrigating land, requesting water, and the vessels, places, shares, and agents associated with watering.

senses.definition: To give a person or animal drink; to cause someone to drink or be given drink.
senses.when: The object may be water, milk, or another drink. The passive forms express being given drink. The expression may specify drink from what is in the bellies of animals.

senses.definition: To water or irrigate land, plants, or cultivated produce.
senses.when: Used for supplying water to growing things, including irrigation by water running over or into the land.

senses.definition: To provide or make available drink or water, so that someone may take and use it as desired; to give someone access to a source of drink.
senses.when: Form IV is presented as broader than directly putting drink to someone's mouth: it can make a river, water, or other drink available to the recipient. Passive forms express being supplied with drink.

senses.definition: To seek or request water or drink.
senses.when: The request may be directed to a person who is asked to provide water.

senses.definition: The provision or service of giving drink, especially the provision of drink to pilgrims.
senses.when: In the Quranic pilgrimage context, the term can denote the service, office, or provision associated with giving drink rather than merely the liquid itself.

senses.definition: A vessel used for drinking, especially a drinking cup.
senses.when: In the Joseph narrative it denotes the king's drinking-cup, also used as a measure.

cautions: Form I directly giving drink and Form IV making drink or a water source available are distinct constructions in the supplied Quran-focused evidence.
سِقَايَة has two Quranic uses here: the provision or service of giving drink and a drinking cup.
The Quranic Form X occurrences attest requesting water or drink; the separate classical rain-request use is listed outside the Quranic sense.

سلم.summary: The root centers on safety, soundness, and freedom from harm, and extends to peace, reconciliation, and willing submission.
سلم.development: From the basic idea of being safe and sound come meanings of securing or saving, making peace, submitting or entering into Islam, and related uses such as advance delivery and a ladder as a means of reaching a safe destination.

senses.definition: to make safe, secure, or free from harm; to save or preserve
senses.when: A transitive causative use, including God's saving or securing someone from danger.

senses.definition: to greet or salute someone with a prayer or declaration of peace
senses.when: Used with عَلَى and related greeting constructions; the greeting invokes safety and freedom from harm.

senses.definition: to deliver, hand over, or pay something to its recipient
senses.when: Used with إِلَى or an expressed recipient; includes handing over property or a required payment.

senses.definition: to submit, assent, or yield without opposition
senses.when: Used of accepting a command, decree, judgment, or established truth; this is distinct from physically handing something over.

senses.definition: to submit or resign oneself to God; to become obedient and submissive
senses.when: In religious usage, the verb can denote entering or professing Islam; in fuller usage it includes inward assent and obedient submission, with the object often understood or expressed with لِ.

senses.definition: submission to God and adherence to the religion of Islam
senses.when: As a legal or theological term, it may refer to outward profession and religious affiliation; in its fuller use it includes belief, obedient action, and resignation to God's decree.

cautions: The QAC groups السَّلْم and السِّلْم separately by vocalization; the latter is presented as سِلْم while the former is presented as سَلْم, with the transmitted Quranic readings retained through their form-group accounting.
Some Lane Quran references use historical chapter-and-verse notation; no such citation has been converted into a modern verse location unless the corresponding QAC location is supplied.
The public headword مُسَلَّم is normalized from the Quranic feminine passive participle مُسَلَّمَة, while feminine and plural active-participle forms are grouped under مُسْلِم.

سمو.summary: The root centers on elevation, height, and being raised above or made prominent.
سمو.development: From physical height and upward movement it extends to visibility, eminence, superiority, upper coverings and the sky; the noun اِسْمٌ is explained as a designation that raises its referent into notice.

senses.definition: To name, call, or designate someone or something by a name or description.
senses.when: The Quran uses the verb for assigning names and for polemical designations whose claimed referents or attributes may be denied; the object may be a person, group, or supposed deity.

senses.definition: Named, designated, or fixed by designation; specified or appointed.
senses.when: It commonly qualifies a term, time, period, or other matter whose identity or limit has been assigned or determined.

senses.definition: The sky or heaven; the elevated expanse above the earth, including the heavens as a collective or plural.
senses.when: The Quran uses the noun in both singular and plural/collective expression, including the seven heavens; grammatical gender and number vary by construction.

senses.definition: A namesake: one who bears the same name.
senses.when: In the Quranic discussion of Yahya, the term denies a prior namesake in the relevant naming relationship, rather than merely denying that anyone anywhere could share a label.

senses.definition: An equal, peer, or counterpart genuinely sharing a name or attribute.
senses.when: In the question concerning God, the term means a counterpart deserving the same name or description in truth, not simply someone who happens to be called by a similar word.

senses.definition: Naming or designating; the act of assigning a name or description.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction, it refers specifically to their assigning a feminine designation to the angels, treating that designation as a claim about their status.

cautions: سَمَاءٌ has both singular and collective/plural Quranic usage; contextual renderings such as “rain from the sky” do not by themselves establish a separate Quranic rain sense.
The Quranic use of سَمِيٌّ concerns a genuine namesake, equal, or counterpart in the relevant name or attribute, not merely anyone sharing a verbal label.
The reported Form VIII pregnancy-testing sense is disputed in the cited Classical evidence.

سوأ.summary: The root centers on ugliness, badness, and what is regarded as foul, harmful, distressing, or disgraceful.
سوأ.development: From perceived ugliness or bad appearance, the lexical field extends to evil conduct, harmful or distressing conditions, misfortune, shameful exposure, and the evil outcome of an act.

senses.definition: To be or become evil, bad, foul, or unseemly; to be an evil course, result, or outcome.
senses.when: Used evaluatively in constructions comparable to بَئْسَ, including expressions in which a course, destination, abode, action, or result is judged evil.

senses.definition: To displease, grieve, vex, or distress someone.
senses.when: Used transitively; passive forms describe someone being distressed or an outward sign of grief or displeasure.

senses.definition: To do evil, act wrongly, or treat someone badly.
senses.when: May be construed with prepositions such as إِلَى, لِ, عَلَى, or بِ; it is the opposite of أَحْسَنَ in conduct.

senses.definition: More or most evil, bad, ugly, or objectionable; worst.
senses.when: Used as an elative adjective in comparison or superlative evaluation.

senses.definition: One who does evil or acts wrongly; an evildoer.
senses.when: Active-participial use of Form IV أَسَاءَ, describing a person characterized by evil conduct.

senses.definition: Evilness or badness, especially evil nature, conduct, or an evil deed.
senses.when: Used as a noun and also attributively in expressions describing a person, action, or quality as evil or displeasing.

cautions: The specialized interpretations of سُوء as possession or madness, leprosy, and Hell-fire are context-bound Quranic readings and should not be generalized to every occurrence of the noun.
Lane's historical Quran citations have not been converted into modern verse locations unless the corresponding QAC occurrence or independently secure Mufradat location is supplied.

سوي.summary: The root centers on straightness, balance, and proper proportion between or within things, yielding the ideas of equality, evenness, symmetry, soundness, and a central or equidistant position.
سوي.development: From this orientation develop the meanings of making something level or well-proportioned, being equal or alike, occupying the middle, becoming upright or settled, and directing oneself toward an intended object.

senses.definition: Be leveled, with the ground made level over or around someone.
senses.when: Used here in the passive Quranic construction describing people being buried or reduced to the level of the earth.

senses.definition: Make equal, even, level, or uniform.
senses.when: Includes making things equal in relation to one another and making a surface or structure level; the Quranic object may be a person, body, land, heaven, or other created thing.

senses.definition: Fashion, proportion, shape, or complete something in a fitting and harmonious form.
senses.when: Used of creation or formation whose parts are made congruent, complete, properly adapted, or soundly ordered.

senses.definition: Make parts uniform or reconstitute them into their proper arrangement.
senses.when: Especially relevant to the Quranic discussion of restoring or equalizing the fingers and reconstructing the body's parts.

senses.definition: Make two things level or equal with one another.
senses.when: Used with two objects or sides brought to the same level, especially by filling or adjusting the space between them.

senses.definition: Become even, upright, firm, settled, or properly established.
senses.when: Used of a thing becoming straight, level, steady, or settled in itself; with عَلَى it can describe becoming firmly seated or established upon something, including boarding or sitting securely.

cautions: The QAC Form I group is retained as authoritative for form accounting, although its Quranic surface تُسَوَّىٰ and the lexical explanation cited for it correspond closely to the passive leveling construction discussed under Form II.

The Form VIII construction اِسْتَوَى عَلَى has several reported interpretive renderings, including becoming established and having ascendancy or mastery; the entry records the lexical construction without imposing a physical interpretation.

Several Lane Quran references use historical citation conventions that do not align mechanically with modern verse numbering; Quran example locations here are taken only from the supplied QAC locations.

سير.summary: The root centers on moving onward, passing along, and flowing.
سير.development: From movement and progression it extends to a way or mode of proceeding, a state or condition, and causative movement. The sense of a thong or stripe is explained through extension and stripe-like form.

senses.definition: To go, move along, travel, proceed, or depart.
senses.when: Used of persons and other moving subjects. With بِـ, it can mean to travel or proceed with someone; Quranic usage includes ordinary travel and movement away.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to go or move; to set in motion, convey, or move away.
senses.when: The Quranic use includes deliberate enabling of travel as well as movement imposed by command, force, or subjugation; passive forms describe things caused to move.

senses.definition: Going, journeying, movement, or progress.
senses.when: A verbal noun referring to the act or course of moving or traveling; Quranic contexts include a journey and a forceful movement.

senses.definition: A traveling company, caravan, or group of travelers.
senses.when: In Quranic usage it denotes a group on the road, not a modern motor vehicle.

senses.definition: The state, condition, or form in which something is; its former or original state.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence, the expression refers to the object's previous condition, rather than to a way of conduct or a biographical narrative.

cautions: سَيَّارَةٌ in the Quranic and Classical evidence means a traveling company or caravan, not the modern noun for an automobile.
سِيرَةٌ has several Classical branches, including conduct and narrative uses; its Quranic occurrence here is specifically the sense of state or condition.
The entry for مُسْتَارٌ preserves a reported lexical alternative between a provision-procuring place and a journey.

سيل.summary: The root denotes flowing and extending, especially the movement of water and other fluids.
سيل.development: Its lexical development includes flowing water, channels through which water runs, causing a substance to flow, abundant flow, and figurative extension or pouring forth. Several specialized nominal and technical uses remain distinct.

senses.definition: To flow or run, especially of water or a watercourse.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction, it is said of valleys as their water flows according to its measure.

senses.definition: To make something flow or run; to cause a liquid or molten substance to flow.
senses.when: Causative Form IV. The Quranic occurrence concerns causing molten copper or brass to flow for Solomon.

senses.definition: A torrent or flood: a large body of rainwater flowing through a valley or watercourse.
senses.when: The Quranic contexts use the noun for a torrent or flood.

cautions: The botanical referent of سَيَالٌ is variously identified in the lexical evidence, including acacia-like and other thorny plants.
The sword-tang sense of سِيلَانٌ is recorded with an explicit qualification that the report was heard but not from a learned authority.
The Quran example for أَسَالَ uses the secure QAC location 34:12; historical citation notation in the lexical evidence is not treated as a modern verse locator.

شبه.summary: A root principle of resemblance and conformity in color, quality, description, or other attributes.
شبه.development: The core notion extends from likeness between things to assimilation and comparison, mutual resemblance, and uncertainty arising when similar things or meanings are difficult to distinguish. A related nominal branch names materials or plants identified by resemblance.

senses.definition: To make someone or something appear to be, or be taken for, another; in the Quranic passive construction, it was made to appear to them as the person they supposed it to be.
senses.when: Quran-attested in the passive form شُبِّهَ, with the identity of the person believed to have been crucified made to appear to the observers.

senses.definition: To resemble one another, become alike, or share a likeness in an attribute or condition.
senses.when: Used mutually of things, persons, qualities, or states; the Quran also applies the construction to hearts sharing error and ignorance.

senses.definition: To become equivocal or difficult to distinguish because of resemblance; to be ambiguous in interpretation.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction ما تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ, the resemblance among meanings or passages makes the intended interpretation unclear or open to differing interpretations.

senses.definition: Resembling one another in a way that makes things difficult to distinguish; similar or liable to be confused.
senses.when: In the Quranic produce context, the resemblance is between the things themselves and may result in confusion or doubt about their identity or properties.

senses.definition: Resembling or conformable in its several parts; similar in appearance, quality, or arrangement.
senses.when: Applied to created things that resemble one another without requiring identity in every property, and to the Quran when its parts correspond in wisdom, rulings, and orderly composition.

senses.definition: Equivocal or ambiguous, especially of Quranic verses whose intended meaning is not immediately determinate.
senses.when: The ambiguity is explained as arising from resemblance to other passages or meanings; interpretation may require reference to clearer verses, repeated consideration, or deeper knowledge.

cautions: The Quranic Form II occurrence is passive شُبِّهَ; the public headword is normalized to the active perfect citation form شَبَّهَ.
Resemblance and ambiguity overlap in some constructions, but the Quranic forms retain their distinct QAC headwords and grammatical patterns.

شدد.summary: A basic sense of القوة في الشيء: strength or force in a thing, especially as made firm by tightening or binding.
شدد.development: The root develops from firm binding and strengthening to force, intensity, severity, contest, hardship, and the attainment of full human strength or maturity.

senses.definition: To make or render firm, strong, sound, or reinforced; to strengthen.
senses.when: Used transitively for strengthening a person, body, support, power, or other established thing.

senses.definition: To bind, tie, or fasten firmly.
senses.when: Used with bonds, restraints, knots, or other things that are tightened or securely fastened.

senses.definition: To make hearts firm against guidance, effectively sealing them from heeding admonition.
senses.when: A Quran-specific construction with على القلوب, as in the prayer شَدَّ على قلوبهم; this is a specialized result of making firm rather than an ordinary physical binding.

senses.definition: To become intensely strong or violent; of the wind, to blow with great force.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence describes the wind becoming violently intense and thereby driving or scattering something.

senses.definition: Strong, powerful, forceful, vigorous, or mighty.
senses.when: May describe a person, power, force, or thing possessing pronounced strength or force.

senses.definition: Severe, intense, harsh, or difficult to bear.
senses.when: Used of punishment, distress, conflict, circumstances, or any attribute whose force or intensity is extreme.

cautions: أَشُدٌّ has a stable core meaning of attained strength or maturity, but the sources give differing age ranges and differing grammatical analyses of its form.
شَدِيدٌ in the expression concerning love of wealth is explicitly interpreted as miserly or withholding, despite contextual English renderings that may emphasize intensity.
أَشَدُّ is used both adjectivally and substantivally in the Quran; its comparative or superlative force is determined by construction and context.

شرك.summary: The root centers on joining or sharing something so that it is not exclusive to one party; a secondary branch denotes extension and linear spread.
شرك.development: The first branch develops into participation, partnership, making someone a partner, and religiously attributing a partner to God. The second develops into road tracks, sandal straps, and hunting snares through the ideas of extension and connected lines.

senses.definition: To share or participate with another; to become a partner or associate in an affair.
senses.when: Takes a person or party as the partner and may be followed by فِي for the affair, property, or matter shared. Quranic usage includes being made a partner in another's affair.

senses.definition: To make someone a partner, associate, or participant in an affair.
senses.when: The person made a partner may be introduced as sharing in an affair, sale, property, or other matter; the Quranic construction وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِي أَمْرِي exemplifies inclusion in an affair.

senses.definition: To attribute a partner or partners to God; to associate another with Him in worship or divine prerogative.
senses.when: This is the Quranic theological construction أَشْرَكَ بِاللَّهِ and includes treating another as sharing God's exclusive divinity. Lexically, unbelief may be described more broadly as a form of this association.

senses.definition: A partner, co-owner, associate, or colleague sharing a thing, affair, right, or dominion.
senses.when: The Quran commonly uses the plural شُرَكَاء for alleged partners of God and for parties treated as sharing authority or possession.

senses.definition: Sharing, participation, partnership; a share or portion in something.
senses.when: The noun can denote participation between parties or an allocated share, including a share in property or an affair.

senses.definition: Religious association: attributing a partner to God or sharing religious devotion or regard with another.
senses.when: In theological usage this includes the great shirk of affirming a partner for God and the more hidden association described as ostentation or hypocrisy in some religious acts.

cautions: Lane's historical Quran citation conventions are not converted into modern verse locations; Quran examples here use only secure QAC-supplied locations.
The wider senses of أَشْرَكَ and مُشْرِك involving unbelief are lexical extensions recorded alongside the primary Quranic sense of associating partners with God.
The masculine, feminine singular, and feminine plural active-participle QAC groups for مُشْرِك are presented under one normalized lexical headword.

شقق.summary: The root centers on cleaving or producing an opening, with extensions to splitting into parts, occupying different sides, distance and hardship, and separation or opposition.
شقق.development: The basic image of an object cleaved or divided yields meanings for a fissure, half or side, a distant tract reached with difficulty, and figurative division or adversarial separation.

senses.definition: to cleave, split, or cut something open
senses.when: Transitive Form I usage; the object may be divided into parts or opened without complete separation.

senses.definition: to make difficult, burden, or distress
senses.when: Used with عَلَى to describe an affair or action as difficult for someone, or to impose a burdensome condition.

senses.definition: to oppose or act adversely toward someone; to take an opposing side
senses.when: A reciprocal or adversarial construction: each party is situated in a side opposed to the other, often with a person, God, or the Messenger as the object of opposition.

senses.definition: to split apart or open into fissures
senses.when: The Form V development describes an object becoming cleft, often with an extended or repeated splitting.

senses.definition: to become split, cleft, or opened apart
senses.when: In Quranic usage, the subject is a heavenly or cosmic body that becomes divided or opened, including the moon and sky.

senses.definition: cleaving or splitting
senses.when: A verbal noun denoting the act of cleaving or splitting, as in the preparation of the earth.

cautions: The Lane match uses contraction of the geminate root شقق to the Lane root شق; the Quranic form identity and counts remain those supplied by QAC.
The Quranic adjective أَشَقّ is presented with its supported comparative difficulty sense; Lane also records separate physical applications of the same adjective for horses.
Two Lane units contain explicitly uncertain or possibly mistranscribed evidence and are retained as ambiguous rather than treated as established meanings.

شمس.summary: A root associated with movement, variation, and lack of settled stability.
شمس.development: The continually moving sun provides the central image; related developments describe sunny or clear conditions and, figuratively, beings or dispositions that resist remaining still, become refractory, or display hostility.

senses.definition: The sun: the solar body or disk, and the light diffused from it.
senses.when: The noun may refer to the celestial solar body or to its radiating light. Quranic occurrences use the ordinary noun across varied grammatical cases and attached particles.

cautions: Classical lexical evidence distinguishes the solar body or disk from the light diffused from it, while the Quranic occurrences are represented under the single noun شَمْسٌ.

شهد.summary: The root centers on presence joined with knowledge and its communication: being present to perceive, knowing what is present, and declaring or establishing it as evidence.
شهد.development: From presence and direct perception develop witnessing, testimony, acknowledgment, authoritative attestation, and the associated nouns for witnesses, testimony, witnessed events, and places of assembly. Some lexical branches retain the notion of presence, while others develop into specialized legal, religious, or technical uses.

senses.definition: To be present at, observe, or witness something; to be there for an event or occasion.
senses.when: Used for presence joined with perception, including attending a time, place, event, or assembly. This sense can overlap with direct observation without implying a subsequent verbal testimony.

senses.definition: To know and declare what one has witnessed or knows; to bear witness, testify, acknowledge, or give decisive information.
senses.when: The verb may take بِ, عَلَى, or occur without a preposition. It includes testimony in legal or argumentative settings, acknowledgment against oneself, and authoritative attestation or declaration; in the divine expression شَهِدَ اللَّهُ, it denotes manifesting, declaring, or establishing the truth.

senses.definition: To make someone witness, present, or aware of something; to call or take someone as a witness.
senses.when: The causative construction can mean making a person observe or know something, causing presence at an event, or formally calling witnesses. It may also have a direct object referring to the matter witnessed.

senses.definition: To ask, require, summon, or call someone to give testimony or serve as a witness.
senses.when: The construction is used for soliciting testimony about an event, person, confession, or legal matter; in legal contexts it may mean calling witnesses or seeking evidential testimony.

senses.definition: A witness: one who has perceived or knows something and can declare or attest to it.
senses.when: The noun may denote an eyewitness, a person who gives testimony, or one who reports decisive knowledge. It is also used for a witness against or in favor of someone.

senses.definition: A person who is present or attending.
senses.when: This use emphasizes personal presence rather than the subsequent act of testimony and may be opposed to being absent.

cautions: شَهِيد and its plural شُهَدَاء have distinct Quranic branches for ordinary witnessing, comprehensive awareness, supporting authority, and martyrdom; context determines the applicable sense.
The plural form group شَهَادَات is accounted for under the singular public headword شَهَادَة; its Quranic occurrences are especially associated with sworn testimony.
The visible/unseen sense of شَهَادَة is a relational theological use and should not be reduced to legal testimony.

شيأ.summary: The root's documented semantic field centers on willing or bringing something about, with شَيْءٌ understood as what may be known, willed, or brought into existence. It also preserves a separate lexical branch for making a face or bodily form ugly.
شيأ.development: The noun شَيْءٌ is analyzed as related to شَاءَ and can thereby denote what is willed or caused to exist, while also functioning as the broadest term for an entity or matter. Independent derived branches concern inciting someone, compelling someone, appeasing anger, and rendering a form unsound or ugly.

senses.definition: To will, wish, desire, or intend something.
senses.when: Used of human or divine willing. The subject, person, number, tense, and voice vary throughout the Quran without creating separate lexical senses.

senses.definition: To will something effectively, determining that it occur or come into existence.
senses.when: Especially in statements concerning God's will, the willing is presented as effectual and connected with the realization of what is willed. Human willing may instead express desire or intention without guaranteeing realization; the lexical tradition also records ordinary overlap with إرادة.

senses.definition: A thing, entity, matter, or anything that can be known or have something predicated of it.
senses.when: A very broad generic noun covering concrete or abstract referents. In Quranic usage it can occur in singular form with a distributive or generic sense, including 'any one or more'; in the expression أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً, the thing is construed as the bearer of the stated predicate. The extension of the term to nonexistent objects is a recorded but disputed theoretical analysis.

senses.definition: What is willed, intended, brought into being, or caused to exist; a willed or created thing.
senses.when: The noun may function as a verbal noun in the sense of a passive participle, especially in Quranic statements about universal creation or what is brought into existence. This use presents the referent as the object or result of willing or making, without restricting it to a previously existing material object.

cautions: The effective-will sense is especially associated with divine willing; human willing may denote desire or intention without implying realization, and the evidence records theological disagreement about how مشيئة relates to إرادة.
The noun's extension to nonexistent objects is reported as a disputed theoretical analysis, not an unqualified Quranic definition.
The reported water sense is attributed to Lth but rejected or not recognized by AM; it is retained only as a qualified Classical report.

صبر.summary: The root centers on holding back or restraining, especially restraining oneself from impatience; it also has distinct branches involving upper edges and hard or collected stone.
صبر.development: The lexical development extends from self-restraint and confinement to things held together, heaped, or made firm, while a separate branch denotes the upper or edge portions of things and stones or stony ground.

senses.definition: To restrain oneself from impatience and endure hardship with patience; to remain steadfast.
senses.when: Used for enduring affliction, resisting desire, remaining firm in obedience, and withholding complaint. It may be intransitive, or occur with the self understood or with عَلَى or عَنْ.

senses.definition: To wait patiently for an appointed outcome or judgment.
senses.when: A Quranic use of patient endurance with an expected ruling or outcome, as in صَبْرٌ لِحُكْمٍ; it is more than mere passive delay.

senses.definition: In the exclamatory construction ما أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ: to be astonishingly bold or heedless in exposing oneself to the Fire.
senses.when: This Quranic construction presents the people addressed as extraordinarily bold to undertake the deeds leading to the Fire, rather than simply praising their patience.

senses.definition: To vie with one another in patience or endurance; to mutually hold firm in trial.
senses.when: In وَصَابِرُوا, the construction conveys active competition or mutual outlasting in patience, conventionally presented as a stronger progression than merely enduring oneself.

senses.definition: To labor to maintain patience; to persevere steadfastly.
senses.when: The Quranic construction اِصْطَبِرْ لِعِبَادَتِهِ emphasizes sustained, effortful perseverance in worship or another demanding course.

senses.definition: One who is patient, enduring, and steadfast.
senses.when: An active-participial epithet for a person who restrains the self and remains firm through affliction, obedience, struggle, or deprivation; the Quran applies the form to masculine and feminine groups as well as individuals.

cautions: The QAC Form I grouping includes the exclamatory occurrence ما أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ; it is represented separately from ordinary patience because its Quranic interpretation is boldness or heedlessness.
Several rare classical branches are explicitly qualified in the evidence, especially the reported myrrh sense, the solitary-man sense, and the uncertain collected-flesh report.

صحب.summary: The root centers on the juxtaposition, proximity, and sustained association of one thing with another.
صحب.development: From proximity and companionship develop meanings of accompanying, making something a companion, adhering to or carrying something along, becoming tractable through association, and designating a companion, possessor, or associated group.

senses.definition: To protect, defend, or keep safe.
senses.when: Quranically attested in the passive construction يُصْحَبُونَ, describing people who receive no protection or safeguarding from others.

senses.definition: To accompany, associate with, or keep company with.
senses.when: The construction denotes sustained companionship or association rather than a merely momentary meeting; it may be used with a person or group.

senses.definition: Companions, associates, or people associated with a person, place, event, or thing.
senses.when: The plural frequently forms names for groups linked to a particular person, location, episode, or distinguishing circumstance; context may render it as the people or inhabitants of that association.

senses.definition: Occupants or inmates of a place or state.
senses.when: In expressions such as أصحاب الجنة and أصحاب النار, the noun denotes those who inhabit or belong to Paradise or the Fire, rather than ordinary companions.

senses.definition: Appointed keepers or custodians.
senses.when: In أصحاب النار in the construction cited for 74:31, the referents are those entrusted with the Fire, not its punished inmates.

senses.definition: A companion, associate, fellow, or close companion.
senses.when: The noun normally denotes a person characterized by sustained association; it can also be used for an associated person in relation to an animal, place, time, or circumstance.

cautions: The Form I Quran occurrence is represented specifically in the protective or defensive construction يُصْحَبُونَ; this does not generalize the protective sense to every ordinary use of the root.
صَاحِب and أَصْحَاب vary between interpersonal companionship, named association, occupancy, and custodianship according to their construction and Quranic context.

صدد.summary: The root centrally expresses turning aside or away: a movement toward one side that can extend to diverting another from a course.
صدد.development: From this orientation arise meanings of avoidance, prevention, lateral position, facing or proximity, and directed attention. Separate lexical branches include clamour or laughter and the blood-mixed purulent fluid called صَدِيد.

senses.definition: To turn away from, avoid, shun, or be averse to something or someone.
senses.when: Intransitive or used with عَنْ; includes turning the face away and refusing or abstaining from the object.

senses.definition: To turn someone away or back; to divert, prevent, or hinder someone from doing something or reaching a course.
senses.when: Transitive construction with عَنْ; the object may be a person, an action, or a path. Passive usage means to be turned away or hindered.

senses.definition: To cry out, vociferate, or raise a clamour.
senses.when: A distinct vocalization is reported for صَدَّ يَصِدُّ; the Quranic occurrence at 43:57 has this lexical possibility alongside the laughter interpretation.

senses.definition: To laugh violently, loudly, or immoderately.
senses.when: A distinct lexical use reported for the same present-tense vocalization; the supplied contextual rendering of 43:57 reflects this interpretation.

senses.definition: To cause someone to be turned away or hindered; in the passive, to be turned away or hindered.
senses.when: The supplied Quranic occurrence is passive. The derived Form II headword is connected lexically with the Form I turning-away and prevention construction.

senses.definition: To clap the hands or raise a clamour.
senses.when: Attested in the Quranic derived-noun construction تَصْدِيَةً; this Quranic construction is distinct from the supplied passive occurrence at 13:33.

cautions: The occurrence at 43:57 is supplied with the contextual gloss “laughed aloud,” while the lexical evidence also records cry or clamour for the same vocalization; both materially distinct readings are retained without treating the contextual gloss as the sole lexical definition.

The Quranic Form II clapping evidence concerns the derived noun تَصْدِيَةً in the cited Quranic expression, whereas the supplied QAC Form II occurrence is the passive verb at 13:33; no unsupplied verse location is used as an example.
A historical citation attached to the صَدِيد discussion is not converted into a modern surah:ayah location; the displayed Quran example uses only the independently supplied QAC location 14:16.

صعق.summary: A forceful striking sound or impact, especially a violent atmospheric thunderclap, with effects that include stunning, death, and destruction.
صعق.development: The root develops from vehement sound and impact to the thunderbolt, the stunned state it produces, and fatal or destructive consequences. These effects remain conceptually connected, though particular derived forms lexicalize them differently.

senses.definition: To swoon, become insensible, or lose awareness under the effect of a vehement sound or overwhelming strike.
senses.when: The Quranic passive occurrence describes people being made to faint or become insensible; the lexical construction can involve being struck by a thunderbolt.

senses.definition: To die or fall dead, as overcome by a devastating sound or strike.
senses.when: In the interpretation of 39:68, the verb is understood as dying or falling dead; related interpretations include falling into a swoon or losing reason.

senses.definition: A violent atmospheric thunderclap or thunderbolt: a powerful strike from the sky accompanied by overwhelming sound.
senses.when: This denotes the atmospheric event or strike itself, including the singular and plural Quranic forms.

senses.definition: The fire or lightning discharge issuing from a violent thunderbolt.
senses.when: This sense emphasizes the fiery or lightning-bearing effect of the atmospheric phenomenon rather than the sound alone.

senses.definition: A destructive punitive visitation, including a fatal visitation or death caused by it.
senses.when: The word may name the destructive effect of the thunderbolt as punishment, especially when the result is death, rather than only the physical atmospheric event.

senses.definition: Unconscious, stunned, or deprived of ordinary awareness.
senses.when: The Quranic nominal use describes a person rendered insensible; it is an adjective-like form used substantivally in the supplied morphology.

cautions: The verb in 39:68 has an explicitly reported interpretive range: death, falling dead, swooning, or loss of reason; the related Quranic senses preserve this distinction rather than forcing one English equivalent.

The Quran-focused discussion treats the thunderbolt, its fire, and its punitive or fatal effects as connected aspects of one phenomenon; they are separated here only where the lexical use highlights a different function or result.

صلح.summary: A root expressing soundness, rightness, and the opposite of فساد, corruption or disorder.
صلح.development: The root develops from being sound or right to making something sound, restoring order, and removing estrangement between people.

senses.definition: To be or become sound, right, or righteous; to come into a proper state.
senses.when: In the Quran, used of persons who are or have become righteous.

senses.definition: To set right, reform, restore, or improve a person, thing, affair, or condition.
senses.when: Includes correcting or restoring something to a sound state, including reforming one's own conduct or affairs.

senses.definition: To reconcile parties, make peace, or restore accord between them.
senses.when: Used for removing estrangement and repairing relations between people or groups.

senses.definition: Setting right, reforming, restoring, or improving.
senses.when: The verbal noun of أَصْلَحَ in its general sense of bringing a person, affair, or condition into a sound state.

senses.definition: Reconciliation or conciliation between people.
senses.when: Used specifically for removing discord or restoring agreement between parties.

senses.definition: Righteous or morally good; in substantivized use, a righteous person or a good or righteous act.
senses.when: Applied in the Quran to morally upright persons and to good or righteous acts. The feminine plural صالحات is commonly substantivized for righteous deeds.

cautions: The identical spelling صَالِح can be the active participle/adjective or the proper name Ṣāliḥ; QAC treats these as separate lexical groups.
The Quranic plural صالحات is presented under the singular active-participle citation form صَالِح.
The Quranic senses are restricted to usages supported by the supplied lexical evidence; additional Classical branches are listed separately.

صلو.summary: The supplied evidence centers this root's Quranic lexical field on prayer, supplication, blessing, places of prayer, and those who pray.
صلو.development: The packet supplies no matched Maqāyīs entry. Lane records additional, distinct branches involving the rear or back, striking, racing, and related derived formations; these are preserved separately rather than collapsed into the Quranic prayer vocabulary.

senses.definition: To perform the prescribed prayer.
senses.when: Used for the religious act of prayer; grammatical aspect and person vary across the Quranic forms.

senses.definition: To pray or supplicate for someone; to invoke good, forgiveness, or commendation on their behalf.
senses.when: Commonly occurs with عَلَى naming the person for whom the prayer is made. The construction may be used of a human or an angelic subject.

senses.definition: To bless, confer blessing, show mercy, or magnify and honor.
senses.when: With God as subject, the construction denotes the conferral of blessing, mercy, honor, or magnification; with angels or people, it denotes invoking such blessing, especially in the Quranic expression concerning the Prophet.

senses.definition: Prayer, supplication, or petition, including prayer made on behalf of another.
senses.when: This is the broader nominal sense from which more specialized religious uses develop; the Quran also uses it in expressions of prayer or blessing for persons.

senses.definition: The prescribed religious prayer or service.
senses.when: A conventional religious act comprising prayer and, in its fully specified form, bowing and prostration; the Quran frequently presents it as an established practice to be performed or maintained.

senses.definition: Blessing, mercy, commendation, or divine favor.
senses.when: With God as the source, it denotes blessing, mercy, commendation, or magnification; in human usage it may denote an invocation of blessing. The Quranic plural can refer to blessings from God or to blessings invoked by people.

cautions: The supplied Mufradāt row is shared ambiguously between Slw and Sly. Only its passages explicitly discussing صلاة, blessings, and prescribed prayer were used; its fire and roasting material was not assigned to this root.

Lane uses historical Quran citation conventions. Its reference to the plural صلوات is not converted mechanically into a modern location; the modern example 22:40 comes independently from the supplied QAC occurrence.
No matched Maqāyīs entry was supplied, so the root-level development statement is limited and does not treat a reconstructed root principle as a direct Quranic sense.

صنع.summary: The root centers on making or bringing something into a formed state, especially through effective or skilled workmanship.
صنع.development: From making with skill, the lexical field extends to craft, careful tending and cultivation, constructed works, and specialized derived uses such as reciprocal inducement and bribery. Some nominal branches designate manufactured objects, occupations, or built installations.

senses.definition: To make, fashion, construct, or perform something through deliberate and effective workmanship.
senses.when: Used both for producing or constructing things and for carrying out deeds or acts; the passive construction in 20:39 has a specialized sense of being reared or cultivated, listed separately.

senses.definition: To rear, nourish, educate, or cultivate someone with sustained care and attention.
senses.when: Especially supported in the construction وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَى عَيْنِي, where the passive verb expresses being brought up under close supervision; the evidence does not restrict the construction to a particular gender or age.

senses.definition: To specially choose or select someone for a designated purpose or office.
senses.when: In وَاصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِي, the choice is presented as a special divine selection for a required mission.

senses.definition: To cultivate, rear, or prepare someone with exceptional care for a designated purpose.
senses.when: The same Quranic construction is also interpreted as special rearing and preparation; this is more than ordinary making or selection.

senses.definition: Craft, handiwork, workmanship, or the making of a manufactured object.
senses.when: The Quran occurrence refers to the making or workmanship of protective armor; the lexical meaning is the craft or manufacture, not armor as a general semantic restriction.

senses.definition: Skilled making, workmanship, or a work produced through effective and well-executed action.
senses.when: The Quran uses the noun for works or efforts and for God's perfectly executed making; it denotes a skilled act or its result rather than every undifferentiated فعل.

cautions: The Form VIII Quranic expression وَاصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِي supports both special selection and exceptional rearing or preparation; the artifact preserves both readings as distinct but closely related senses.

مَصَانِعُ in 26:129 is a context-sensitive plural: the Quranic evidence supports substantial constructed places or strongholds, while broader Classical Arabic evidence also records reservoirs, wells, towns, and horse compounds.
The report that صَنِعَ means 'to become skilled' is attributed to one authority and rejected by another; it is retained as a qualified Classical meaning rather than treated as a Quranic sense.

صنو.summary: The root centers on close relation or common origin between separate things.
صنو.development: Its central image is multiple trees or shoots emerging from one root; this extends to kinship and physical proximity, while a divergent lexical branch denotes a ground depression or water-hole.

senses.definition: One of multiple tree-shoots or trees issuing from a single root; in the Quran, a palm tree growing together with others from one root.
senses.when: The singular names each member in relation to its companions; the Quranic plural صِنْوَانٌ is contrasted with trees having separate roots.

cautions: Lane records dialectal vocalic variants of صِنْوٌ and variant plural forms; the public Quranic headword uses the supported singular citation form.
The صُنَيٌّ entry preserves alternative reported interpretations rather than resolving them into a single physical referent.

صوب.summary: A root oriented toward descent, arrival, and settling in the proper place or state.
صوب.development: From something descending and settling come the related notions of rain falling, an arrow reaching its mark, an event befalling someone, and correctness as arriving at what is right. The noun مُصِيبَةٌ developed toward the specialized sense of an affliction or calamity.

senses.definition: To reach, strike, or befall a person or thing; to take effect upon it, including by afflicting it or bringing a benefit to it.
senses.when: The Quran uses the active Form IV verb for events, harms, benefits, rain, and other effects that reach or take effect upon an object. English renderings therefore include “strike,” “befall,” “afflict,” and, in beneficial contexts, “bestow.”

senses.definition: To go or proceed wherever one intends or wishes.
senses.when: This distinct directional-volitional use is attested in the Quranic expression describing movement wherever the agent desires; it is not merely the sense of suffering an event or reaching a target.

senses.definition: What is right or correct; a right or correct saying, judgment, or action.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence refers specifically to a correct utterance, while the lexical term also applies to correctness in conduct, judgment, and other matters.

senses.definition: Rain-bearing cloud or pouring rain; a rainstorm.
senses.when: In the Quranic simile, the term is explained both as a cloud possessing rain and as the rain itself; the lexical evidence does not require choosing only one of these readings.

senses.definition: Striking, reaching, or befalling; one that hits or takes effect upon someone or something.
senses.when: This is the active participle of أَصَابَ and occurs in the Quran with an understood or expressed object that is to be struck or affected.

senses.definition: An affliction, calamity, misfortune, disaster, or other evil accident that befalls someone.
senses.when: In Quranic usage, the noun is specialized for a harmful event or adversity, whether portrayed as striking people or as occurring through what they have done.

cautions: صَيِّبٌ has an explicitly reported Quranic interpretive range: it may denote the rain-bearing cloud or the rain itself.
The Quranic intent example for أَصَابَ is anchored to the independently supplied QAC occurrence 38:36:8; no modern verse location is inferred from Lane's historical citation notation.
مُصِيبَةٌ is a Quranic noun for calamity, while the older arrow-shot association is kept separately as a classical lexical meaning.

ضرب.summary: The root centers on causing one thing to fall upon, affect, or be applied to another; its uses extend from striking to travel, imprinting, comparison, imposition, and related forms of impact or movement.
ضرب.development: The basic notion of striking or making an impact is extended metaphorically to journeying across the earth, laying or imposing something over another, producing an impression or likeness, and setting forth a parable or way.

senses.definition: to strike, hit, beat, or smite; to inflict a blow or physical impact
senses.when: Includes active and passive constructions, striking with a hand, weapon, or other object, and striking a bodily part; in context it can extend to smiting or killing.

senses.definition: to travel, go forth, or journey through the land
senses.when: Used with فِي الأَرْضِ and related constructions for going about or journeying, including travel for a purpose such as seeking provision.

senses.definition: to set forth, present, compare, or propound a parable, example, or similitude
senses.when: Used with مَثَلًا and related objects; the construction may present a case as an illustrative comparison or make something the subject of a parable.

senses.definition: to lay, cast, impose, or set something over or upon another; hence to cover, enclose, or establish a barrier
senses.when: Includes imposing a condition, laying a covering or veil over something, causing sleep by covering the ears, and setting a separating wall or barrier between parties.

senses.definition: to assign, make, or open a way or route
senses.when: Used in the construction ضرب طريقًا, including making a route through or across a place such as the sea.

senses.definition: to turn away, dismiss, or withhold from a person, matter, or subject
senses.when: The construction ضرب عن can mean turning away from or neglecting something; in discourse it can indicate digression or withdrawal from a subject.

cautions: The Quranic verb group contains active and passive forms and several construction-specific extensions; these are grouped by lexical relation rather than by grammatical voice.
The nominal ضَرْبٌ is presented as a verbal noun even though QAC tags its occurrences as nouns.
Lane's Quran citation conventions are retained only through independently secure QAC locations; no historical Lane citation has been converted into a modern location.

ضرر.summary: The root centers on harm or detriment, contrasted with benefit, and extends to states of adversity, constraint, and impairment.
ضرر.development: The lexical tradition also connects the root with gathered or accumulated parts and with strength or endurance; from adversity and straitness developed the sense of being compelled by necessity, while related formations describe co-wives, bodily masses, wealth, and persistent vigor.

senses.definition: To harm, injure, damage, or cause detriment to someone or something.
senses.when: A transitive use; Quranic contexts contrast causing harm with benefit and may express inability to harm another independently.

senses.definition: To harm or be harmed through reciprocal or adversarial dealings; to inflict injury on one another.
senses.when: The Quranic forms occur in constructions that can be read actively or passively: causing harm, being subjected to harm, or making someone suffer through a harmful interaction.

senses.definition: To compel, constrain, or drive someone to something, especially against the will and through necessity; to be compelled or forced to resort to or do something.
senses.when: The construction may be transitive or intransitive. Compulsion can arise from an external force or threat, or from an internal necessity such as life-threatening hunger.

senses.definition: One who harms; harmful or injurious.
senses.when: An active-participial description of a person or agent as capable of causing harm; Quranic contexts deny that such agents can independently harm others.

senses.definition: Harm, detriment, or a damaging effect.
senses.when: A noun contrasted with benefit; Quranic uses may express the capacity or result of causing harm rather than an adverse condition as such.

senses.definition: Hardship, distress, adversity, or a hurtful condition.
senses.when: A condition of adversity contrasted with prosperity or ease; it can concern a person's circumstances, livelihood, or bodily state.

cautions: The Quranic Form III verb is morphologically supplied as passive in QAC, while the lexical discussion records active and passive readings; the sense therefore states both reciprocal harming and being subjected to harm.

The Quranic form ضَرَر is defined from direct lexical evidence as detriment, deficiency, impairment, or loss; the supplied contextual rendering “the disabled” illustrates its Quranic construction but is not used alone to establish an additional sense.
Lane's cited Quran references in its discussion were not converted into modern verse locations unless independently supplied by QAC.

ضلل.summary: The root centers on losing, missing, or departing from the proper course, whether literally, intellectually, morally, or in the outcome of an action.
ضلل.development: From loss of a way or object, the meanings extend to error and straying, disappearance or concealment, perishing and annulment, and causatively to leading another into error.

senses.definition: To go astray, deviate from what is right, or miss the proper way.
senses.when: Used both intransitively and with a way or course understood; the Qur'an applies it to error, deviation, and loss of right direction.

senses.definition: To become lost, perish, or come to nothing.
senses.when: Includes the loss or annulment of an undertaking and, in the Qur'anic expression concerning the body, becoming dust and bones.

senses.definition: To be absent from awareness or memory; to forget or be unmindful.
senses.when: In Qur'anic constructions this includes a lapse of memory and the statement that nothing escapes or is forgotten by the Lord.

senses.definition: To cause someone to go astray, mislead, or turn away from right guidance.
senses.when: The causative may describe human or satanic misleading and divine letting or causing someone to remain in straying; the latter is presented in the Qur'anic discussion as connected with the person's prior course or disposition.

senses.definition: To cause something to perish, be lost, or become without effect.
senses.when: Used of works, plots, and other outcomes that are rendered futile, unrecognized, or unrecompensed, as well as of causing a person or thing to be lost.

senses.definition: More astray, farther from the right course, or most astray.
senses.when: A comparative or superlative evaluation of distance from right guidance; the degree of straying varies with the comparison and context.

cautions: The QAC nominal أَضَلُّ is presented as a comparative adjective and is not merged with the Form IV verb أَضَلَّ.
The active participle ضَالّ has a Qur'anic use for a state of not yet being guided or of inadvertence; this should not automatically be equated with culpable doctrinal error.
Lane's historical Quran citation notation was used only as lexical evidence; modern verse locations in examples are taken from independently supplied QAC occurrences.

طرف.summary: The root centers on an edge, extremity, or boundary, and on movement of the eyelids in looking.
طرف.development: The edge sense extends to sides, portions, and the ends of periods; eyelid movement gives rise to the meanings eye, glance, and gaze. Related developments include selecting or acquiring something new, as though taking from an outer or newly reached portion.

senses.definition: An extremity, end, side, region, or portion of something.
senses.when: Used of material things and of periods of time: أَطْرَافُ النَّهَارِ and طَرَفَا النَّهَارِ refer to the ends or portions of the day, while أَطْرَافُ الأَرْضِ refers to its borders, sides, or districts. In the Quranic expression about reducing the land from its edges, the phrase has also been interpreted figuratively as reducing its inhabitants, produce, or learned and notable people.

senses.definition: A look, glance, or gaze; the act of looking.
senses.when: The word can denote the movement of the eyelids in looking and, by association, the resulting glance or gaze. It includes a look that returns or is withdrawn and a restrained or lowered gaze.

senses.definition: The eye or eyes, viewed as the organ or faculty of sight.
senses.when: The eye sense is a substantive development from the eyelid movement associated with looking; in Quranic usage the plural or collective sense can refer to eyes or their gaze.

cautions: The Quranic occurrences of طَرْف and طَرَف represent overlapping eye/gaze and edge/portion branches; translations such as “eye,” “gaze,” “glance,” “ends,” and “borders” reflect construction and context.
The interpretation of أَطْرَافِ الأَرْضِ in the Quran varies between physical borders or districts and figurative reduction of inhabitants, produce, or learned people.
Several Classical Arabic entries preserve variant authorities or disputed readings, especially lineage adjectives, poetic descriptions, and the idiomatic uses of مَطْرُوفَة.

طمع.summary: A strong inward hope or desire directed toward a thing.
طمع.development: The root develops from powerful expectation and longing into eager coveting, hoping for an outcome, and related causative, adjectival, and object-noun formations.

senses.definition: To desire, long for, or covet something eagerly.
senses.when: Describes a strong inclination toward a desired thing. The emphasis may fall on eager wanting rather than on the expectation that the thing will actually be obtained.

senses.definition: To hope for or expect a desired outcome.
senses.when: Commonly used with a following event or goal, including constructions with أَنْ. It can refer to an outcome regarded as relatively near or possible, though that is not an absolute restriction.

senses.definition: To lust after or be moved by sexual desire.
senses.when: A context-specific use of eager desire. In the Quranic construction involving speech that may awaken desire, the sense is sexual, but the lexical construction itself is described neutrally and is not restricted to a particular gender or object class.

senses.definition: Hope or eager desire for a desired outcome.
senses.when: An abstract noun describing hopeful longing, especially when paired with fear or used of an anticipated benefit, relief, or fulfillment.

cautions: The Quranic verb group consists of imperfect active Form I occurrences; the public headword is normalized to the classical perfect citation form طَمِعَ.

Hope, eager desire, and coveting overlap semantically, but context determines whether expectation or strong wanting is foregrounded. The sexual sense is specifically contextual and should not be projected onto every occurrence.

طوع.summary: The root centers on yielding, accompanying another, and complying with a will or direction.
طوع.development: From the basic idea of submission and compliance develop obedience, voluntary undertaking, mutual accommodation, and the ability or practical feasibility to carry something out. The Form X verb is explained as historically related to an original form meaning the acquisition of capacity.

senses.definition: To be obeyed; to have one's command or will complied with.
senses.when: The supplied Quran occurrences are passive imperfect forms and describe a person whose direction is obeyed or an intercessor whose word is heeded.

senses.definition: To make an act acceptable or easy to oneself; to induce, prompt, or encourage oneself to undertake it.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction with the soul or mind, the verb describes inward yielding that facilitates or prompts the contemplated act, rather than ordinary obedience to a command.

senses.definition: To obey; to comply with another's command, direction, or will.
senses.when: The Quran uses this verb for carrying out the direction of God, the Messenger, a prophet, or another person; it may also describe compliance with a desired course of action.

senses.definition: To undertake a good act voluntarily, especially an act not made obligatory.
senses.when: The Quranic usage concerns voluntary or supererogatory good; the form conveys willing self-commitment rather than merely being commanded to act.

senses.definition: To be able or capable of doing, accomplishing, obtaining, or possessing something; to have the practical means for it.
senses.when: The verb commonly concerns practical feasibility rather than unrestricted power. The lexical discussion associates it with the agent's constitution and conception of the act, the suitability of what is acted upon, and an instrument when one is required.

senses.definition: To consent to, comply with, or answer a request.
senses.when: This is an explicitly reported interpretation of the Quranic question about sending down a table from heaven in 5:112; it is distinct from the ordinary capacity sense and should not be generalized to every occurrence.

cautions: The Form I public headword is normalized to طَاعَ although the supplied Quran occurrences are passive imperfect forms يُطَاعُ and يُطَاعَ.

The Form X usage in 5:112 has explicitly reported competing interpretations: ordinary ability, seeking or receiving consent, and answering a request. The latter is recorded as a distinct but restricted Quranic sense.
The Quranic form مُطَّوِّعِين is presented under the singular dictionary citation form مُتَطَوِّع; the doubled طاء reflects assimilation in the Quranic form.

طيب.summary: The root denotes what is good, pleasant, pure, wholesome, or otherwise the opposite of khabīth (bad or impure).
طيب.development: Its central orientation extends from sensory and inward pleasantness to purity, lawful and wholesome provision, morally sound persons and deeds, good speech, favorable conditions, and blessed outcome.

senses.definition: To be or become good, pleasant, pure, or wholesome; to be in a favorable state.
senses.when: Used of persons or states, including the expression طِبْتُمْ in the welcome to the inhabitants of Paradise.

senses.definition: To be agreeable, acceptable, suitable, or lawful to someone.
senses.when: Especially in the construction طَابَ لِـ, where what is agreeable or legally available to a person is intended.

senses.definition: To become willing, content, or free in mind to relinquish, remit, or grant something.
senses.when: The construction طَابَتْ نَفْسُهُ بِـ or طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ expresses willing concession without compulsion.

senses.definition: Good, pleasant, agreeable to the senses, wholesome, pure, or clean.
senses.when: Used of food, drink, water, ground, land, and other things whose qualities are pleasant or free from impurity.

senses.definition: Lawful, permitted, legitimate, or soundly acquired.
senses.when: In Quranic contrasts with khabīth, this may describe lawful property, provision, deeds, or other things accepted as legally proper.

senses.definition: Morally or spiritually good and pure; commendable in persons, deeds, or speech.
senses.when: This substantivized or attributive use can refer to good persons, good works, and good words, without reducing the sense to physical cleanliness.

cautions: The public طَيِّبَةٌ entry combines the feminine singular adjective with its Quranic plural طَيِّبَات; occurrence_count therefore aggregates both supplied QAC groups.
طُوبَىٰ has both an abstract interpretation of blessedness or good outcome and reported concrete interpretations referring to the tree of Paradise or Paradise itself.

ظلل.summary: The root centers on one thing covering, screening, or protecting another, especially through shade.
ظلل.development: From physical shade and covering, the lexicon develops meanings of protection, shelter, security, ease, and the daytime continuation or persistence expressed by ظَلَّ.

senses.definition: To remain or continue in a state or activity; to pass the daytime doing something.
senses.when: An incomplete verb whose original temporal association is with the daytime; Quranic usage also expresses persistence or continuation without making the daytime meaning prominent.

senses.definition: To become or turn into a state.
senses.when: Used as an incomplete verb with a predicate describing the resulting state; this is distinct from merely continuing in an already established state.

senses.definition: To shade someone or something; to cause a covering or shade to extend over it.
senses.when: A causative/transitive construction, including placing someone under the shade of clouds or another covering.

senses.definition: Providing abundant, dense, extensive, or lasting shade.
senses.when: The adjective may describe shade that is constant or extensive; in Quranic usage, the image can also imply protection from heat and pleasant ease of life, without requiring a separate lexical meaning.

senses.definition: Shade or shadow: the area or covering screened from the sun, and by extension anything that shades or covers.
senses.when: The Quran uses the noun for ordinary shade and shadow as well as for shade associated with Paradise, clouds, trees, or other coverings. Classical distinctions between ظِلّ and فَيْء vary by time of day.

senses.definition: Figuratively, protection, security, power of resistance, or a life of ease and plenty.
senses.when: A figurative extension of shade as shelter and defense; Quranic interpretation applies it especially to divine protection, honor, security, and paradisal well-being.

cautions: Classical authorities distinguish ظِلّ and فَيْء differently with respect to time of day; the physical sense is therefore stated broadly rather than imposing one timing rule.
Some Quranic shade passages are interpreted physically and others figuratively as protection, power, or ease; both readings are represented where the lexical evidence explicitly supports them.

ظلم.summary: The root has two closely related semantic orientations: darkness or the absence of light, and placing something outside its proper position or due.
ظلم.development: From the latter orientation developed the meanings of transgression, injustice, deprivation, and wrongful treatment; from the former developed darkness and figurative darkness such as ignorance, unbelief, and unrighteousness.

senses.definition: To wrong, act unjustly, injure, or transgress against someone or something.
senses.when: Used intransitively for acting wrongfully and transitively for wronging another; Quranic usage also includes wrongdoing against God, other people, or oneself.

senses.definition: To deprive, despoil, or cause loss of a due or right.
senses.when: Includes causing someone to suffer loss; in the Quran, the verb can deny that God deprives anyone of even the smallest due.

senses.definition: To reject or disbelieve signs, thereby treating them wrongfully.
senses.when: A Quran-attested construction with بِ; the object may be understood as the signs or as those wronged because of them.

senses.definition: To become dark or enter into darkness.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence the verb is used of darkness coming upon or surrounding them; its transitivity is discussed in the classical evidence.

senses.definition: More or most wrongful, unjust, or transgressive.
senses.when: A comparative or superlative adjective used to identify the graver instance of wrongdoing or the more unjust claimant or act.

senses.definition: One who wrongs, acts unjustly, injures, or transgresses; a wrongdoer.
senses.when: The active participle functions adjectivally or substantivally and is used for wrongdoing against God, people, or oneself; gender and case forms are included under this headword.

cautions: The Quranic material distinguishes physical darkness from figurative darkness; the latter is especially associated with ignorance, unbelief, polytheism, and unrighteousness.
The intensity implied by ظَلُوم and ظَلَّام is lexical, although contextual translations may render both simply as “unjust.”
The classical evidence records disagreement over whether أَظْلَمَ may be transitive as well as intransitive; the Quranic example is represented without resolving that broader grammatical issue.

ظهر.summary: The root centers on emergence into view and strength expressed through the back: what becomes outward, elevated, dominant, or relied upon.
ظهر.development: The semantic field develops from the human back as the outward and supporting side. From this arise meanings of appearing, becoming manifest, rising above or overcoming, supporting another, carrying burdens, and putting something behind one's back.

senses.definition: To emerge into visibility or become apparent, manifest, or prevalent.
senses.when: Used for something becoming perceptible after being hidden; with a condition such as فساد, it can mean becoming widespread or manifest.

senses.definition: To prevail over, overcome, or gain mastery of someone or something.
senses.when: Commonly construed with عَلَى; the object may be an opponent, a thing to be overcome, or a structure to be surmounted.

senses.definition: To come to know, become acquainted with, or gain awareness of something.
senses.when: Especially with عَلَى; in the Quran this includes attaining awareness of private matters and discovering or recognizing people.

senses.definition: To mount, climb onto, or get upon the top or back of something.
senses.when: Used with a physical object such as a wall, mountain, or other elevated structure.

senses.definition: To aid, assist, support, or back someone, including by aiding one side against another.
senses.when: The reciprocal or opposing-party construction can express support for one another or support against an adversary.

senses.definition: To pronounce the formula of ẓihār: to declare one's wife to be to oneself like the back of one's mother, thereby treating marital relations as forbidden.
senses.when: A conventional pre-Islamic repudiation formula, Quranically discussed in the construction ظَاهَرَ مِنِ امْرَأَتِهِ and its variant readings.

cautions: With عَلَى, Form I ظَهَرَ can mean becoming acquainted with, prevailing over, or mounting/surmounting; the object and construction determine the sense.

Some Quranic translations of the appearance and predominance senses overlap; the artifact keeps causative manifestation, dominance, and temporal noon uses distinct where the lexical evidence supports them.
The Form VI verb also has an attested Classical Arabic contrary use meaning to turn one's back on one another; that specialization is kept outside the Quranic mutual-support sense.

عبد.summary: The root has two attested semantic axes: yieldingness, humility, and servitude on the one hand, and strength or hardness on the other.
عبد.development: The first axis develops from the status of a slave or subject into worship, humble obedience, devotion, enslavement, and the making of things tractable or well-trodden. The second axis yields strength, solidity, anger, and disdain-related usages.

senses.definition: To worship, serve, or adore a deity, especially through humble and submissive obedience.
senses.when: Used in the Quran with God, false gods, or the Devil as object. The active, imperative, imperfect, perfect, and passive forms are grammatical variants of this lexical use; the passive means “be worshipped.”

senses.definition: In an alternate Quranic reading, to become an object of worship.
senses.when: This is an explicitly reported alternative interpretation of a Quranic expression; the cited historical Lane reference is not converted here into a modern verse location.

senses.definition: To enslave someone or make someone as a slave; to bring someone under servile submission.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence refers to enslaving or subjugating people. The causative force includes reducing someone to the condition or work of a slave.

senses.definition: A worshipper, devotee, or one who serves a deity with devotion.
senses.when: The Quran includes masculine and feminine forms. The object may be God or, by secondary application, an idol or other deity; the feminine form عَابِدَات is included here.

senses.definition: One who rejects, disdains, or angrily repudiates a claim.
senses.when: This is a reported interpretation of the Quranic expression in which العابدين is variously explained as worshippers, angry rejecters, scorners, or deniers. The interpretive alternatives are not treated as a settled restriction on the ordinary participle.

senses.definition: A slave or bondman; a person in a legally enslaved condition.
senses.when: The Quranic legal usage includes the contrast between a slave and a free person. In the evidence, عَبِيد is associated with owned slaves, while عِبَاد commonly denotes servants or worshippers; عَبِيد with a divine genitive can nevertheless be broader.

cautions: The alternate interpretation of عَبُدَ الطَّاغُوتِ is retained as Quran-focused evidence, but Lane's historical citation is not treated as a modern surah:ayah location.

The Quranic expression العابدين in 43:81 has materially different reported interpretations, including worshippers and angry or disdainful rejecters; the ordinary worshipper sense remains the primary presentation.

The Quranic noun group combines singular and several plural patterns. The evidence reports a common distinction between عبيد for owned slaves and عباد for servants or worshippers of God, but also notes broader overlap in divine-genitive constructions.
