senses.definition: To oppress or humiliate by subduing or overbearing someone.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence, it is a prohibition against oppressing or humiliating the orphan.

senses.definition: One who overcomes, conquers, or subdues.
senses.when: This is the agentive use, including the plural description of people who exercise subjugating power.

senses.definition: The Subduer of created beings by sovereign authority and power.
senses.when: As a divine epithet, it includes disposing of creatures as desired, with or against their will.

senses.definition: Intensively one who overcomes and subdues—the Irresistible.
senses.when: A divine adjective emphasizing overwhelming or pervasive subduing power; all Quranic occurrences are in divine descriptions.

cautions: The Quranic Form I occurrence is normalized from the imperfect form تَقْهَرْ to the classical citation form قَهَرَ.
The QAC nominal tag for قَاهِر occurrences is presented as an active participle because the supplied derived morphology identifies them as ACTIVE_PARTICIPLE.

قول.summary: The root centers on قول, articulated speech or an utterance.
قول.development: From the basic act of speaking, the lexicon develops meanings for a saying or statement, inwardly conceived speech, authoritative pronouncement, forms of eloquence, and several derived terms connected with speech and its content.

senses.definition: To say, speak, utter, or express a word, proposition, or statement.
senses.when: The object may be a word, a complete proposition, a command, or a sound signifying something. The form includes ordinary speech, reported speech, and assertions, without making grammatical voice or tense a separate lexical sense.

senses.definition: To entertain or formulate an unspoken thought or saying in the mind.
senses.when: This use describes what is conceived inwardly before being expressed aloud; the Quranic context explicitly locates the saying in the speakers' selves.

senses.definition: To communicate, command, or bring about something by a divine pronouncement, inspiration, or imposed response rather than ordinary audible address.
senses.when: The Quran applies the verb to inspired direction and to created beings responding through divine subjection; the expression need not describe ordinary human speech heard by an addressee.

senses.definition: To fabricate or make up speech, especially to falsely attribute a statement to someone.
senses.when: In the Quran this describes inventing a saying and falsely presenting it as authoritative or revealed speech.

senses.definition: An utterance, saying, speech, statement, word, or expressed proposition.
senses.when: In Quranic usage it may denote a single word or a complete statement, and may refer to the speech of a person, messenger, or its ultimate source. It can also name the claim or matter expressed by speech. The plural أَقَاوِيل in 69:44 denotes sayings or claims; the associated fabrication is expressed by تَقَوَّلَ.

senses.definition: A binding divine pronouncement or decree whose fulfillment has become certain.
senses.when: In expressions such as حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ, قول denotes the divine determination or word established against a people, rather than merely an audible utterance.

cautions: The Form I QAC group combines many persons, aspects, voices, and imperative forms; the public headword is the normalized citation form قَالَ, and these grammatical variants are not separate senses.
أَقَاوِيل is merged under قَوْل as its plural, while قِيل and قَائِل remain separate public forms because they are distinct nominal formations.
The internal QAC form identity for قِيل is retained as a nominal form; no Lane historical citation has been converted into a modern verse location.

قوم.summary: The root centers on two related principles: a gathered body of people, and standing upright or taking something up with resolve.
قوم.development: From standing and undertaking arise meanings of establishing, maintaining, supporting, correcting, remaining firm, and valuing; the people-sense forms a separate root branch.

senses.definition: to stand or rise; to become standing, established, or operative
senses.when: Used literally of rising or standing and figuratively of something coming into effect or being established. In contexts of resolve, it can introduce undertaking or proceeding to an action.

senses.definition: to set upright, establish, or put into proper order
senses.when: Applies to a physical object, a path, an affair, a standard, or a proof when it is made upright or put right.

senses.definition: to maintain and duly perform an ordinance, prayer, or revealed law
senses.when: In constructions such as establishing prayer or the Torah, the expression includes fulfilling its due requirements and maintaining it in practice, not merely performing an outward act.

senses.definition: to become or remain straight, upright, rightly directed, and firm
senses.when: Used of a person, path, affair, or discourse; with a way or truth, it denotes continuing without deviation in the right course.

senses.definition: establishing or maintaining
senses.when: In the Quran, the verbal noun occurs in contexts of establishing and maintaining worship.

senses.definition: settling, staying, or establishing oneself in a place
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence refers to the stability or settlement provided by dwellings and encampments.

cautions: The QAC قَائِم grouping includes the forms قِيَامٌ and قِيَامٍ as active-participle-derived material; they are retained under that public form because the supplied QAC grouping assigns them there.
قَوْم is lexically associated especially with men in part of the Classical evidence, but the Quranic usage commonly includes an entire associated people, including women.
The Quranic sense of قِيَم in ديناً قيماً reflects the supplied lexical discussion of an upright, corrective religion; it should not be conflated mechanically with every occurrence of قَيِّم.

كبر.summary: A root oriented toward becoming or being great rather than small, whether in physical size, age, rank, importance, severity, or perceived superiority.
كبر.development: The lexical field extends from physical magnitude and growth to age, eminence, consequence, and the evaluation of an affair as difficult or grave. It also develops into magnification, divine majesty, and—when claimed improperly—self-exaltation and arrogance.

senses.definition: To become great, large, or significant; to grow up or attain maturity.
senses.when: Used of physical or recognized greatness and, in Quranic contexts, of growing up or becoming momentous.

senses.definition: To be difficult, severe, grievous, or burdensome.
senses.when: Frequently occurs with عَلَيْهِ, describing an affair or message as difficult or distressing to someone; it can also characterize a grave or momentous statement or matter.

senses.definition: To make great; to magnify or honor.
senses.when: In Quranic worship language, it denotes magnifying God, declaring His greatness, and expressing that greatness in devotion.

senses.definition: To regard something as great; to be greatly impressed by it.
senses.when: The Quranic use describes a strong reaction of admiration or astonishment upon seeing someone or something.

senses.definition: To exalt oneself arrogantly; to regard oneself as superior and act disdainfully.
senses.when: In the Quran, the form denotes blameworthy self-exaltation, including holding oneself above submission or refusing what one ought to accept; بِـ or فِي constructions specify the sphere of the arrogance.

senses.definition: To act arrogantly, claim superiority, or refuse submission and acceptance of truth.
senses.when: The Quranic use is consistently blameworthy: it may describe arrogant conduct generally, arrogance toward a command or sign, or refusal to submit, with عَنْ marking disdainful rejection and فِي marking the sphere in which superiority is claimed.

cautions: كَبُرَ and كَبِرَ are distinct vocalized verbs: the Quranic Form I group is كَبُرَ, while the Classical age verb discussed separately is كَبِرَ.
أَكْبَرَ as a Form IV verb and أَكْبَر as a comparative adjective are homographic but are separate QAC form groups and public entries.
The Quranic uses of اِسْتَكْبَرَ, مُسْتَكْبِر, and مُتَكَبِّر are predominantly blameworthy; the lexical tradition also records distinct laudatory or legitimate uses of related forms.

كتب.summary: The root denotes joining or bringing one thing together with another, especially by writing, binding, or assembling.
كتب.development: From the idea of joining, it develops into writing as the joining of letters, then into a written document, an established prescription or decree, a record, and a formal contract.

senses.definition: To write, inscribe, or record.
senses.when: Includes writing down a text, statement, or account; active, passive, and imperative forms occur in the Quran.

senses.definition: To prescribe, ordain, decree, or establish as fixed or due.
senses.when: Used for divine laws and obligations, appointed outcomes, allotted matters, and what is firmly established, including something established in the heart. The passive construction كُتِبَ عَلَى or كُتِبَ لِ commonly means “was prescribed” or “was decreed for.”

senses.definition: To include or place someone among a group.
senses.when: Especially used with مَعَ in the Quranic construction “include us among …,” rather than meaning physical writing.

senses.definition: To enter into a written contract of emancipation with someone.
senses.when: The Quranic construction concerns a contract between an enslaved person and the master, under which payment leads to freedom; the act is reciprocal between the parties.

senses.definition: To have a text written for oneself; to procure or fabricate a written account.
senses.when: In the Quranic accusation, the subject is said to have had earlier tales written or transcribed for him, rather than necessarily writing them personally.

senses.definition: A writer, scribe, secretary, or recorder.
senses.when: The active participle can denote a person engaged in writing or recording, including scribes and recorders.

cautions: Lane’s historical Quran citation notation is used only as lexical evidence; modern verse locations in the examples come from the supplied QAC occurrences.
The Form III Quran occurrence is an inflected imperative; the public headword is normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form كَاتَبَ.
The possessive form كتابي is accounted for under the core noun كتاب rather than displayed as a separate lexical headword.

كثر.summary: The root denotes the opposite of paucity: being numerous, abundant, or increased in quantity or number.
كثر.development: Its basic quantitative sense extends to comparative superiority, making or acquiring more, rivalry over having more, and intensified abundance such as كَوْثَر.

senses.definition: To become numerous, abundant, or great in quantity; to multiply.
senses.when: An intransitive verb describing an increase or state of plurality in people, things, or quantity.

senses.definition: To make numerous, abundant, or greater in quantity; to increase or multiply something.
senses.when: A causative transitive use, with the object being the people, things, or quantity increased.

senses.definition: To make something abundant, numerous, or greater; to multiply it.
senses.when: A causative use that may take an explicit object, including an action or state made more extensive.

senses.definition: To do, say, or produce much; to be profuse or excessive in an activity.
senses.when: The object may be explicit or suppressed; the construction can describe profuse speech, action, or production.

senses.definition: To desire, seek, or aim to obtain much of something.
senses.when: The desired object may be material or immaterial, such as property, good, or another desired quantity.

senses.definition: To do or have much of something; to engage in or produce it abundantly.
senses.when: This use is equivalent to doing more or much of an activity or thing, with the relevant object or complement supplied by context.

cautions: أَكْثَر appears in separate QAC groups as both the comparative/superlative nominal and a Form IV verb; they are retained as distinct public forms.
كَوْثَر has two Quran-attested interpretive branches in the supplied lexical evidence: abundant good and the river in Paradise.

كره.summary: The root centers on rejection, aversion, or non-acceptance, opposite to رضى and محبت.
كره.development: Its lexical range develops from disliking or being averse to something to the experience of an unwanted burden or externally imposed action, the causative making of something hateful, and qualities or objects viewed as detestable. Classical evidence also preserves specialized extensions involving battle severity and an intractable camel.

senses.definition: To dislike, reject, or be averse to something; to hate it.
senses.when: The aversion may be instinctive or an evaluative, rational, or religious disapproval. The verb expresses the subject’s aversion and does not by itself establish that the disliked thing is objectively bad.

senses.definition: To make something disliked, disapproved of, or hateful to someone.
senses.when: A causative construction in which an object is made an object of aversion for another person.

senses.definition: To compel or force someone to do something against their will.
senses.when: The active construction takes the compelled person as object; the passive means to be forced. Quranic contexts include coercion in conduct, speech, or religious profession.

senses.definition: Compulsion or coercion: forcing someone to do what they dislike or would not choose.
senses.when: The noun denotes externally imposed compulsion; in لا إكراه في الدين it names the absence or rejection of such coercion.

senses.definition: One who dislikes, rejects, or is unwilling to accept or do something.
senses.when: An agentive participle used adjectivally or substantively for a person characterized by aversion or unwillingness.

senses.definition: Against one’s will; under externally imposed compulsion or unwillingly.
senses.when: This noun is used adverbially for an action performed without consent, including constructions rendered “by force” or “unwillingly.” Some lexical analyses distinguish this outwardly imposed condition from كُرْه.

cautions: The distinction between كَرْه and كُرْه is explicitly reported as disputed: one analysis differentiates external compulsion from inwardly experienced aversion or hardship, while another treats the forms as equivalent. The entries preserve the differentiated usage without presenting it as uncontested.

Mufradat records several contextual interpretations of Quranic expressions involving compulsion and willing or unwilling submission. These are interpretive alternatives within the coercion and unwillingness senses, not additional lexical meanings.

كسب.summary: The root centers on seeking and attaining a desired object, benefit, or result.
كسب.development: This orientation extends from seeking sustenance and acquiring wealth to what a person obtains through actions, including beneficial or harmful deeds. The self-directed Form VIII develops the sense of acquiring or incurring something for oneself.

senses.definition: To gain, acquire, or earn something, especially wealth, sustenance, benefit, or another obtained result.
senses.when: Used for what a person obtains through effort or action. In the interpretation of 111:2, a person's children may also be described as part of what he has acquired or earned.

senses.definition: To perform or incur a deed, thereby earning or bringing upon oneself its consequence; especially to do good or evil and to incur sin or blame.
senses.when: The Quran applies this use to both righteous and wrongful acts. It may describe the deed itself, or the reward, punishment, burden, or blame resulting from it; it is not restricted to sinful action.

senses.definition: To acquire or earn something for oneself, especially a benefit, share, possession, or other personal gain.
senses.when: The Form VIII expression is self-directed in contrast with broader uses of كَسَبَ. It is attested for beneficial acquisition, including a person's share of what he or she has acquired.

senses.definition: To incur, bring upon oneself, or acquire for oneself a deed or consequence, especially harm, blame, sin, or another adverse result.
senses.when: This self-directed use occurs in morally adverse contexts as well as in the contrastive construction of 2:286. Interpretations that divide كَسَبَ strictly between good and اِكْتَسَبَ strictly between evil are reported but are not uniformly maintained.

cautions: The Quran-linked discussion of the contrast between كَسَبَ and اِكْتَسَبَ in 2:286 records more than one interpretation; a strict division of good for كَسَبَ and evil for اِكْتَسَبَ is not uniform.
The interpretation of ما كسب in 111:2 as including children is a reported contextual extension of acquisition, not a restriction on the ordinary meaning of the verb.

كفر.summary: The root centrally denotes covering, concealing, or placing something under a covering.
كفر.development: From physical covering and concealment, the lexical field develops into concealing or denying a favor or truth, disbelief, and related expressions for things that cover or enclose other things.

senses.definition: To cover or conceal; in a Quran-focused construction, to conceal or cover over what should be recognized.
senses.when: The covering sense is literal in the lexical field and is also used figuratively in the Quranic expression explained as concealing a bond or familiar relationship. The historical citation supplied for that expression is not converted into a modern verse location here.

senses.definition: To disbelieve in, deny, or reject God, revelation, faith, or an established truth.
senses.when: This is the principal Quranic religious use and may describe denial in the heart, denial in speech, or refusal to accept the truth. Voice, tense, and person vary grammatically without creating separate lexical senses.

senses.definition: To deny, conceal, or fail to acknowledge a favor or benefit; to be ungrateful.
senses.when: Often used of failing to acknowledge divine favors or failing to render the gratitude and duty owed for them; the object may be expressed with بِ or directly.

senses.definition: To repudiate or disavow someone or something; to declare oneself free of an association or claim.
senses.when: This Quran-attested construction is used with بِ and expresses disavowal or refusal of responsibility, association, or an alleged partner.

senses.definition: To efface, remove, or cover over sins and wrongful acts.
senses.when: The Quranic construction commonly takes the sins or evil acts as the object, expressing their removal or concealment so that they are treated as no longer standing against the person.

senses.definition: How ungrateful or disbelieving he is!
senses.when: A Quranic exclamatory construction describing the human tendency toward ingratitude and denial; it is not the ordinary causative Form IV meaning found in broader Classical Arabic.

cautions: كَافُور in 76:5 has more than one explicitly reported interpretation: camphor or a camphor-like mixture, and a spring or fountain in Paradise.
The Quranic context glosses vary between religious disbelief, denial, and ingratitude; the lexical evidence supports these as related but materially distinct branches.
Historical Lane Quran citations are preserved as lexical attestations without being converted into modern verse locations when the identification is not independently secure.

كفف.summary: The root centers on grasping, contracting, and holding back, represented concretely by the hand and extended to restraint, enclosure, and surrounding.
كفف.development: From the act of grasping or closing the hand, the lexical family develops meanings of restraining or preventing, forming an edge or enclosing rim, surrounding something, and related derived actions. These root-level relations do not make every development a meaning of each Quranic form.

senses.definition: To restrain, hold back, withhold, avert, or prevent.
senses.when: Used transitively with a person, action, force, or the hands as object; the Quranic contexts include restraining people from acting, withholding hands, and averting an attack or harm.

senses.definition: All together, collectively, or comprehensively; as a whole.
senses.when: A collective or comprehensive qualifier, sometimes rendered “all,” “entirely,” or “completely.” In the Quran it can describe a group acting together or the comprehensive scope of an action or address.

senses.definition: Restraining or holding people back, especially from wrongdoing.
senses.when: An explicitly reported Quranic interpretation of كَافَّةً لِلنَّاسِ and of the parallel construction in the command concerning the polytheists; it represents the restraint-related interpretation rather than a general replacement for the collective sense.

senses.definition: The hand, especially the palm or grasping part of the hand.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrences are the dual possessive form كَفَّيْهِ, “his two hands”; the singular citation form is used here for the lexical headword.

cautions: كَافَّةٌ has an explicitly reported Quranic restraint-related interpretation in addition to its collective or comprehensive interpretation; the two are retained as separate senses.
A poetic derived-form use reported in the root discussion is ambiguous: مُسْتَكِفَّاتٌ is interpreted either as eyes or as gathered camels. It is not used to define a separate public meaning here.

كفي.summary: The supplied lexical evidence centers the root on sufficiency: filling a need and bringing an intended matter to its desired result.
كفي.development: Related attested extensions include standing in for another by undertaking an affair, warding off harm, and being content with what suffices. These extensions are not automatically meanings of every Quranic form.

senses.definition: To suffice for someone or something; to be enough to fill a need, attain an intended result, or make further provision unnecessary.
senses.when: Quranic uses include an agent sufficing a person or group, including by making a threat, opposition, or required action unnecessary. The agent may also be introduced with بِـ in a sufficiency construction such as كَفَى بِنَا.

senses.definition: To suffice or serve in a specified capacity, especially to be sufficient as a witness.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا, بِـ may be understood as introducing the agent of “Allah suffices as witness.” The supplied lexical discussion also records an alternative construal equivalent to taking or being content with Allah as witness.

senses.definition: Sufficient or enough to meet a need.
senses.when: An active participle used predicatively or after بِـ, as in بِكَافٍ, “sufficient.”

cautions: The construction كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا is reported with two grammatical interpretations: Allah suffices as witness, or contentment with Allah as witness.
The supplied Mufradat row for كاف discusses the homonymous simile particle and is not evidence for the active participle كَافٍ; it is excluded from the form senses.

كلل.summary: The root exhibits three broad orientations: loss of sharpness or force, enclosure or surrounding, and a bodily member. These develop into meanings of dullness, fatigue, dependence, encompassing totality, collateral relation, and crown-like encirclement.
كلل.development: The loss-of-edge branch yields dullness, weakness, fatigue, and burden; the enclosing branch yields total inclusion, collateral kinship, and crown or surrounding formations. Related lexical developments also include anatomical and figurative extensions.

senses.definition: A deceased person who leaves neither parent nor offspring; by extension, the inheritance situation defined by that absence.
senses.when: Used in inheritance discourse; the term may refer to the deceased person or to the estate and succession case associated with the absence of direct ascendants and descendants.

senses.definition: The collateral heirs of a person who leaves neither parent nor offspring—heirs other than the direct parent or child.
senses.when: Used in inheritance discourse for heirs connected through a collateral relationship rather than the direct parent-child line.

senses.definition: A burden, especially a dependent person who must be supported.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction كَلٌّ عَلَى مَوْلَاهُ, the term describes someone or something burdensome to a supporting patron.

senses.definition: The whole or complete extent of a thing, including all of its relevant parts or states; fully or completely.
senses.when: Used with a noun, pronoun, or an understood complement when the emphasis is on the entirety or complete degree of a thing or state.

senses.definition: Every, each, or all: encompassing the members or kinds of a set.
senses.when: Used with a definite plural, a pronoun, a singular indefinite, or an understood complement; the construction may be distributive or collective according to context.

senses.definition: Any one.
senses.when: In a negative clause followed by an exception, كُلٌّ means “any one,” as in the Quranic negative–exception construction.

cautions: كَلَالَةٌ is used in the supplied Quran-focused evidence both for the deceased or inheritance situation lacking a parent and child and for the collateral heirs; these are presented as separate but related senses.
The negative–exception sense of كُلٌّ is illustrated at the independently supplied QAC location 38:14; the historical printed citation in the lexical evidence is not converted into a modern location.
A reported comparison of كَلَّلَ with نكل in the root discussion does not have a securely recoverable sense in the supplied evidence.

كلم.summary: The root has two principal branches: intelligible speech and physical wounding. The Quranic vocabulary chiefly develops the speech branch.
كلم.development: The speech branch extends from meaningful utterance to the word, statement, discourse, and divine pronouncement; the other branch denotes a wound or perceptible injury. A rare, tentative usage also applies كَلَامٌ to rough or hard ground.

senses.definition: To speak to, address, or communicate verbally with someone.
senses.when: The Quran uses the form for direct or mediated address, including divine speaking to a human being. Its passive occurrence describes someone being spoken to; this is a voice variation of the same lexical action.

senses.definition: To speak or utter speech.
senses.when: The Quranic Form V use presents the subject as speaking; the object or addressee may be supplied by context rather than by the verb itself.

senses.definition: Speech, spoken words, or discourse, including the meaning conveyed by an utterance.
senses.when: In Quranic usage it can denote words or speech attributed to God, as well as speech that is heard, transmitted, or referred to collectively. The noun may cover a saying or discourse rather than only a single word.

senses.definition: An intelligible expression or proposition: a word, saying, sentence, assertion, or expressed opinion.
senses.when: The singular denotes one expression or statement; the merged plural forms denote multiple words or statements. The Quran also uses the noun for a complete expressed proposition rather than merely an isolated lexical word.

senses.definition: A divinely established pronouncement, promise, command, judgment, or decree.
senses.when: In constructions such as “the word of your Lord” or “the word of punishment,” the noun refers to an enacted divine determination, promise, revealed decision, or binding outcome, not necessarily to a single spoken utterance.

senses.definition: The “Word” as a designation of Jesus, associated with his coming into being by God’s command and with the guidance conveyed through him.
senses.when: This specialized Quranic usage occurs in the expression describing Jesus as a word from God and as His word cast to Mary.

cautions: The evidence distinguishes the speech and wound branches of كلم; they should not be treated as one semantic development.

Interpretations of Quranic كلمة in divine constructions include revelation, promise, command, decree, judgment, and established outcome; these are grouped under one constructional sense rather than asserted as a single exclusive referent.
The supplied Lane supplement includes كُلْيَةٌ under this root record; it is retained under its own headword and object-specific meaning rather than being assimilated to the speech vocabulary.

كون.summary: The root centers on reporting that something occurs, is present, or comes to be, with reference to past or present time.
كون.development: This orientation develops into the existential and copular verb كَانَ and related ideas of being and coming into existence. The derivation of مَكَانٌ from كَانَ يَكُونُ is reported as a qualified view, not as an established direct meaning of the root.

senses.definition: To be, exist, or be in a stated condition; also to serve as a copula linking a subject with its predicate.
senses.when: It commonly presents a state or existence with past-time reference, but the surrounding construction may yield present, future, habitual, or counterfactual translations. It may be used without an independently emphasized time meaning as a copula. With divine predicates or generic subjects, it can mark a characteristic understood as enduring or little subject to separation; a past reference may describe either a continuing state or one that later changed. In كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ, the past form can point to the status assigned in divine determination or judgment rather than simply replacing a present-tense form.

senses.definition: To occur, come about, or be realized or present.
senses.when: Explicitly attested in the conditional construction إِنْ كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ, where the sense is that a hardship or condition has occurred or is present.

senses.definition: A place of being or existence; a place or position occupied by someone or something.
senses.when: The Quranic noun can refer literally to a place, as well as to the place in which a group or thing is situated.

senses.definition: Position, standing, or state; the condition or station in which someone is placed.
senses.when: Used especially in expressions concerning a person's or group's position, standing, or condition.

senses.definition: A place, location, or site.
senses.when: Includes a physical location or a designated place; the LOC-tagged Quranic occurrences are included under this same noun.

senses.definition: A position, station, or rank.
senses.when: Used figuratively for a person's or group's position or station, including a place in an evaluative or social order.

cautions: The derivation of مَكَانٌ from كَانَ يَكُونُ is reported as a qualified lexical view, not asserted as certain.
كَانَ often functions grammatically as an auxiliary or copula, so English tense choices are strongly dependent on construction and context.
Historical citation notation in the lexical evidence has not been converted into additional modern Quran locations; the examples use only supplied QAC locations.

كيف.summary: The direct semantic center of كَيْف is inquiry into a describable state, quality, or manner—“how?”. The same root record also contains the distinct noun الكِيفَة, “a piece of cloth.”
كيف.development: The evidence juxtaposes the cloth noun with the interrogative كيف without establishing a secure derivational path between them. In Quranic usage, inquiry into state or manner also functions rhetorically to alert or rebuke the addressee.

senses.definition: How?—asking about the state, quality, or manner of a person, thing, or event.
senses.when: The question concerns a describable condition or mode of occurrence, whether the answer is explicit or understood. Quranic rhetorical references to divine matters are treated under the following usage.

senses.definition: How could, can, or will it be?—a rhetorical question used to draw attention to a matter or to rebuke the addressee.
senses.when: In Quranic rhetoric, especially in statements concerning divine acts or the conduct of people, كيف may alert or reproach rather than seek an ordinary informational answer.

cautions: QAC separates three occurrences under a nominal tag and eighty under INTG; they are presented together because the evidence supports one lexical interrogative كيف with the same Quranic uses.

لبب.summary: The root centers on remaining or adhering, and on the pure or choice inner part of something.
لبب.development: From remaining and steadfast adherence develop senses of persistence, service, and repeated response; from the inner or choicest part develop meanings for kernel, essence, and purified intellect. Several bodily, garment-related, and figurative uses extend from the chest or inner core.

senses.definition: Pure, sound intellect; discerning understanding.
senses.when: The Quranic form أَلْبَاب is the plural of لُبّ and occurs in constructions referring to people characterized by such purified understanding, including أُولُوا الْأَلْبَابِ. It is presented as a more particular kind of intellect than intellect in general.

cautions: The canonical Quran form is the plural أَلْبَاب, normalized here under the singular citation form لُبّ.

The Lane material is matched through the contracted geminate root لب; broader meanings below remain attached to their stated headwords and derived forms rather than being treated as meanings of the Quranic plural.
Some Classical entries preserve explicitly reported alternative readings or regional usages; these are identified in their usage conditions rather than presented as Quranic senses.

لعن.summary: The root centers on forceful removal and exclusion, especially banishment under condemnation.
لعن.development: The basic notion of driving away develops into cursing: for God, exclusion from mercy, guidance, and ultimately blessedness; for people, an invocation of condemnation against another. Reciprocal and reflexive cursing constructions develop from the same semantic field.

senses.definition: To curse: to invoke or impose banishment from mercy as an expression of condemnation.
senses.when: When attributed to God, the curse denotes exclusion from mercy and guidance in this world and punishment or banishment in the Hereafter. When attributed to people, it is a supplication or invocation against another. Active and passive voice express the same lexical action and result.

senses.definition: Cursing; the act or invocation of pronouncing a curse.
senses.when: A verbal noun for the act of invoking condemnation or exclusion from mercy; the Quranic occurrence appears in an intensified construction.

senses.definition: A curse; an imposed state or sentence of exclusion from mercy.
senses.when: Used as a countable or definite noun, including in expressions such as God's curse and the curse upon a people or party.

senses.definition: One who curses; one who invokes a curse against another.
senses.when: The Quranic plural refers to those who pronounce curses, in a construction where they curse people who conceal or suppress revealed guidance.

senses.definition: Accursed; subjected to condemnation and exclusion from mercy.
senses.when: Used adjectivally or substantively for one placed under a curse; the Quranic forms include feminine singular and masculine plural inflections.

cautions: The Quran-only plural active participle لَاعِنُون and the feminine and masculine plural passive participles مَلْعُونَة and مَلْعُونِين are normalized to singular dictionary citation forms.
The Quranic noun لَعْنَة meaning “a curse” is distinct in vocalization and meaning from the Classical personal epithet لُعْنَة meaning “a person who is much cursed.”

لقي.summary: The root expresses encounter or convergence, casting or placing something, and a separate archaic branch associated with curvature.
لقي.development: Its principal semantic developments are coming face to face or finding, and throwing or placing something where it may be encountered. Derived forms extend these ideas to reciprocal meeting, receiving, conveying, bestowing, and casting.

senses.definition: To meet, encounter, come upon, or find someone or something.
senses.when: Used for direct encounter and for finding or coming upon an object; tense and grammatical voice do not create separate lexical senses.

senses.definition: To experience or undergo something that befalls one, including hardship, good, or evil.
senses.when: The object may be an experience or condition rather than a person; the Quran explicitly applies the usage to experiencing fatigue.

senses.definition: To cause someone to receive or undergo something; to greet, bestow, or impart something to them.
senses.when: The recipient may be given a greeting, a quality or state such as radiance and joy, or a conveyed message; passive forms describe something being received or granted.

senses.definition: To meet or encounter someone face to face; to have an interview with them.
senses.when: The Form III construction presents the meeting as an encounter between parties.

senses.definition: To throw, cast, put, place, or cause to fall.
senses.when: The object may be cast down, out, into a place, or onto something; active and passive constructions express the corresponding placing or being cast.

senses.definition: To convey, present, offer, or address something to another.
senses.when: The construction with إِلَى or عَلَى is used for words, a message, salutation or submission, affection, and other things presented or communicated to a recipient.

cautions: The Quranic phrase لِقَاءُ الله and related forms conventionally refer to the eschatological meeting, resurrection, and return to God; this is a contextual specialization of the broader meeting noun.

ليس.summary: The supplied evidence supports negation as the central orientation: ليس denies a predicate or asserted state.
ليس.development: The form is a defective Form I verb whose ordinary predicate-negation may, by context, refer beyond the present and may also acquire generalized force in constructions meaning that there is no such circumstance.

senses.definition: To be not; to negate a predicate or asserted state.
senses.when: A defective negative verb, ordinarily used for particular predicate-negation, especially concerning the present state. It governs a nominative subject and an accusative predicate; context can extend the negation to another time, and the verb may also negate a following verbal assertion.

senses.definition: To negate generally or universally: there is no such thing, circumstance, or liability.
senses.when: Used in a generalizing negative construction, equivalent in force to لا التبرئة. This includes constructions such as ليس عليكم جناح, in which no blame or liability is asserted.

cautions: Classical grammatical analysis records disagreement over whether ليس is a defective verb or a particle; QAC identifies the supplied Quranic occurrences as Verb · Form I.

ليل.summary: The root denotes night as the temporal counterpart of day, with لَيْل referring generally to night and لَيْلَة to an individual or designated night.
ليل.development: The lexical family distinguishes the general night-period from a counted or specified night and its plural forms, including لَيَالٍ and لَيْلَاتٌ.

senses.definition: Night; the period opposed to daytime.
senses.when: Used as a temporal noun, including prepositional and adverbial constructions meaning by, in, or at night. Its plural forms include لَيَالٍ and لَيْلَاتٌ; these are grammatical variants of the same lexical branch.

senses.definition: A single, counted, or specifically designated night.
senses.when: Used for an individual night or a night identified by an event or designation, including a specified number of nights and the Night of Decree. Its plural forms include لَيَالٍ and لَيْلَاتٌ.

cautions: The principal meaning ‘night, opposite to day’ is explicit in the root-level and Quran-focused evidence; the main Lane line for لَيْل is a cross-reference rather than a full definition.

متع.summary: A root centered on benefit, enjoyment, and useful provision whose benefit may extend over a period of time.
متع.development: Its lexical development connects enjoyment and usefulness with duration and extension: something useful is made available for continued benefit, while the day, vegetation, a mirage, or a rope may be described through rising or lasting extension. The sources also preserve an alternate emphasis on pleasure or immediate enjoyment.

senses.definition: To grant someone enjoyment, benefit, or provision, allowing continued use or comfort for a period; to let someone live on in such benefit.
senses.when: The construction commonly takes a person or group as object and may specify a limited duration or brief worldly enjoyment. The duration is not inherently fixed.

senses.definition: To provide a divorced woman with a compensatory gift or provision.
senses.when: A divorce-related construction; the provision may consist of necessities such as food, clothing, household utensils, or furniture and is assigned according to means.

senses.definition: To enjoy or benefit from something; to make use of it or have its enjoyment.
senses.when: Usually construed with بِـ. Duration may be extended, but the expression does not always imply a specifically long period. In several worldly Quranic commands and warnings, the enjoyment is presented as temporary or threatening contextually.

senses.definition: In the pilgrimage construction, to perform ʿumrah together with hajj, taking the ʿumrah as the enjoyment or preliminary use before hajj.
senses.when: A specialized construction with بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ; it is distinct from the ordinary meaning of enjoying or benefiting from something.

senses.definition: To live or remain alive for a time.
senses.when: A Quran-linked lexical equivalence to عاش reported for this form; it should not be inferred as the gloss of every Quran occurrence of تَمَتَّعَ.

senses.definition: To seek or derive benefit and enjoyment from something; to profit by or enjoy it.
senses.when: Normally construed with بِـ and applicable to taking one's benefit or enjoyment from a thing, person, or share. The Quranic contexts may express mutual or worldly benefit without requiring a separate sexual sense.

cautions: The Form V worldly-enjoyment passages may carry a threatening or admonitory pragmatic force, but that force is contextual rather than a separate lexical sense.
A Form V equivalence with عاش is retained as lexical evidence without assigning Lane's historical citation to a modern Quran location not supplied as a QAC occurrence.
The anatomical meaning of المَتَاعُ is a rare tropical Classical Arabic specialization and is not assigned to the Quranic nominal senses.

مثل.summary: A relation of likeness, correspondence, or conformity between one thing and another.
مثل.development: From the basic idea of one thing being like or set as a model for another develop the senses of counterpart, comparison, parable, exemplary punishment, representation, and upright standing.

senses.definition: To assume or appear in a particular form or likeness.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction تَمَثَّلَ, the subject takes on a represented appearance; the attested passage concerns appearing in human form.

senses.definition: More exemplary, best, or closest to virtue.
senses.when: Used adjectivally for what is most like the excellent or most conducive to goodness.

senses.definition: A likeness or descriptive comparison; the comparable condition, state, or case of something.
senses.when: Used for describing one thing through its resemblance or correspondence to another, including a comparable state or situation.

senses.definition: A parable or illustrative example: a saying, image, or presented case used to clarify another matter through resemblance.
senses.when: Common in expressions introducing or presenting a comparison for reflection, instruction, or illustration.

senses.definition: An exemplary punishment or punitive affliction made a warning to deter others.
senses.when: The Quranic plural refers to punishments that serve as deterrent examples for similar wrongdoing.

senses.definition: A like, counterpart, or likeness; something corresponding to another in a relevant respect.
senses.when: The comparison may concern kind, quality, quantity, manner, or another aspect of correspondence; attached pronouns and plural forms identify the thing or people compared.

cautions: The مَثَل group is normalized to the singular citation form although its Quranic occurrences include inflected singular and plural forms and one adjectival tag.
مُثْلَة and تِمْثَال are presented as singular citation forms for Quranic plural form groups.
The rare classical interpretation of تَمَاثِيل as written books is kept separate from the Quranic representation/statue sense.

محل.summary: The root has two principal semantic orientations: deprivation of beneficial provision, especially through drought, and hostile pursuit or advocacy involving a charge against someone.
محل.development: The deprivation branch appears in drought, barren land, rainless stars, and spoiled milk. A separate interpersonal branch concerns pursuing someone with an accusation, while also extending to arguing in someone's defense. The Quranic مِحَال is interpreted either through punitive seizure or through power and strategic capacity.

senses.definition: Punitive seizure: taking someone with punishment or intending harm against him.
senses.when: Used in the Quranic expression شَدِيدُ الْمِحَالِ, where it describes formidable punitive action directed against wrongdoers.

senses.definition: Power, force, or effective capacity to act, including strategic ability.
senses.when: An alternative interpretation of شَدِيدُ الْمِحَالِ derives the word from حَوْل and حِيلَة; this is an interpretation of the same Quranic occurrence, not a separate occurrence.

cautions: The two Quranic senses of مِحَالٌ are alternative interpretations of its single supplied occurrence in 13:13; the contextual gloss “(in) Strength” does not by itself resolve the lexical interpretation.

محو.summary: The root expresses causing something to go away, especially by removing its trace or effect.
محو.development: The basic orientation develops from making clouds or other things pass away to erasing writing, traces, signs, or effects. The noun مَحْوَةٌ for the north wind is explained through its dispersing of clouds.

senses.definition: To efface, erase, obliterate, or cancel something, causing it or its trace or effect to disappear.
senses.when: A transitive Form I verb of removal and disappearance. In the Quran it is used for divine erasure, including erasing what is willed and erasing a sign; the same general removal sense covers making something pass away or cancelling its effect.

مدد.summary: The root centers on drawing or extending something lengthwise and on joining an added thing to another.
مدد.development: From physical stretching and lengthening, the meanings develop toward prolonging, increasing or replenishing, supplying aid or provisions, and the related nouns for extension, measure, ink, and material addition.

senses.definition: To extend, stretch, or spread outward.
senses.when: In the Quran, used for spreading or extending the earth, shade, or another thing; the basic physical extension may be expressed transitively or through a resulting state.

senses.definition: To stretch one's sight toward something with desire or attention.
senses.when: A sight-directed construction with the eye or gaze extended toward an object; this is distinct from merely spreading or lengthening a thing.

senses.definition: To prolong or cause someone to continue in a condition, especially error or punishment.
senses.when: Used of extending a person's continuation or exposure to a condition; Quranic examples concern error, delusion, or punishment rather than physical extension.

senses.definition: To increase, replenish, or augment one thing by adding to it.
senses.when: Used when a river, sea, or other quantity is fed or augmented by an additional supply; the result is increased abundance or flow.

senses.definition: To provide, furnish, or increase someone’s supply of provisions or resources.
senses.when: The added provision may be food, wealth, children, or other resources; the construction commonly takes the supplied person or group and the thing supplied with bi- or an equivalent complement.

senses.definition: To reinforce, aid, or succour with additional support or forces.
senses.when: Used especially of strengthening people with helpers, troops, or other means of support; supplying and military reinforcement are closely related but distinguishable applications.

cautions: Lane's printed Quran references use historical citation conventions; the artifact relies on the independently supplied QAC locations rather than converting Lane bracketed references.

The distribution of the meanings of مَدَّ and أَمَدَّ between prolonging, adding, and aiding is not absolute in the Classical evidence; the Quranic senses preserve the constructions explicitly supported here.

مكث.summary: The root centers on stopping or staying with waiting and expectation.
مكث.development: From stopping and waiting, the lexical range extends to tarrying in a place, abiding, deliberate lack of haste, and loitering while proceeding.

senses.definition: To tarry, stay, or remain, especially while waiting or expecting.
senses.when: Used of remaining or pausing in a place, including an imperative to stay and a narrative statement that someone remained or stayed.

senses.definition: Tarrying or waiting; a stay or period of remaining.
senses.when: Verbal noun referring to the act or duration of staying, tarrying, or waiting.

senses.definition: Remaining, staying, or abiding.
senses.when: Active participle describing one who remains or abides, including continued residence or presence over time.

مكر.summary: The main lexical orientation is deliberate, often concealed maneuvering that diverts another through stratagem, deception, or cunning. A separate lexical branch concerns the thickness or fleshiness of the legs.
مكر.development: The principal branch extends across the act of plotting, the resulting scheme or plot, its active agent, reciprocal forms, and the Quranic usage of divine counteraction or requital. The moral value of mكر varies with its object, while the leg-related branch is treated as lexically distinct.

senses.definition: To employ a covert stratagem, deception, or artifice to divert another from what they intend; to plot or scheme.
senses.when: The action may be praiseworthy or blameworthy according to its object. With بِ, the construction means to deceive, beguile, or circumvent someone; the verb may also be used for plotting a thing.

senses.definition: Of God, to counter or requite opponents’ plotting, including by granting them respite and worldly enablement until punishment overtakes them.
senses.when: This is the specialized Quranic construction مَكَرَ اللهُ. Its transmitted explanations include divine counteraction or requital and the gradual taking of those who are allowed to prosper while their wrongdoing brings about their punishment.

senses.definition: One who practices mكر: a plotter or deviser of a covert stratagem.
senses.when: The Quranic plural مَاكِرِينَ is used of God as the superior counter-planner against hostile plotting.

senses.definition: A covert stratagem, deception, or artful scheme used to divert or circumvent another; a plot or machination.
senses.when: The noun may denote the plotting itself or the resulting plan. Its moral value depends on the object and purpose of the scheme.

senses.definition: God’s counteraction or requital of plotting; also His granting of respite and worldly enablement that leads the wrongdoer toward punishment.
senses.when: This is the Quranic expression مَكْرُ اللهِ and related constructions referring to divine action against plotters.

cautions: Divine مكر has several transmitted explanations, including counteraction or requital and the granting of respite with worldly enablement; it should not be reduced mechanically to ordinary human deception.
The bodily sense concerning thick or fleshy legs is lexically separate from the main deception-and-stratagem branch.

ملك.summary: A firm hold or strength in a thing, extending to possession, control, authority, and sovereignty.
ملك.development: The root's basic notion of strength and firmness develops into having a secure hold over property or affairs, exercising power and rule, and designating kingship, ownership, and related realms of dominion.

senses.definition: To possess or own; to hold something under one's control.
senses.when: In the Quranic construction مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ and related expressions, the object is a person under ownership; the verb is otherwise general and is not restricted to persons or property.

senses.definition: To have power or capacity over something; to be able to affect or dispose of it.
senses.when: Often used with benefit, harm, life, death, resurrection, or another outcome; this use denotes capability or effective control rather than simple possession.

senses.definition: To exercise command or rule over an affair or a people.
senses.when: The construction may concern the ordering of an affair or the exercise of dominion over people, emphasizing governing authority.

senses.definition: Owner, possessor, or master: one who possesses something and has disposal or authority over it.
senses.when: Can designate human ownership or mastery and divine ownership and authority; it may occur in relation to a thing, a realm, or an affair.

senses.definition: An angel; a single member of the angelic beings.
senses.when: The singular denotes one angel, while مَلَائِكَة refers to angels collectively or in the plural; Quranic compounds also include the angel of death.

senses.definition: God's dominion or kingdom: the encompassing realm of divine sovereignty over creation.
senses.when: In Quranic usage it is associated especially with the heavens and earth and with recognition of God's comprehensive authority.

cautions: The proper-name occurrence Mālik at 43:77 is excluded from the lexical form list and is not conflated with مَالِك, owner or master.
مَلَك meaning angel and the Classical homonym مَلَك meaning water are distinct lexical branches.
The Quranic مَلِيك occurrence is subsumed under the king/sovereign branch of مَلِك; the Classical مِلِيك meaning slave is a different vocalization and meaning.

ملو.summary: An orientation toward extending or prolonging something across time, space, or another span.
ملو.development: The root develops from widening or extending something to prolonged life or duration, granting respite, and the extension of a text through dictation. The Quranic forms use these branches for giving respite, dictating, and a long duration.

senses.definition: To grant respite; to defer or allow someone more time.
senses.when: The Quranic usage concerns giving a person or group time, sometimes rendered as prolonging or deferring; the active and passive forms do not create separate lexical senses.

senses.definition: To dictate a text to someone.
senses.when: Used in the construction of dictating or reciting written material to a recipient, as in the expression meaning that it is dictated to him.

senses.definition: A long while; a prolonged duration.
senses.when: In the Quranic occurrence, the adjective is used adverbially with the meaning “for a long time.”

cautions: No Lane primary entry was matched for this root in the supplied evidence. The Mufradat record is headed ملا through final-weak-root normalization, but it explicitly explains the relevant Quranic forms and cites their Quranic usages.

مهد.summary: The root denotes preparing, smoothing, leveling, and making something ready or easy.
مهد.development: Its concrete orientation is the preparation of a level bed or surface; this develops into arranging affairs, preparing benefits or conditions, and naming a prepared resting expanse. Related lexical branches include the spreading or elevation of a camel's hump and several specialized nominal uses.

senses.definition: To prepare or provide something for oneself.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrence uses the verb with a reflexive or benefactive construction, referring to what people prepare or provide for themselves, including beneficial things or consequences.

senses.definition: To prepare, arrange, and make something plain or easy for someone.
senses.when: The Quranic construction is transitive with a beneficiary introduced by لِـ; it can describe making an affair ready and manageable.

senses.definition: One who spreads, levels, or prepares a place.
senses.when: The Quranic form is plural and is used of spreading or preparing the earth.

senses.definition: A child's cradle or bed.
senses.when: This is the prepared place in which a child sleeps or rests.

senses.definition: A bed or prepared, level expanse for lying, sitting, or habitation.
senses.when: The term can denote an even or smooth surface, including the earth as an expanse made ready for use.

senses.definition: What a person has prepared for himself as his final place or condition.
senses.when: This figurative Quran-attested interpretation concerns a person's prepared end or final place; the reported citation is preserved without assigning it a modern verse location.

cautions: مَهْدٌ and مِهَادٌ overlap in the sense of a prepared bed or resting expanse, while مَهْدٌ also has a specifically child-cradle use.
One Lane Quran citation for the figurative final-place interpretation uses historical citation notation and is not converted into a modern surah:ayah location.

موت.summary: The root centers on the loss or departure of force, vitality, or life from something; hence موت is the opposite of life.
موت.development: From physical death, the lexical field extends to lifeless land, loss of sensation or understanding, sleep, stillness, exhaustion, mortality, and figurative states resembling death. Derived forms also express causing death, seeking or feigning death, and states associated with mortality.

senses.definition: to die; to undergo the departure of life
senses.when: Used literally of a person or other living being. Perfect, imperfect, imperative, and passive-context translations reflect grammatical form rather than separate lexical meanings.

senses.definition: to become deprived of sensation, as though dead
senses.when: A Quran-attested figurative use in which the loss of bodily feeling or vitality is expressed through death language.

senses.definition: to become as though dead through overwhelming grief, sorrow, or fear
senses.when: A figurative construction describing an emotion that disturbs or diminishes life; it should not be restricted to literal death.

senses.definition: to cause someone or something to die; to put to death
senses.when: A transitive causative construction. The subject may be God or another agent in the Quranic wording; the core meaning is causing death, not merely undergoing it.

senses.definition: dying; death as an event or state
senses.when: A nominal expression for the occasion or condition of dying, including possessive constructions such as “my dying” and “their death.”

senses.definition: death; lifelessness, the opposite of life
senses.when: The ordinary noun for death or the absence of life, including the loss of vitality in living beings and the lifeless condition of things such as land.

cautions: مَيْت and مَيِّت are displayed as one normalized public form because the lexical evidence explicitly treats them as equivalent or contracted variants, although some authorities distinguish a dead person from one near death.
The Quranic form senses preserve figurative uses explicitly explained in the lexical evidence; contextual English renderings alone have not been used to create meanings.
Lane's historical Quran citations are not converted into modern verse locations unless the corresponding QAC occurrence is independently supplied and secure.

موه.summary: The root centers on water and water-like qualities: a liquid source that can be brought forth, enter, or be applied.
موه.development: The historical form مَوَه is presented as the basis of ماء. Related developments extend the water image to coating with silver or gold, facial freshness, seepage, and other water-related actions.

senses.definition: Water, the ordinary liquid substance.
senses.when: Used in contexts including rain, flowing or stored water, purification, life, growth, and flooding; these are contextual applications of the same noun rather than separate lexical senses. Quranic surface forms vary with case, definiteness, and attached pronouns.

cautions: The public headword ماء is a normalized citation form; the QAC occurrences include case endings, definiteness, and attached pronouns.

نبأ.summary: The root centers on something coming from one place to another: a person, sound, report, or information arriving from elsewhere.
نبأ.development: The movement principle extends to reports as information that reaches a hearer, to the informer, and to the prophet as one who conveys knowledge of God and the unseen. Related classical branches also describe sound, emergence, elevation, and arrival from another place.

senses.definition: To inform, tell, or make someone know something.
senses.when: The Quranic form is used for conveying information to a recipient, including information about deeds, events, or previously unknown matters. It is presented in the lexical discussion as more emphatic than أَنْبَأَ, especially where the information is strongly established or confirmed.

senses.definition: To inform someone of something, tell it to them, or make it known to them.
senses.when: The Quranic construction presents a recipient together with the information disclosed. It overlaps in meaning with نَبَّأَ, while the latter is described as the more emphatic form in some usages.

senses.definition: To seek information or ask to be informed.
senses.when: In its Quranic occurrence, the verb describes asking for information about whether something is true.

senses.definition: A significant report, piece of news, account, or narrative.
senses.when: The term may denote information or a reported account; in its more specific characterization, it is a report of consequence from which knowledge or a strong probability results and which is not false. In النَّبَأُ الْعَظِيمُ, the report is described in interpretation as the Qur'an, the resurrection, or the Prophet's case, without those being separate lexical meanings.

senses.definition: An allegation, plea, or excuse offered in response to a matter.
senses.when: This Quran-attested contextual use occurs in the plural الْأَنْبَاءُ in the expression describing people who have no answer, allegation, or excuse available to them.

senses.definition: A prophet: a person who conveys divine guidance and is informed concerning God and matters of the unseen.
senses.when: The Quranic noun is the unhamzated form نَبِيّ. In the lexical distinction recorded here, every رسول is a نبيّ, but not every نبيّ is necessarily a رسول.

cautions: The Quranic form نَبِيٌّ is unhamzated. Classical sources discuss نَبِىْءٌ as a hamzated variant or related headword and also record competing derivations from informing and elevation; these etymological and pronunciation discussions should not be treated as separate Quranic senses.

نَبَّأَ and أَنْبَأَ both mean to inform in Quranic usage, while the lexical discussion presents نَبَّأَ as more emphatic in some constructions; the distinction is one of force and usage, not a wholly separate reporting domain.

نخل.summary: The root centers on selecting and choosing, especially taking the best portion of something.
نخل.development: The lexical evidence extends this orientation to sifting, which separates material and leaves its bran, and to selecting the choicest part. The palm-tree term is connected with the palm's pre-eminence among trees with trunks; the root also denotes a palm-shaped ornament.

senses.definition: Date palm; date palms collectively.
senses.when: The noun is explicitly reported as usable for either a single palm or multiple palms, depending on context.

senses.definition: Date palms.
senses.when: Identified in the lexical evidence as the plural of نَخْل.

senses.definition: A date palm.
senses.when: The singular form corresponding to the date-palm noun; the lexical evidence identifies نَخْلَة as the one palm, with نَخِيل as its plural.

cautions: The supplied Lane material contains derived-form and related lexical entries rather than a direct nominal entry for the Quranic palm terms; the Quranic nominal senses are therefore supported by the supplied Quran-focused lexical evidence.

نذر.summary: The root centers on causing fear or apprehension, especially by communicating a danger, and on becoming wary of a danger.
نذر.development: From warning and taking heed developed the sense of informing someone with an admonitory or threatening implication. The noun نَذْر also denotes an obligation voluntarily imposed on oneself, as though one fears the consequence of failing to fulfill it.

senses.definition: To vow; make an act, offering, or future action binding or obligatory upon oneself.
senses.when: Used with the person making the vow as subject, often with عَلَى نَفْسِهِ or لِلّٰهِ. The Quranic use includes voluntarily dedicating a child to religious service by vow.

senses.definition: To become aware of something and take heed of it; become wary or remain on guard against it.
senses.when: The Quranic passive occurrence presents the result as being warned or made aware and cautious of a danger.

senses.definition: To warn someone of a danger or consequence; caution, put on guard, or put in fear by communicating it.
senses.when: The Quranic form is used for announcing punishment, danger, or an impending event in an admonitory context. Voice, tense, and object marking vary grammatically without changing the lexical sense.

senses.definition: One who has been warned, cautioned, or put in fear.
senses.when: This is the passive-participial state resulting from being warned or admonished; the Quran uses the plural form for those who have received such warning.

senses.definition: One who warns or cautions; a warner.
senses.when: The Quran uses the active participle for individual or collective bearers of warning, including prophetic warners.

senses.definition: A warner; one who gives notice of a danger, enemy, or other consequential matter.
senses.when: The term may denote a human or a nonhuman bearer of warning. Its plural نُذُر occurs in Quranic contexts referring either to warners or to warnings, according to construction and interpretation.

cautions: The reported interpretation of نَذِير as hoariness or whiteness of hair is retained as a less probable Quran-specific reading; the historical citation is not treated as a modern verse reference.
The Form I and Form IV passive imperfects can have the same visible Quranic surface pattern in transcription; the grouping and occurrence assignments follow the supplied QAC morphology.

نزل.summary: The root centers on descending, coming down, and arriving at a lower place or position.
نزل.development: From physical descent and alighting, the lexicon develops senses of settling, bringing something down, progressive delivery, stations or stages, hospitality for one who arrives, and figurative things that befall or descend upon people.

senses.definition: To descend or come down; to alight, settle, or remain in a place.
senses.when: Used for downward movement and for arrival at or sojourn in a place; the construction نَزَلَ بِهِ can describe coming down with or bearing something.

senses.definition: To send down or reveal, especially by successive or repeated delivery.
senses.when: In Quranic discourse this form is particularly associated with revelation or other things delivered progressively, in portions, or repeatedly; voice and tense variations do not create separate senses.

senses.definition: To send down, reveal, or bestow from above; to cause something to reach its recipients.
senses.when: The Quran applies this broad causative to revelation, rain, provisions, clothing, iron, armies, signs, punishment, and other benefits or afflictions; the object may be sent down literally or its causes and guidance may be provided.

senses.definition: To cause a person or thing to descend, alight, or settle at a place.
senses.when: This includes the request أَنْزِلْنِي مُنْزَلًا مُبَارَكًا, ‘cause me to alight at a blessed landing place,’ and is distinct from simply descending oneself.

senses.definition: To descend or come down, often in succession or gradually.
senses.when: In the Quranic examples it is used of angels, the spirit, and the divine command or other created agents; it presents the subject as descending or coming down itself.

senses.definition: A place or station of alighting, settlement, or passage; a stage or phase in a sequence.
senses.when: The Quranic plural مَنَازِل refers to the successive stations or phases assigned to the moon.

cautions: Form II is described in the Quran-focused evidence as especially associated with progressive or successive delivery, whereas Form IV is broader and includes general sending down or bestowal.
The مُنْزَل group contains both a passive-participial ‘sent down’ use and the place-noun use in 23:29, despite the supplied morphology grouping.

The Quranic active-participle group normalized to مُنْزِل is distinct from مُنْزَل: the former names an agent who sends down or hosts, while the latter primarily denotes something sent down or a landing place.

نشأ.summary: The root centers on rising, elevation, and emergence: something rises, comes forth, grows, or is brought into being.
نشأ.development: From physical rising and becoming elevated, the lexical range develops toward growth, emergence, creation, formation, and the production of new forms or states. Related extensions include composing speech and seeking something by raising it toward the senses.

senses.definition: To rear, bring up, or foster to growth.
senses.when: The Quran attests the passive form, describing someone brought up or reared in adornment.

senses.definition: To bring into being; create, originate, or produce.
senses.when: Quranic uses include bringing people, communities, bodily forms, and a later creation into existence. The construction is especially associated with divine creation and production.

senses.definition: To raise, form, or bring forth progressively.
senses.when: This developmental aspect is used of clouds as they form and rise and of living beings as they are brought into growth; it remains a form of bringing something into being rather than a merely physical elevation.

senses.definition: Bringing into being; creation or formative production.
senses.when: In the Quranic expression concerning the creation of the inhabitants of Paradise, the verbal noun denotes a distinctive act of bringing into being and forming.

senses.definition: Raised or elevated.
senses.when: The Quranic plural مُنْشَآت describes ships with their sails raised. The expression is also associated in transmitted interpretations with ships raising their sails, advancing and retiring, or commencing their courses.

senses.definition: Those who bring into being or produce.
senses.when: The Quranic active participle occurs in a contrast between human production and divine production.

cautions: The Quranic expression نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ has closely related interpretations: night prayer or standing, the first part or hours of night, and rising after sleep; these are retained as usage nuances rather than separate lexical forms.

The Quranic مُنْشَآت is presented under the singular passive-participle citation form مُنْشَأَة; transmitted interpretations of the associated ship expression include both elevated sails and variant motion-related readings.

نعم.summary: The root centers on flourishing, ease, pleasant living, and a good or sound condition, extending to bestowed benefit, prosperity, enjoyment, and valued livestock.
نعم.development: The lexical branches develop from thriving and pleasant life to favor or blessing conferred on another, abundant enjoyment or bliss, and livestock understood as a valuable form of prosperity. Several specialized and figurative uses arise through resemblance or association with softness, flourishing, or ease.

senses.definition: A formula of commendation: excellent, very good, or best is …
senses.when: Used in the fixed praise construction نِعْمَ, opposed to بِئْسَ in blame; it may be followed by a noun or predicate identifying what is praised.

senses.definition: To cause someone to enjoy ease, prosperity, and a pleasant state of life; to make comfortable or favored.
senses.when: The Quranic use presents a person as being placed in a condition of نعمة, ease, and plentiful living.

senses.definition: To bestow a favor, benefit, or grace upon someone; to confer благation or benefaction.
senses.when: Commonly construed with عَلَى and a recipient. In the explicitly described Quranic usage, the recipient is a rational or speaking being.

senses.definition: Abundant enjoyment, bliss, delight, or prosperous ease.
senses.when: Often denotes the abundant or enduring enjoyment associated with blessed life, including the Quranic gardens of bliss.

senses.definition: Prosperity, favor, or a favorable condition, especially as contrasted with adversity or affliction.
senses.when: Used as the counterpart of ضرّاء or بأساء, including the state of well-being that follows hardship.

senses.definition: A benefit, favor, blessing, bounty, or other good bestowed upon someone; a beneficial or well-being-producing condition.
senses.when: The form can denote one favor or the category of favor generally, whether small or abundant. Quranic uses commonly present the favor as bestowed by God.

cautions: The Quranic praise formula نِعْمَ, the affirmative particle نَعَمْ, and the livestock noun نَعَمٌ/أَنْعَامٌ are distinct lexical items despite their shared consonants.
نِعْمَةٌ ‘favor or blessing’ and نَعْمَةٌ ‘ease or pleasant living’ are kept distinct by vocalization and lexical evidence.
The active-participle Quranic form نَاعِمَةٌ is normalized under the citation form نَاعِمٌ; its Quranic occurrence is feminine singular.

نفس.summary: The root centers on breath or the issuing of air, and by extension on the animating self, vitality, relief, and what is highly valued.
نفس.development: The basic image is the خروج النسيم, the emergence of breath or air. From it develop meanings connected with breathing, the soul sustained by breath, relief as an easing of constraint, extension or spaciousness, and precious things pursued by emulation.

senses.definition: Of dawn or morning, to emerge, spread, and brighten as it becomes clear.
senses.when: Used in the Quranic construction وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ, describing the dawn's appearing and expansion rather than literal animal respiration.

senses.definition: To vie or aspire with one another for something desirable; to strive emulously to attain it.
senses.when: A reciprocal construction involving emulation and pursuit of excellence; the Quran-focused explanation emphasizes striving without harming the other party.

senses.definition: One who vies or aspires with others for a desirable good; an aspirer or competitor.
senses.when: Active participle of تَنَافَسَ, used of those who pursue a valued good through emulation.

senses.definition: Soul, spirit, or vital self: the animating principle or life-bearing self of a living being.
senses.when: Used of the soul or vital principle, including in contexts of its being taken, released, or associated with life; grammatical gender and number vary by construction.

senses.definition: The self, inner being, mind, or concealed contents of a person or being; hence oneself, himself, herself, themselves, and similar reflexive uses.
senses.when: In possessive and prepositional constructions it may denote one's own person, inner state, thought, knowledge, or concealed matter. In divine constructions it can denote the divine self or essence without implying two beings.

senses.definition: A person, individual, or living being considered as a whole.
senses.when: This use treats the individual as comprising the whole living person, soul and body; it is not restricted to one gender or social class.

cautions: The Form V Quranic occurrence describes dawn's emergence and expansion; literal breathing is a broader Classical use of the same verb, not the direct contextual gloss of that occurrence.
The divine construction يُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ has a reported interpretive variation between “Himself” and “His punishment.”
Lane’s historical Quran citation notation has not been converted into modern verse locations unless the corresponding QAC location was independently present and secure.

نفع.summary: The root denotes benefit and utility, in contrast to harm: what helps bring about good or fulfills a desired purpose.
نفع.development: The basic opposition to harm develops into beneficial effect, advantage, and useful means. Its derived patterns express causing benefit, benefiting from something, and seeking benefit.

senses.definition: To benefit, profit, avail, or be useful to someone or something.
senses.when: An active transitive use in which a person or thing is the beneficiary or object of benefit; Quranic contexts may affirm or deny that something will provide benefit.

senses.pos: Noun · plural form in the Quran
senses.definition: Benefits, advantages, utilities, or useful means by which good or a desired purpose is attained.
senses.when: The Quranic occurrences are the broken plural مَنَافِع of مَنْفَعَة and can denote concrete or abstract forms of usefulness.

senses.definition: Benefit or useful good; something that helps attain good, as opposed to harm.
senses.when: An abstract noun for beneficial effect, advantage, or usefulness; Quranic usage also occurs in contexts that deny the efficacy or availability of benefit.

cautions: The QAC group مَنَافِع is presented under the supported singular citation form مَنْفَعَة; its occurrence count remains the eight Quranic occurrences of the plural form.

نفق.summary: The root centers on going out, passing away, or reaching an exit, alongside concealment and hidden passage.
نفق.development: These orientations develop into meanings of expenditure as something that passes away, a subterranean passage with an outlet, and hypocrisy as concealed departure from what is outwardly professed.

senses.definition: To act hypocritically: to profess adherence to Islam while concealing another religion or contrary belief.
senses.when: In Quranic usage, the verb describes religious hypocrisy and concealed opposition behind an outward profession.

senses.definition: To expend or disburse wealth and other resources; to spend or give out, including gifts.
senses.when: The Quranic verb is used for spending from what one possesses, whether in obligation, charity, support, or other expenditure; grammatical forms include commands, imperfects, and perfects.
